at runtime instead of compile time. cookies_from_request   Parses @msg’s Cookie request header and returns a `glib::SList``SoupCookie`s. cookies_from_response   Parses @msg’s Set-Cookie response headers and returns a `glib::SList``SoupCookie`s. date_time_new_from_http_string      Parses @date_string and tries to extract a date from it. date_time_to_string    Converts @date to a string in the format described by @format. header_contains  Parses @header to see if it contains the token @token (matched
case-insensitively). header_contains_case_sensitive    `v3_8`Parses @header to see if it contains the token @token (matched
case-sensitively). header_g_string_append_param     Appends something like `name=value` to @string, taking care to quote @value
if needed, and if so, to escape any quotes or backslashes in @value. header_g_string_append_param_quoted      Appends something like `name="value"` to
@string, taking care to escape any quotes or backslashes in @value. header_parse_list   Parses a header whose content is described by RFC2616 as `#something`. headers_parse  Parses the headers of an HTTP request or response in @str and
stores the results in @dest. headers_parse_request   Parses the headers of an HTTP request in @str and stores the
results in @req_method, @req_path, @ver, and @req_headers. headers_parse_response   Parses the headers of an HTTP response in @str and stores the
results in @ver, @status_code, @reason_phrase, and @headers. headers_parse_status_line    Parses the HTTP Status-Line string in @status_line into @ver,
@status_code, and @reason_phrase. major_version  Returns the major version number of the libsoup library. micro_version  Returns the micro version number of the libsoup library. minor_version  Returns the minor version number of the libsoup library. tld_domain_is_public_suffix     Looks whether the @domain passed as argument is a public domain
suffix (.org, .com, .co.uk, etc) or not. tld_get_base_domain    Finds the base domain for a given @hostname uri_decode_data_uri    Decodes the given data URI and returns its contents and @content_type. uri_equal

# Auth in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Auth.html

`pub struct Auth { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The abstract base class for handling authentication.

Specific HTTP Authentication mechanisms are implemented by its subclasses, but applications never need to be aware of the specific subclasses being used.

[ Auth](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Auth.html) objects store the authentication data associated with a given bit
of web space. They are created automatically by

[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#authority)`authority`

The authority (host:port) being authenticated to.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#is-authenticated)`is-authenticated`

Whether or not the auth has been authenticated.

Readable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#is-cancelled)`is-cancelled`

Whether or not the auth has been cancelled.

Readable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#is-for-proxy)`is-for-proxy`

Whether or not the auth is for a proxy server.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#realm)`realm`

The authentication realm.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#scheme-name)`scheme-name`

The authentication scheme name.

Readable

## Implementations[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implementations)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/auth.rs.html#76)

Creates a new [ Auth](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Auth.html) of type @type_ with the information from
@msg and @auth_header.

This is called by [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html); you will normally not create auths
yourself.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#type_)`type_`

the type of auth to create (a subtype of [ Auth](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Auth.html))

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#msg)`msg`

the #SoupMessage the auth is being created for

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#auth_header)`auth_header`

the WWW-Authenticate/Proxy-Authenticate header

and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of

#### fn [watch_closure](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.ObjectExt.html#tymethod.watch_closure)(&self, closure: &impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Closure](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/closure/struct.Closure.html)>)

`closure` to the lifetime of the object. When
the object’s reference count drops to zero, the closure will be

#### fn [watch_closure](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.ObjectExt.html#tymethod.watch_closure)(&self, closure: &impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Closure](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/closure/struct.Closure.html)>)

`closure` to the lifetime of the object. When
the object’s reference count drops to zero, the closure will be
invalidated. An invalidated closure will ignore any calls to

# AuthDomain in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.AuthDomain.html

`pub struct AuthDomain { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Server-side authentication.

A [ AuthDomain](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html) manages authentication for all or part of a

[. To make a server require authentication, first create an appropriate subclass of](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server`[, and then add it to the server with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html)

`AuthDomain`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExt.html#method.add_auth_domain)

`ServerExt::add_auth_domain()`In order for an auth domain to have any effect, you must add one or more
paths to it (via [ AuthDomainExt::add_path()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.AuthDomainExt.html#method.add_path)). To require authentication for
all ordinary requests, add the path

`"/"`. (Note that this does not include
the special `"*"` URI (eg, “OPTIONS *”), which must be added as a separate
path if you want to cover it.)If you need greater control over which requests should and shouldn’t be
authenticated, add paths covering everything you *might* want authenticated,
and then use a filter ([ AuthDomainExt::set_filter()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.AuthDomainExt.html#method.set_filter) to bypass
authentication for those requests that don’t need it.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

# AuthDomainBasic in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.AuthDomainBasic.html

`pub struct AuthDomainBasic { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Server-side “Basic” authentication.

[ AuthDomainBasic](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainBasic.html) handles the server side of HTTP “Basic” (ie,
cleartext password) authentication.

#### pub fn [set_auth_callback](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_auth_callback)<P: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&[AuthDomainBasic](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainBasic.html), &[ServerMessage](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html), &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) + 'static>(
    &self,
    callback: P,
)

Sets the callback that @self will use to authenticate incoming requests.

For each request containing authorization, @self will invoke the callback, and then either accept or reject the request based on @callback’s return value.

You can also set the auth callback by setting the
[ auth-callback](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainBasic.html#auth-callback) and

[properties, which can also be used to set the callback at construct time.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainBasic.html#auth-data)

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

Server-side “Digest” authentication.

[ AuthDomainDigest](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainDigest.html) handles the server side of HTTP “Digest”

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/auth_domain_digest.rs.html#112-155)

#### pub fn [set_auth_callback](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_auth_callback)<P: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&[AuthDomainDigest](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainDigest.html), &[ServerMessage](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html), &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)> + 'static>(
    &self,
    callback: P,
)

Sets the callback that @self will use to authenticate incoming requests.

For each request containing authorization, @self will invoke the callback, and then either accept or reject the request based on @callback’s return value.

You can also set the auth callback by setting the
[ auth-callback](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainDigest.html#auth-callback) and

[properties, which can also be used to set the callback at construct time.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainDigest.html#auth-data)

`auth-data`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#callback)`callback`

the callback

Encodes the username/realm/password triplet for Digest authentication.

That is, it returns a stringified MD5 hash of
@username, @realm, and @password concatenated together. This is
the form that is needed as the return value of
[ AuthDomainDigest](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomainDigest.html)’s auth handler.

For security reasons, you should store the encoded hash, rather than storing the cleartext password itself and calling this method only when you need to verify it. This way, if your server is compromised, the attackers will not gain access to cleartext passwords which might also be usable at other sites. (Note also that the encoded password returned by this method is identical to the encoded password stored in an Apache .htdigest file.)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#username)`username`

a username

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#realm-1)`realm`

an auth realm name

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#password)`password`

the password for @username in @realm

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns)Returns

the encoded password

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/auth_domain_digest.rs.html#205-227)

#### pub fn [connect_auth_data_notify](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.connect_auth_data_notify)<F: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&Self) + 'static>(
    &self,
    f: F,
) -> [SignalHandlerId](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/signal/struct.SignalHandlerId.html)

# AuthManager in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.AuthManager.html

`pub struct AuthManager { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

HTTP client-side authentication handler.

[ AuthManager](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthManager.html) is the

[that handles HTTP authentication for a](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)

`SessionFeature`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`A [ AuthManager](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthManager.html) is added to the session by default, and normally
you don’t need to worry about it at all. However, if you want to
disable HTTP authentication, you can remove the feature from the
session with

[or disable it on individual requests with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.remove_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::remove_feature_by_type()`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.disable_feature)

`Message::disable_feature()`You can use this with [ SessionExt::remove_feature_by_type()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.remove_feature_by_type) or

[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.disable_feature)

`Message::disable_feature()`(Although this type has only been publicly visible since libsoup 2.42, it has
always existed in the background, and you can use `g_type_from_name  ("SoupAuthManager")` to get its `alias::GObject.Type` in earlier releases.)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/auth_manager.rs.html#39-72)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#impl-AuthManager)

### impl [AuthManager](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthManager.html)

Records that @auth is to be used under @uri, as though a WWW-Authenticate header had been received at that URI.

This can be used to “preload” @self’s auth cache, to avoid an extra HTTP round trip in the case where you know ahead of time that a 401 response will be returned.

This is only useful for authentication types where the initial Authorization header does not depend on any additional information from the server. (Eg, Basic or NTLM, but not Digest.)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#uri)`uri`

the #GUri under which @auth is to be used

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#auth)`auth`

the #SoupAuth to use

# AuthNegotiate in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.AuthNegotiate.html

`pub struct AuthNegotiate { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

HTTP-based GSS-Negotiate authentication, as defined by
[RFC 4559](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4559).

[ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)s do not support this type by default; if you want to
enable support for it, call

[, passing](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()``SOUP_TYPE_AUTH_NEGOTIATE`.This auth type will only work if libsoup was compiled with GSSAPI
support; you can check `supported()` to see if it
was.

[ AuthExt](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.AuthExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`]GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will

#### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of a source flags value with the complement of a target flags value (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# ContentDecoder in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.ContentDecoder.html

`pub struct ContentDecoder { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Handles decoding of HTTP messages.

[ ContentDecoder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentDecoder.html) handles adding the “Accept-Encoding” header on
outgoing messages, and processing the “Content-Encoding” header on
incoming ones. Currently it supports the “gzip”, “deflate”, and “br”
content codings.

A [ ContentDecoder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentDecoder.html) will automatically be
added to the session by default. (You can use

[if you don’t want this.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.remove_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::remove_feature_by_type()`If [ ContentDecoder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentDecoder.html) successfully decodes the Content-Encoding,
the message body will contain the decoded data; however, the message headers
will be unchanged (and so “Content-Encoding” will still be present,
“Content-Length” will describe the original encoded length, etc).

If “Content-Encoding” contains any encoding types that
[ ContentDecoder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentDecoder.html) doesn’t recognize, then none of the encodings
will be decoded.

(Note that currently there is no way to (automatically) use Content-Encoding when sending a request body, or to pick specific encoding types to support.)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], `SessionFeatureExt`

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# ContentSniffer in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.ContentSniffer.html

`pub struct ContentSniffer { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Sniffs the mime type of messages.

A [ ContentSniffer](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentSniffer.html) tries to detect the actual content type of
the files that are being downloaded by looking at some of the data
before the

[emits its](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[signal.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-headers)

`got-headers`[implements](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentSniffer.html)

`ContentSniffer`[, so you can add content sniffing to a session with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)

`SessionFeature`[or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature)

`SessionExt::add_feature()`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], `SessionFeatureExt`

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# Cookie in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Cookie.html

`pub struct Cookie { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Implements HTTP cookies, as described by
[RFC 6265](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265.txt).

To have a [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) handle cookies for your appliction
automatically, use a

[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html)

`CookieJar`@name and @value will be set for all cookies. If the cookie is generated from a string that appears to have no name, then @name will be the empty string.

@domain and @path give the host or domain, and path within that host/domain, to restrict this cookie to. If @domain starts with “.”, that indicates a domain (which matches the string after the “.”, or any hostname that has @domain as a suffix). Otherwise, it is a hostname and must match exactly.

@expires will be non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the cookie uses either the original
“expires” attribute, or the newer “max-age” attribute. If @expires
is

[, it indicates that neither “expires” nor “max-age” was specified, and the cookie expires at the end of the session.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`If @http_only is set, the cookie should not be exposed to untrusted code (eg, javascript), so as to minimize the danger posed by cross-site scripting attacks.

GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implementations)

Creates a new [ Cookie](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html) with the given attributes.

Use [ set_secure()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html#method.set_secure) and

[if you need to set those attributes on the returned cookie.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html#method.set_http_only)

`set_http_only()`If @domain starts with “.”, that indicates a domain (which matches the string after the “.”, or any hostname that has @domain as a suffix). Otherwise, it is a hostname and must match exactly.

@max_age is used to set the “expires” attribute on the cookie; pass
-1 to not include the attribute (indicating that the cookie expires
with the current session), 0 for an already-expired cookie, or a
lifetime in seconds. You can use the constants
`SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_HOUR`, `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_DAY`,
`SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_WEEK` and `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_YEAR` (or
multiples thereof) to calculate this value. (If you really care
about setting the exact time that the cookie will expire, use
[ set_expires()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html#method.set_expires).)

As of version 3.4.0 the default value of a cookie’s same-site-policy
is [ SameSitePolicy::Lax](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.SameSitePolicy.html#variant.Lax).

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/cookie.rs.html#290-294)

#### pub fn [set_max_age](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_max_age)(&mut self, max_age: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html))

Sets @self’s max age to @max_age.

If @max_age is -1, the cookie is a session cookie, and will expire at the end
of the client’s session. Otherwise, it is the number of seconds until the
cookie expires. You can use the constants `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_HOUR`,
`SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_DAY`, `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_WEEK` and
`SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_YEAR` (or multiples thereof) to calculate this value.
(A value of 0 indicates that the cookie should be considered
already-expired.)

This sets the same property as [ set_expires()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html#method.set_expires).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#max_age-1)`max_age`

the new max age

Parses @header and returns a [ Cookie](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html).

If @header contains multiple cookies, only the first one will be parsed.

If @header does not have “path” or “domain” attributes, they will
be defaulted from @origin. If @origin is [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), path will default
to “/”, but domain will be left as

[. Note that this is not a valid state for a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[, and you will need to fill in some appropriate string for the domain if you want to actually make use of the cookie.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html)

`Cookie`As of version 3.4.0 the default value of a cookie’s same-site-policy
is [ SameSitePolicy::Lax](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.SameSitePolicy.html#variant.Lax).

a cookie string (eg, the value of a Set-Cookie header)

# CookieJar in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.CookieJar.html

`pub struct CookieJar { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Automatic cookie handling for SoupSession.

A [ CookieJar](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html) stores

[s and arrange for them to be sent with the appropriate](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Cookie.html)

`Cookie`[s.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[implements](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html)

`CookieJar`[, so you can add a cookie jar to a session with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)

`SessionFeature`[or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature)

`SessionExt::add_feature()`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()`Note that the base [ CookieJar](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html) class does not support any form
of long-term cookie persistence.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#accept-policy)`accept-policy`

The policy the jar should follow to accept or reject cookies.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#read-only)`read-only`

Whether or not the cookie jar is read-only.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#changed)`changed`

Emitted when @jar changes.

If a cookie has been added,
@new_cookie will contain the newly-added cookie and
@old_cookie will be [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None). If a cookie has been deleted,
@old_cookie will contain the to-be-deleted cookie and
@new_cookie will be

[. If a cookie has been changed, @old_cookie will contain its old value, and @new_cookie its new value.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[ CookieJarExt](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.CookieJarExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], [,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionFeatureExt.html)

`SessionFeatureExt`

`CookieJarExtManual`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# CookieJarDB in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.CookieJarDB.html

`pub struct CookieJarDB { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Database-based Cookie Jar.

[ CookieJarDB](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJarDB.html) is a

[that reads cookies from and writes them to a sqlite database in the new Mozilla format.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html)

`CookieJar`(This is identical to `SoupCookieJarSqlite` in
libsoup-gnome; it has just been moved into libsoup proper, and
renamed to avoid conflicting.)

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

The policy the jar should follow to accept or reject cookies.

Readable | Writeable

#### pub fn [new](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.new)(filename: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), read_only: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [CookieJarDB](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJarDB.html)

Creates a [ CookieJarDB](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJarDB.html).

@filename will be read in at startup to create an initial set of cookies. If
@read_only is [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), then the non-session cookies will be written to
@filename when the

[signal is emitted from the jar. (If @read_only is](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html#changed)

`changed`[, then the cookie jar will only be used for this session, and changes made to it will be lost when the jar is destroyed.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#filename-1)`filename`

the filename to read to/write from, or `None`

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#read_only)`read_only`

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if @filename is read-only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns)Returns

the new #SoupCookieJar

`changed`[, then the cookie jar will only be used for this session, and changes made to it will be lost when the jar is destroyed.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

#### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of a source flags value with the complement of a target flags value (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# HSTSEnforcer in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html

`pub struct HSTSEnforcer { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Automatic HTTP Strict Transport Security enforcing for [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html).

A [ HSTSEnforcer](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html) stores HSTS policies and enforces them when
required.

[implements](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html)

`HSTSEnforcer`[, so you can add an HSTS enforcer to a session with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)

`SessionFeature`[or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature)

`SessionExt::add_feature()`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()`[ HSTSEnforcer](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html) keeps track of all the HTTPS destinations that,
when connected to, return the Strict-Transport-Security header with
valid values.

[will forget those destinations upon expiry or when the server requests it.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html)

`HSTSEnforcer`When the [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) the

[is attached to queues or restarts a message, the](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html)

`HSTSEnforcer`[will rewrite the URI to HTTPS if the destination is a known HSTS host and is contacted over an insecure transport protocol (HTTP). Users of](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html)

`HSTSEnforcer`[are advised to listen to changes in the](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html)

`HSTSEnforcer`[property in order to be aware of changes in the message URI.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#uri)

`uri`Note that [ HSTSEnforcer](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html) does not support any form of long-term
HSTS policy persistence. See

[for a persistent enforcer.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcerDB.html)

`HSTSEnforcerDB`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#changed)`changed`

Emitted when @hsts_enforcer changes.

If a policy has been added,
@new_policy will contain the newly-added policy and
@old_policy will be [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None). If a policy has been deleted,
@old_policy will contain the to-be-deleted policy and
@new_policy will be

[. If a policy has been changed, @old_policy will contain its old value, and @new_policy its new value.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`Note that you shouldn’t modify the policies from a callback to this signal.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[ HSTSEnforcerExt](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.HSTSEnforcerExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`],

`SessionFeatureExt`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# Session in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Session.html

`pub struct Session { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Soup session state object.

[ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) is the object that controls client-side HTTP. A

[encapsulates all of the state that libsoup is keeping on behalf of your program; cached HTTP connections, authentication information, etc. It also keeps track of various global options and features that you are using.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`Most applications will only need a single [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html); the primary
reason you might need multiple sessions is if you need to have
multiple independent authentication contexts. (Eg, you are
connecting to a server and authenticating as two different users at
different times; the easiest way to ensure that each

[is sent with the authentication information you intended is to use one session for the first user, and a second session for the other user.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`Additional [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) functionality is provided by

[objects, which can be added to a session with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)

`SessionFeature`[or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature)

`SessionExt::add_feature()`[For example,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()`[provides support for logging HTTP traffic,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html)

`Logger`[provides support for compressed response handling, and](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentDecoder.html)

`ContentDecoder`[provides support for HTML5-style response body content sniffing. Additionally, subtypes of](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentSniffer.html)

`ContentSniffer`[can be added as features, to add support for additional authentication types.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Auth.html)

`Auth`All `SoupSession`s are created with a [ AuthManager](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthManager.html), and support
for

`SOUP_TYPE_AUTH_BASIC` and `SOUP_TYPE_AUTH_DIGEST`. Additionally,
sessions using the plain [class (rather than one of its deprecated subtypes) have a](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`[by default.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ContentDecoder.html)

`ContentDecoder`Note that all async methods will invoke their callbacks on the thread-default context at the time of the function call.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#accept-language)`accept-language`

If non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), the value to use for the “Accept-Language” header
on

[s sent from this session.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`Setting this will disable [ accept-language-auto](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#accept-language-auto).

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#accept-language-auto)`accept-language-auto`

If [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),

[will automatically set the string for the “Accept-Language” header on every](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`[sent, based on the return value of](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message``get_language_names()`.Setting this will override any previous value of
[ accept-language](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#accept-language).

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#idle-timeout)`idle-timeout`

Connection lifetime (in seconds) when idle. Any connection left idle longer than this will be closed.

Although you can change this property at any time, it will
only affect newly-created connections, not currently-open
ones. You can call [ SessionExt::abort()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.abort) after setting this
if you want to ensure that all future connections will have
this timeout value.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#local-address)`local-address`

Sets the [ gio::InetSocketAddress](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/inet_socket_address/struct.InetSocketAddress.html) to use for the client side of
the connection.

Use this property if you want for instance to bind the local socket to a specific IP address.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#max-conns)`max-conns`

The maximum number of connections that the session can open at once.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#max-conns-per-host)`max-conns-per-host`

The maximum number of connections that the session can open at once to a given host.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#proxy-resolver)`proxy-resolver`

A [ gio::ProxyResolver](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/proxy_resolver/struct.ProxyResolver.html) to use with this session.

If no proxy resolver is set, then the default proxy resolver
will be used. See [ gio::ProxyResolver::default()](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/proxy_resolver/struct.ProxyResolver.html#method.default).
You can set it to

[if you don’t want to use proxies, or set it to your own](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[if you want to control what proxies get used.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/proxy_resolver/struct.ProxyResolver.html)

`gio::ProxyResolver`Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#remote-connectable)`remote-connectable`

Sets a socket to make outgoing connections on. This will override the default behaviour of opening TCP/IP sockets to the hosts specified in the URIs.

This function is not required for common HTTP usage, but only when connecting
to a HTTP service that is not using standard TCP/IP sockets. An example of
this is a local service that uses HTTP over UNIX-domain sockets, in that case
a `Gio::UnixSocketAddress` can be passed to this function.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#timeout)`timeout`

The timeout (in seconds) for socket I/O operations (including connecting to a server, and waiting for a reply to an HTTP request).

Although you can change this property at any time, it will
only affect newly-created connections, not currently-open
ones. You can call [ SessionExt::abort()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.abort) after setting this
if you want to ensure that all future connections will have
this timeout value.

Not to be confused with [ idle-timeout](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#idle-timeout) (which is
the length of time that idle persistent connections will be
kept open).

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#tls-database)`tls-database`

Sets the [ gio::TlsDatabase](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/tls_database/struct.TlsDatabase.html) to use for validating SSL/TLS
certificates.

If no certificate database is set, then the default database will be
used. See `Gio::TlsBackend::get_default_database()`.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#tls-interaction)`tls-interaction`

A [ gio::TlsInteraction](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/tls_interaction/struct.TlsInteraction.html) object that will be passed on to any

`Gio::TlsConnection`s created by the session.This can be used to provide client-side certificates, for example.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#user-agent)`user-agent`

User-Agent string.

If non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), the value to use for the “User-Agent” header
on

[s sent from this session.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`RFC 2616 says: “The User-Agent request-header field contains information about the user agent originating the request. This is for statistical purposes, the tracing of protocol violations, and automated recognition of user agents for the sake of tailoring responses to avoid particular user agent limitations. User agents SHOULD include this field with requests.”

The User-Agent header contains a list of one or more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most significant product token coming first. The tokens must be brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although “-”, “_”, and “.” are also allowed), and may optionally include a “/” followed by a version string. You may also put comments, enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.

If you set a [ user-agent](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#user-agent) property that has trailing
whitespace,

[will append its own product token (eg,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session``libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the
header for you.Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-queued)`request-queued`

Emitted when a request is queued on @session.

When sending a request, first [ request-queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-queued)
is emitted, indicating that the session has become aware of
the request.

After a connection is available to send the request various
[ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) signals are emitted as the message is
processed. If the message is requeued, it will emit

[, which will then be followed by other](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#restarted)

`restarted`[signals when the message is re-sent.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`Eventually, the message will emit [ finished](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#finished).
Normally, this signals the completion of message
processing. However, it is possible that the application
will requeue the message from the “finished” handler.
In that case the process will loop back.

Eventually, a message will reach “finished” and not be
requeued. At that point, the session will emit
[ request-unqueued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-unqueued) to indicate that it is done
with the message.

To sum up: [ request-queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-queued) and

[are guaranteed to be emitted exactly once, but](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-unqueued)

`request-unqueued`[(and all of the other](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#finished)

`finished`[signals) may be invoked multiple times for a given message.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-unqueued)`request-unqueued`

Emitted when a request is removed from @session’s queue, indicating that @session is done with it.

See [ request-queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-queued) for a detailed description of
the message lifecycle within a session.

Persistent HTTP Strict Transport Security enforcer.

[ HSTSEnforcerDB](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcerDB.html) is a

[that uses a SQLite database as a backend for persistency.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html)

Creates a [ HSTSEnforcerDB](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcerDB.html).

@filename will be read in during the initialization of a
[ HSTSEnforcerDB](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcerDB.html), in order to create an initial set of HSTS
policies. If the file doesn’t exist, a new database will be created
and initialized. Changes to the policies during the lifetime of a

[will be written to @filename when](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcerDB.html)

`HSTSEnforcerDB`[is emitted.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html#changed)

`changed`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#filename-1)`filename`

the filename of the database to read/write from.

# HSTSPolicy in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.HSTSPolicy.html

`pub struct HSTSPolicy { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ HSTSPolicy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSPolicy.html) implements HTTP policies, as described by

[RFC 6797](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6797).

@domain represents the host that this policy applies to. The domain
must be IDNA-canonicalized. `HSTSPolicy::new()` and related methods
will do this for you.

@max_age contains the ‘max-age’ value from the Strict Transport Security header and indicates the time to live of this policy, in seconds.

@expires will be non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the policy has been set by the host and
hence has an expiry time. If @expires is

[, it indicates that the policy is a permanent session policy set by the user agent.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`If @include_subdomains is [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), the Strict Transport Security policy
must also be enforced on subdomains of @domain.

GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

#### pub fn [new](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.new)(
    domain: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    max_age: c_ulong,
    include_subdomains: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),

Creates a new [ HSTSPolicy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSPolicy.html) with the given attributes.

@domain is a domain on which the strict transport security policy represented by this object must be enforced.

@max_age is used to set the “expires” attribute on the policy; pass
`SOUP_HSTS_POLICY_MAX_AGE_PAST` for an already-expired policy, or a
lifetime in seconds.

If @include_subdomains is [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), the strict transport security policy
must also be enforced on all subdomains of @domain.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#domain)`domain`

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/hsts_policy.rs.html#147-155)#### pub fn [new_session_policy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.new_session_policy)(domain: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), include_subdomains: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [HSTSPolicy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSPolicy.html)

#### pub fn [new_session_policy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.new_session_policy)(domain: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), include_subdomains: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [HSTSPolicy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSPolicy.html)

Creates a new session [ HSTSPolicy](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSPolicy.html) with the given attributes.

A session policy is a policy that is valid during the lifetime of
the [ HSTSEnforcer](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html) it is added to. Contrary to regular policies,
it has no expiration date and is not stored in persistent
enforcers. These policies are useful for user-agent to load their
own or user-defined rules.

@domain is a domain on which the strict transport security policy represented by this object must be enforced.

If @include_subdomains is [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), the strict transport security policy
must also be enforced on all subdomains of @domain.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#domain-2)`domain`

policy domain or hostname

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#include_subdomains-2)`include_subdomains`

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if the policy applies on sub domains

a new #SoupHSTSPolicy.

# Logger in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Logger.html

`pub struct Logger { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Debug logging support

[ Logger](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html) watches a

[and logs the HTTP traffic that it generates, for debugging purposes. Many applications use an environment variable to determine whether or not to use](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`[, and to determine the amount of debugging output.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html)

`Logger`To use [ Logger](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html), first create a logger with

[, optionally configure it with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html#method.new)

`new()`[,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html#method.set_request_filter)

`set_request_filter()`[, and [](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html#method.set_response_filter)

`set_response_filter()``set_printer()`][Self::set_printer()], and
then attach it to a session (or multiple sessions) with
[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature)

`SessionExt::add_feature()`By default, the debugging output is sent to `stdout`, and looks something
like:

```
> POST /unauth HTTP/1.1
> Soup-Debug-Timestamp: 1200171744
> Soup-Debug: SoupSession 1 (0x612190), SoupMessage 1 (0x617000), GSocket 1 (0x612220)
> Host: localhost
> Content-Type: text/plain
> Connection: close
< HTTP/1.1 201 Created
< Soup-Debug-Timestamp: 1200171744
< Soup-Debug: SoupMessage 1 (0x617000)
< Date: Sun, 12 Jan 2008 21:02:24 GMT
< Content-Length: 0
```
The `Soup-Debug-Timestamp` line gives the time (as a `time_t`) when the
request was sent, or the response fully received.

The `Soup-Debug` line gives further debugging information about the
[ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html),

[, and](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[involved; the hex numbers are the addresses of the objects in question (which may be useful if you are running in a debugger). The decimal IDs are simply counters that uniquely identify objects across the lifetime of the](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/socket/struct.Socket.html)

`gio::Socket`[. In particular, this can be used to identify when multiple messages are sent across the same connection.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html)

`Logger`Currently, the request half of the message is logged just before
the first byte of the request gets written to the network (from the
[ starting](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#starting) signal).

The response is logged just after the last byte of the response body is read
from the network (from the [ got-body](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-body) or

[signal), which means that the](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-informational)

`got-informational`[signal, and anything triggered off it (such as](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-headers)

`got-headers`[) will be emitted](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#authenticate)

`authenticate`*before*the response headers are actually logged.

If the response doesn’t happen to trigger the [ got-body](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-body) nor

[signals due to, for example, a cancellation before receiving the last byte of the response body, the response will still be logged on the event of the](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-informational)

`got-informational`[signal.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#finished)

`finished`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#level)`level`

The level of logging output.

Readable | Writeable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#max-body-size)`max-body-size`

If [ level](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html#level) is

[, this gives the maximum number of bytes of the body that will be logged. (-1 means “no limit”.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.LoggerLogLevel.html#variant.Body)

`LoggerLogLevel::Body`Readable | Writeable | Construct

Sets up a filter to determine the log level for a given request.

For each HTTP request @self will invoke @request_filter to
determine how much (if any) of that request to log. (If you do not
set a request filter, @self will just always log requests at the
level passed to [ new()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html#method.new).)

# Message in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Message.html

`pub struct Message { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Represents an HTTP message being sent or received.

A [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) represents an HTTP message that is being sent or
received.

You would create a [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) with

[or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.new)

`new()`[, set up its fields appropriately, and send it.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.from_uri)

`from_uri()`[ status-code](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#status-code) will normally be a

[value, eg,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.Status.html)

`Status`[, though of course it might actually be an unknown status code.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.Status.html#variant.Ok)

`Status::Ok`[is the actual text returned from the server, which may or may not correspond to the “standard” description of @status_code. At any rate, it is almost certainly not localized, and not very descriptive even if it is in the user’s language; you should not use](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#reason-phrase)

`reason-phrase`[in user-visible messages. Rather, you should look at](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#reason-phrase)

`reason-phrase`[, and determine an end-user-appropriate message based on that and on what you were trying to do.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#status-code)

`status-code`Note that libsoup’s terminology here does not quite match the HTTP
specification: in RFC 2616, an “HTTP-message” is *either* a Request, *or* a
Response. In libsoup, a [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) combines both the request and the
response.

[, which will continue until you return without calling](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-body)`got-body`

Emitted after receiving the complete message response body.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-body-data)`got-body-data`

Emitted after reading a portion of the message body from the network.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-headers)`got-headers`

Emitted after receiving the Status-Line and response headers.

See also `Message::add_header_handler()` and
`Message::add_status_code_handler()`, which can be used to
connect to a subset of emissions of this signal.

If you cancel or requeue @msg while processing this signal,
then the current HTTP I/O will be stopped after this signal
emission finished, and @msg’s connection will be closed.
(If you need to requeue a message–eg, after handling
authentication or redirection–it is usually better to
requeue it from a [ got-body](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got-body) handler rather
than a

[handler, so that the existing HTTP connection can be reused.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#got_headers)

`got_headers`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-informational)`got-informational`

Emitted after receiving a 1xx (Informational) response for a (client-side) message.

The response_headers will be filled in with the headers associated with the informational response; however, those header values will be erased after this signal is done.

If you cancel or requeue @msg while processing this signal, then the current HTTP I/O will be stopped after this signal emission finished, and @msg’s connection will be closed.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#hsts-enforced)`hsts-enforced`

Emitted when [ HSTSEnforcer](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.HSTSEnforcer.html) has upgraded the protocol
for @msg to HTTPS as a result of matching its domain with
a HSTS policy.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#network-event)`network-event`

Emitted to indicate that some network-related event related to @msg has occurred.

This essentially proxies the [`event`][struct@crate::Gio::SocketClient#event] signal,
but only for events that occur while @msg “owns” the connection; if
@msg is sent on an existing persistent connection, then this signal
will not be emitted. (If you want to force the message to be sent on
a new connection, set the [ MessageFlags::NEW_CONNECTION](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageFlags.html#associatedconstant.NEW_CONNECTION) flag on it.)

See [`event`][struct@crate::Gio::SocketClient#event] for more information on what
the different values of @event correspond to, and what
@connection will be in each case.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-certificate)`request-certificate`

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message.rs.html#409-423)

Creates a new [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) and sets it up to send the given @encoded_form
to @uri via @method. If @method is “GET”, it will include the form data
into @uri’s query field, and if @method is “POST” or “PUT”, it will be set as
request body.

This function takes the ownership of @encoded_form, that will be released
with `free()` when no longer in use. See also `form_encode()`,
`form_encode_hash()` and `form_encode_datalist()`.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method-2)`method`

the HTTP method for the created request (GET, POST or PUT)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#uri_string-1)`uri_string`

the destination endpoint (as a string)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#encoded_form)`encoded_form`

a encoded form

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-1)Returns

the new #SoupMessage, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if
@uri_string could not be parsed or @method is not “GET, “POST” or “PUT”

#### pub fn [disable_feature](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.disable_feature)(&self, feature_type: [Type](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/types/struct.Type.html))

Disables the actions of [ SessionFeature](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)s with the
given @feature_type (or a subclass of that type) on @self.

@self is processed as though the feature(s) hadn’t been added to the session. Eg, passing #SOUP_TYPE_CONTENT_SNIFFER for @feature_type will disable Content-Type sniffing on the message.

You must call this before queueing @self on a session; calling it on a message that has already been queued is undefined. In particular, you cannot call this on a message that is being requeued after a redirect or authentication.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#feature_type)`feature_type`

the #GType of a `SessionFeature`

#### pub fn [set_priority](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_priority)(&self, priority: [MessagePriority](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.MessagePriority.html))

Sets the priority of a message.

Note that this won’t have any effect unless used before the message is added to the session’s message processing queue.

The message will be placed just before any other previously added message with lower priority (messages with the same priority are processed on a FIFO basis).

Setting priorities does not currently work with synchronous messages because in the synchronous/blocking case, priority ends up being determined semi-randomly by thread scheduling.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#priority-1)`priority`

the #SoupMessagePriority

Emitted to indicate that some network-related event related to @msg has occurred.

This essentially proxies the [`event`][struct@crate::Gio::SocketClient#event] signal,
but only for events that occur while @msg “owns” the connection; if
@msg is sent on an existing persistent connection, then this signal
will not be emitted. (If you want to force the message to be sent on
a new connection, set the [ MessageFlags::NEW_CONNECTION](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageFlags.html#associatedconstant.NEW_CONNECTION) flag on it.)

See [`event`][struct@crate::Gio::SocketClient#event] for more information on what
the different values of @event correspond to, and what
@connection will be in each case.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#event)`event`

the network event

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#connection)`connection`

the current state of the network connection

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `downcast` and `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast_ref)

# MessageBody in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.MessageBody.html

`pub struct MessageBody { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ MessageBody](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html) represents the request or response body of a

[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`Note that while @length always reflects the full length of the
message body, @data is normally [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), and will only be filled in
after

[is called. For client-side messages, this automatically happens for the response body after it has been fully read. Likewise, for server-side messages, the request body is automatically filled in after being read.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.flatten)

`flatten()`As an added bonus, when @data is filled in, it is always terminated
with a `\0` byte (which is not reflected in @length).

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

#### pub fn [append_take](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.append_take)(&self, data: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)])

Appends @length bytes from @data to @self.

This function is exactly equivalent to `MessageBody::append()`
with [ MemoryUse::Take](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.MemoryUse.html#variant.Take) as second argument; it exists mainly for
convenience and simplifying language bindings.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#data)`data`

data to append

Tags @self as being complete.

Call this when using chunked encoding after you have appended the last chunk.

Fills in @self’s data field with a buffer containing all of the data in @self.

Adds an additional `\0` byte not counted by @self’s
length field.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-1)Returns

a #GBytes containing the same data as @self.
(You must `GLib::Bytes::unref()` this if you do not want it.)

Gets a [ glib::Bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/bytes/struct.Bytes.html) containing data from @self starting at @offset.

The size of the returned chunk is unspecified. You can iterate
through the entire body by first calling
[ chunk()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.chunk) with an offset of 0, and then on each
successive call, increment the offset by the length of the
previously-returned chunk.

If @offset is greater than or equal to the total length of @self,
then the return value depends on whether or not
[ complete()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.complete) has been called or not; if it has,
then

[will return a 0-length chunk (indicating the end of @self). If it has not, then](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.chunk)

`chunk()`[will return](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.chunk)

`chunk()`[(indicating that @self may still potentially have more data, but that data is not currently available).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#offset)`offset`

an offset

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-3)Returns

a #GBytes

Handles the [ MessageBody](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html) part of receiving a chunk of data from
the network.

Normally this means appending @chunk to @self, exactly as with
[ append_bytes()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.append_bytes), but if you have set @self’s accumulate
flag to

[, then that will not happen.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`This is a low-level method which you should not normally need to use.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#chunk)`chunk`

a #GBytes received from the network

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_body.rs.html#178-182)#### pub fn [set_accumulate](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_accumulate)(&self, accumulate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_body.rs.html#178-182)

#### pub fn [set_accumulate](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_accumulate)(&self, accumulate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Sets or clears the accumulate flag on @self.

(The default value is [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).) If set to

[, @self’s data field will not be filled in after the body is fully sent/received, and the chunks that make up @self may be discarded when they are no longer needed.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`If you set the flag to [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) on the

[request_body of a client-side message, it will block the accumulation of chunks into @self’s data field, but it will not normally cause the chunks to be discarded after being written like in the server-side](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[response_body case, because the request body needs to be kept around in case the request needs to be sent a second time due to redirection or authentication.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#accumulate)`accumulate`

whether or not to accumulate body chunks in @self

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_body.rs.html#204-208)#### pub fn [wrote_chunk](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.wrote_chunk)(&self, chunk: &[Bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/bytes/struct.Bytes.html))

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_body.rs.html#204-208)

#### pub fn [wrote_chunk](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.wrote_chunk)(&self, chunk: &[Bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/bytes/struct.Bytes.html))

Handles the [ MessageBody](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html) part of writing a chunk of data to the
network.

Normally this is a no-op, but if you have set @self’s accumulate flag to
[ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), then this will cause @chunk to be discarded to free up memory.

This is a low-level method which you should not need to use, and there are further restrictions on its proper use which are not documented here.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#chunk-1)`chunk`

a #GBytes returned from `chunk()`

# MessageHeaders in soup - Rust

`pub struct MessageHeaders { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The HTTP message headers associated with a request or response.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implementations)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_headers.rs.html#34-37)#### pub fn [new](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.new)(type_: [MessageHeadersType](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.MessageHeadersType.html)) -> [MessageHeaders](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html)

Creates a [ MessageHeaders](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html).

([ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) does this automatically for its own headers. You would only
need to use this method if you are manually parsing or generating message
headers.)

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#type_)`type_`

the type of headers

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns)Returns

a new #SoupMessageHeaders

Appends a new header with name @name and value @value to @self.

(If there is an existing header with name @name, then this creates a second
one, which is only allowed for list-valued headers; see also
[ replace()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.replace).)

The caller is expected to make sure that @name and @value are syntactically correct.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#name)`name`

the header name to add

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#value)`value`

the new value of @name

#### pub fn [clean_connection_headers](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.clean_connection_headers)(&self)

Removes all the headers listed in the Connection header.

Calls @func once for each header value in @self.

Beware that unlike [ list()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.list), this processes the
headers in exactly the way they were added, rather than
concatenating multiple same-named headers into a single value.
(This is intentional; it ensures that if you call

[multiple times with the same name, then the I/O code will output multiple copies of the header when sending the message to the remote implementation, which may be required for interoperability in some cases.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.append)

`append()`You may not modify the headers from @func.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#func)`func`

callback function to run for each header

Parses @self’s Content-Range header and returns it in @start, @end, and @total_length. If the total length field in the header was specified as “*”, then @total_length will be set to -1.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-2)Returns

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if @self contained a “Content-Range” header
containing a byte range which could be parsed,

`false`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#start)`start`

resource, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if you don’t care.

Gets the message body encoding that @self declare.

This may not always correspond to the encoding used on the wire; eg, a HEAD response may declare a Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding, but it will never actually include a body.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-3)Returns

the encoding declared by @self.

Gets the value of header @name in @self.

Use this for headers whose values are comma-delimited lists, and which are
therefore allowed to appear multiple times in the headers. For
non-list-valued headers, use [ one()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.one).

If @name appears multiple times in @self,
[ list()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.list) will concatenate all of the values
together, separated by commas. This is sometimes awkward to parse
(eg, WWW-Authenticate, Set-Cookie), but you have to be able to deal
with it anyway, because the HTTP spec explicitly states that this
transformation is allowed, and so an upstream proxy could do the
same thing.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#name-1)`name`

header name

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-6)Returns

the header’s value or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if not found.

Gets the value of header @name in @self.

Use this for headers whose values are *not* comma-delimited lists, and which
therefore can only appear at most once in the headers. For list-valued
headers, use [ list()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.list).

If @self does erroneously contain multiple copies of the header, it is not defined which one will be returned. (Ideally, it will return whichever one makes libsoup most compatible with other HTTP implementations.)

#### pub fn [set_content_length](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_content_length)(&self, content_length: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html))

Sets the message body length that @self will declare, and sets
@self’s encoding to [ Encoding::ContentLength](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.Encoding.html#variant.ContentLength).

You do not normally need to call this; if @self is set to use
Content-Length encoding, libsoup will automatically set its
Content-Length header for you immediately before sending the
headers. One situation in which this method is useful is when
generating the response to a HEAD request; Calling
[ set_content_length()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.set_content_length) allows you to put the
correct content length into the response without needing to waste
memory by filling in a response body which won’t actually be sent.
