[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_headers.rs.html#447-454)#### pub fn [set_expectations](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_expectations)(&self, expectations: [Expectation](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Expectation.html))

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_headers.rs.html#447-454)

#### pub fn [set_expectations](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_expectations)(&self, expectations: [Expectation](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Expectation.html))

Sets @self’s “Expect” header according to @expectations.

Currently [ Expectation::CONTINUE](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Expectation.html#associatedconstant.CONTINUE) is the only known expectation
value. You should set this value on a request if you are sending a
large message body (eg, via POST or PUT), and want to give the
server a chance to reject the request after seeing just the headers
(eg, because it will require authentication before allowing you to
post, or because you’re POSTing to a URL that doesn’t exist). This
saves you from having to transmit the large request body when the
server is just going to ignore it anyway.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#expectations)`expectations`

the expectations to set

Looks up the “Content-Disposition” header in @self, parses it, and returns its value in *@disposition and *@params.

@params can be [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if you are only interested in the disposition-type.

In HTTP, the most common use of this header is to set a disposition-type of “attachment”, to suggest to the browser that a response should be saved to disk rather than displayed in the browser. If @params contains a “filename” parameter, this is a suggestion of a filename to use. (If the parameter value in the header contains an absolute or relative path, libsoup will truncate it down to just the final path component, so you do not need to test this yourself.)

Content-Disposition is also used in “multipart/form-data”, however
this is handled automatically by [ Multipart](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Multipart.html) and the associated
form methods.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-10)Returns

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if @self contains a “Content-Disposition”
header,

[if not (in which case *@disposition and *@params will be unchanged).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#disposition)`disposition`

return location for the
disposition-type, or `None`

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#params)`params`

return
location for the Content-Disposition parameters, or `None`

of how Content-Disposition is used in HTTP.

# MessageMetrics in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.MessageMetrics.html

`pub struct MessageMetrics { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Contains metrics collected while loading a [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) either from the
network or the disk cache.

Metrics are not collected by default for a [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html), you need to add the
flag

[to enable the feature.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageFlags.html#associatedconstant.COLLECT_METRICS)

`MessageFlags::COLLECT_METRICS`Temporal metrics are expressed as a monotonic time and always start with a fetch start event and finish with response end. All other events are optional. An event can be 0 because it hasn’t happened yet, because it’s optional or because the load failed before the event reached.

Size metrics are expressed in bytes and are updated while the [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) is
being loaded. You can connect to different

[signals to get the final result of every value.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implementations)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/message_metrics.rs.html#48-50)

#### pub fn [connect_end](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.connect_end)(&mut self) -> [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

Get the time immediately after the [ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) completed the
connection to the server. This includes the time for the proxy
negotiation and TLS handshake.

It will be 0 if no network connection was required to fetch the resource (a persistent connection was used or resource was loaded from the local disk cache).

# Multipart in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Multipart.html

`pub struct Multipart { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Represents a multipart HTTP message body, parsed according to the syntax of RFC 2046.

Of particular interest to HTTP are `multipart/byte-ranges` and
`multipart/form-data`,

Although the headers of a [ Multipart](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Multipart.html) body part will contain the
full headers from that body part, libsoup does not interpret them
according to MIME rules. For example, each body part is assumed to
have “binary” Content-Transfer-Encoding, even if its headers
explicitly state otherwise. In other words, don’t try to use

[for handling real MIME multiparts.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Multipart.html)

`Multipart`GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implementations)

Creates a new empty [ Multipart](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Multipart.html) with a randomly-generated
boundary string.

Note that @mime_type must be the full MIME type, including “multipart/”.

See also: [ Message::from_multipart()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.from_multipart).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#mime_type)`mime_type`

the MIME type of the multipart to create.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns)Returns

a new empty #SoupMultipart of the given @mime_type

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/multipart.rs.html#85-101)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/multipart.rs.html#85-101)

Adds a new MIME part containing @body to @self

Uses “Content-Disposition: form-data”, as per the HTML forms specification.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#control_name)`control_name`

the name of the control associated with this file

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#filename)`filename`

the name of the file, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if not known

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#content_type)`content_type`

the MIME type of the file, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if not known

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#body-1)`body`

the file data

# MultipartInputStream in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.MultipartInputStream.html

`pub struct MultipartInputStream { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Handles streams of multipart messages.

This adds support for the multipart responses. For handling the
multiple parts the user needs to wrap the [ gio::InputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/input_stream/struct.InputStream.html) obtained by
sending the request with a

[and use](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html)

`MultipartInputStream`[before reading. Responses which are not wrapped will be treated like non-multipart responses.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html#method.next_part)

`next_part()`Note that although [ MultipartInputStream](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html) is a

[, you should not read directly from it, and the results are undefined if you do.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/input_stream/struct.InputStream.html)

`gio::InputStream`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

Obtains the headers for the part currently being processed.

Note that the [ MessageHeaders](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html) that are returned are owned by the

[and will be replaced when a call is made to](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html)

`MultipartInputStream`[or its async counterpart, so if keeping the headers is required, a copy must be made.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html#method.next_part)

`next_part()`Note that if a part had no headers at all an empty [ MessageHeaders](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html)
will be returned.

#### pub fn [next_part](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.next_part)(
    &self,
    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/cancellable/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[InputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/input_stream/struct.InputStream.html)>, [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Obtains an input stream for the next part.

When dealing with a multipart response the input stream needs to be wrapped
in a [ MultipartInputStream](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html) and this function or its async counterpart
need to be called to obtain the first part for reading.

After calling this function,
[ headers()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MultipartInputStream.html#method.headers) can be used to obtain the
headers for the first part. A read of 0 bytes indicates the end of
the part; a new call to this function should be done at that point,
to obtain the next part.

@error will only be set if an error happens during a read, [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)
is a valid return value otherwise.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#cancellable)`cancellable`

a #GCancellable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-2)Returns

a new #GInputStream, or
[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if there are no more parts

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# Server in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.Server.html

`pub struct Server { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) provides a basic implementation of an HTTP server. The
recommended usage of this server is for internal use, tasks like
a mock server for tests, a private service for IPC, etc. It is not
recommended to be exposed to untrusted clients as it may be vulnerable
to denial of service attacks or other exploits.

To begin, create a server using `Server::new()`. Add at least one
handler by calling [ ServerExtManual::add_handler()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExtManual.html#method.add_handler) or

[; the handler will be called to process any requests underneath the path you pass. (If you want all requests to go to the same handler, just pass “/” (or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExtManual.html#method.add_early_handler)

`ServerExtManual::add_early_handler()`[) for the path.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`When a new connection is accepted (or a new request is started on
an existing persistent connection), the [ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) will emit

[and then begin processing the request as described below, but note that once the message is assigned a status-code, then callbacks after that point will be skipped. Note also that it is not defined when the callbacks happen relative to various](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-started)

`request-started`[signals.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)

`ServerMessage`Once the headers have been read, [ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) will check if there is
a

`AuthDomain``(qv)` covering the Request-URI; if so, and if the
message does not contain suitable authorization, then the
[will set a status of](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html)

`AuthDomain`[on the message.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.Status.html#variant.Unauthorized)

`Status::Unauthorized`After checking for authorization, [ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) will look for “early”
handlers (added with

[) matching the Request-URI. If one is found, it will be run; in particular, this can be used to connect to signals to do a streaming read of the request body.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExtManual.html#method.add_early_handler)

`ServerExtManual::add_early_handler()`(At this point, if the request headers contain `Expect:  100-continue`, and a status code has been set, then
[ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) will skip the remaining steps and return the response.
If the request headers contain

`Expect:  100-continue` and no status code has been set,
[will return a](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

Otherwise (assuming no previous step assigned a status to the

[if an I/O error occurred before handling was completed).](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-aborted)

`request-aborted`If you want to handle the special “*” URI (eg, “OPTIONS *”), you
must explicitly register a handler for “*”; the default handler

If you want to process https connections in addition to (or instead

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#server-header)`server-header`

Server header.

If non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), the value to use for the “Server” header on

[s processed by this server.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)

`ServerMessage`The Server header is the server equivalent of the User-Agent header, and provides information about the server and its components. It contains a list of one or more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most significant product token coming first. The tokens must be brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although “-”, “_”, and “.” are also allowed), and may optionally include a “/” followed by a version string. You may also put comments, enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.

Some HTTP server implementations intentionally do not use version numbers in their Server header, so that installations running older versions of the server don’t end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security holes.

As with [ user_agent](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#user_agent), if you set a

[property that has trailing whitespace,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#server-header)

`server-header`[will append its own product token (eg,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server``libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the header for you.Readable | Writeable | Construct

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-aborted)`request-aborted`

Emitted when processing has failed for a message.

This could mean either that it could not be read (if
[ request-read](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-read) has not been emitted for it yet), or that
the response could not be written back (if

[has been emitted but](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-read)

`request-read`[has not been).](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-finished)

`request-finished`@message is in an undefined state when this signal is
emitted; the signal exists primarily to allow the server to
free any state that it may have allocated in
[ request-started](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-started).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-finished)`request-finished`

Emitted when the server has finished writing a response to a request.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-read)`request-read`

Emitted when the server has successfully read a request.

@message will have all of its request-side information filled in, and if the message was authenticated, @client will have information about that. This signal is emitted before any (non-early) handlers are called for the message, and if it sets the message’s #status_code, then normal handler processing will be skipped.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#request-started)`request-started`

Emitted when the server has started reading a new request.

@message will be completely blank; not even the Request-Line will have been read yet. About the only thing you can usefully do with it is connect to its signals.

If the request is read successfully, this will eventually
be followed by a [ request_read](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request_read) signal]. If a
response is then sent, the request processing will end with
a

[signal. If a network error occurs, the processing will instead end with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-finished)

`request-finished`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-aborted)

runtime, while `downcast` and `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast_ref)

#### fn [add_auth_domain](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.add_auth_domain)(&self, auth_domain: &impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[AuthDomain](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html)>)

Adds an authentication domain to @self.

Each auth domain will have the chance to require authentication for each request that comes in; normally auth domains will require authentication for requests on certain paths that they have been set up to watch, or that meet other criteria set by the caller. If an auth domain determines that a request requires authentication (and the request doesn’t contain authentication), @self will automatically reject the request with an appropriate status (401 Unauthorized or 407 Proxy Authentication Required). If the request used the SoupServer:100-continue Expectation, @self will reject it before the request body is sent.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#auth_domain)`auth_domain`

a #SoupAuthDomain

#### fn [disconnect](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.disconnect)(&self)

Closes and frees @self’s listening sockets.

Note that if there are currently requests in progress on @self, that they
will continue to be processed if @self’s [ glib::MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/auto/main_context/struct.MainContext.html) is still
running.

You can call [ listen()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.listen), etc, after calling this function
if you want to start listening again.

Gets @self’s list of listening sockets.

You should treat these sockets as read-only; writing to or modifiying any of these sockets may cause @self to malfunction.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-1)Returns

a list of listening sockets.

Gets a list of URIs corresponding to the interfaces @self is listening on.

These will contain IP addresses, not hostnames, and will also indicate whether the given listener is http or https.

Note that if you used [ listen_all()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.listen_all) the returned URIs will use
the addresses

`0.0.0.0` and `::`, rather than actually returning separate
URIs for each interface on the system.[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-5)Returns

a list of [ glib::Uri](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/auto/uri/struct.Uri.html), which you
must free with each element with

`GLib::Uri::unref()` when you are done with it.Checks whether @self is capable of https.

In order for a server to run https, you must call
[ set_tls_certificate()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.set_tls_certificate), or set the

[property, to provide it with a certificate to use.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#tls-certificate)

`tls-certificate`If you are using the deprecated single-listener APIs, then a return value of
[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicates that the

[serves https exclusively. If you are using](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server`[, etc, then a](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.listen)

`listen()`[return value merely indicates that the server is](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`*able*to do https, regardless of whether it actually currently is or not. Use

[to see if it currently has any https listeners.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.uris)

#### fn [listen](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.listen)(
    &self,
    address: &impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[SocketAddress](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/socket_address/struct.SocketAddress.html)>,
    options: [ServerListenOptions](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerListenOptions.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Attempts to set up @self to listen for connections on @address.

If @options includes [ ServerListenOptions::HTTPS](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerListenOptions.html#associatedconstant.HTTPS), and @self has
been configured for TLS, then @self will listen for https
connections on this port. Otherwise it will listen for plain http.

You may call this method (along with the other “listen” methods) any number of times on a server, if you want to listen on multiple ports, or set up both http and https service.

After calling this method, @self will begin accepting and processing
connections as soon as the appropriate [ glib::MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/auto/main_context/struct.MainContext.html) is run.

Note that this API does not make use of dual IPv4/IPv6 sockets; if @address is an IPv6 address, it will only accept IPv6 connections. You must configure IPv4 listening separately.

the address of the interface to listen on

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#options)`options`

listening options for this server

Attempts to set up @self to listen for connections on all interfaces on the system.

That is, it listens on the addresses `0.0.0.0` and/or `::`, depending on
whether @options includes [ ServerListenOptions::IPV4_ONLY](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerListenOptions.html#associatedconstant.IPV4_ONLY),

[, or neither.) If @port is specified, @self will listen on that port. If it is 0, @self will find an unused port to listen on. (In that case, you can use](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerListenOptions.html#associatedconstant.IPV6_ONLY)

`ServerListenOptions::IPV6_ONLY`[to find out what port it ended up choosing.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.uris)

`uris()`See [ listen()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.ServerExt.html#method.listen) for more details.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#port)`port`

the port to listen on, or 0

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#options-1)`options`

listening options for this server

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-8)Returns

Server header.

If non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), the value to use for the “Server” header on

[s processed by this server.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)

`ServerMessage`The Server header is the server equivalent of the User-Agent header, and provides information about the server and its components. It contains a list of one or more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most significant product token coming first. The tokens must be brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although “-”, “_”, and “.” are also allowed), and may optionally include a “/” followed by a version string. You may also put comments, enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.

Some HTTP server implementations intentionally do not use version numbers in their Server header, so that installations running older versions of the server don’t end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security holes.

As with [ user_agent](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#user_agent), if you set a

[property that has trailing whitespace,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#server-header)

`server-header`[will append its own product token (eg,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server``libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the header for you.[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/server.rs.html#910-912)#### fn [set_server_header](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_server_header)(&self, server_header: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>)

Emitted when the server has started reading a new request.

@message will be completely blank; not even the Request-Line will have been read yet. About the only thing you can usefully do with it is connect to its signals.

If the request is read successfully, this will eventually
be followed by a [ request_read](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request_read) signal]. If a
response is then sent, the request processing will end with
a

[signal. If a network error occurs, the processing will instead end with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-finished)

`request-finished`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#request-aborted)

# ServerMessage in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.ServerMessage.html

`pub struct ServerMessage { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An HTTP server request and response pair.

A [ ServerMessage](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html) represents an HTTP message that is being sent or
received on a

[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server`[ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) will create

[s automatically for incoming requests, which your application will receive via handlers.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)

`ServerMessage`Note that libsoup’s terminology here does not quite match the HTTP
specification: in RFC 2616, an “HTTP-message” is *either* a Request, *or* a
Response. In libsoup, a [ ServerMessage](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html) combines both the request and the
response.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#tls-peer-certificate)`tls-peer-certificate`

The peer’s #GTlsCertificate associated with the message

Readable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#tls-peer-certificate-errors)`tls-peer-certificate-errors`

The verification errors on `tls-peer-certificate`

Readable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#accept-certificate)`accept-certificate`

Emitted during the @msg’s connection TLS handshake
after client TLS certificate has been received.
You can return [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) to accept @tls_certificate despite
@tls_errors.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#connected)`connected`

Emitted when the @msg’s socket is connected and the TLS handshake completed.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#disconnected)`disconnected`

Emitted when the @msg’s socket is disconnected.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#finished)`finished`

Emitted when all HTTP processing is finished for a message.
(After [ wrote-body](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#wrote-body)).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-body)`got-body`

Emitted after receiving the complete request body.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-chunk)`got-chunk`

Emitted after receiving a chunk of a message body.

Note that “chunk” in this context means any subpiece of the body, not necessarily the specific HTTP 1.1 chunks sent by the other side.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#got-headers)`got-headers`

Emitted after receiving the Request-Line and request headers.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#wrote-body)`wrote-body`

Emitted immediately after writing the complete response body for a message.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#wrote-body-data)`wrote-body-data`

Emitted immediately after writing a portion of the message body to the network.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#wrote-chunk)`wrote-chunk`

Emitted immediately after writing a body chunk for a message.

Note that this signal is not parallel to
[ got-chunk](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#got-chunk); it is emitted only when a complete
chunk (added with

`MessageBody::append()` or
[has been written. To get more useful continuous progress information, use](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.append_bytes)

`MessageBody::append_bytes()`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#wrote-body-data)

`wrote-body-data`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#wrote-headers)`wrote-headers`

Emitted immediately after writing the response headers for a message.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#wrote-informational)`wrote-informational`

Emitted immediately after writing a 1xx (Informational) response.

Sets @self’s status_code to @status_code and adds a Location header
pointing to @redirect_uri. Use this from a [ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html) when you
want to redirect the client to another URI.

@redirect_uri can be a relative URI, in which case it is
interpreted relative to @self’s current URI. In particular, if
@redirect_uri is just a path, it will replace the path
*and query* of @self’s URI.

“Steals” the HTTP connection associated with @self from its [ Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html). This
happens immediately, regardless of the current state of the connection; if

discarded; you can steal the connection from a

[or](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#wrote-informational)

`wrote-informational`[signal handler if you need to wait for part or all of the response to be sent.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#wrote-body)

`wrote-body`Note that when calling this function from C, @self will most likely be freed as a side effect.

connection). No guarantees are made about what kind of #GIOStream
is returned.

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# SessionFeature in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.SessionFeature.html

`pub struct SessionFeature { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Interface for miscellaneous [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) features.

[ SessionFeature](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html) is the interface used by classes that extend
the functionality of a

[. Some features like HTTP authentication handling are implemented internally via](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`[s. Other features can be added to the session by the application. (Eg,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html)

`SessionFeature`[,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Logger.html)

`Logger`[.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html)

`CookieJar`See [ SessionExt::add_feature()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.add_feature), etc, to add a feature to a session.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# WebsocketConnection in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.WebsocketConnection.html

`pub struct WebsocketConnection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The WebSocket Protocol

Provides support for the [WebSocket](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6455)
protocol.

To connect to a WebSocket server, create a [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) and call

`Session::websocket_connect_async()`. To accept WebSocket
connections, create a [and add a handler to it with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExtManual.html#method.add_websocket_handler)

`ServerExtManual::add_websocket_handler()`(Lower-level support is available via
`websocket_client_prepare_handshake()` and
`websocket_client_verify_handshake()`, for handling the client side of the
WebSocket handshake, and `websocket_server_process_handshake()` for
handling the server side.)

[ WebsocketConnection](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html) handles the details of WebSocket communication. You
can use

[and](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#method.send_text)

`send_text()``WebsocketConnection::send_binary()` to send data, and the
[signal to receive data. (](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#message)

`message`[currently only supports asynchronous I/O.)](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html)

`WebsocketConnection`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#connection-type)`connection-type`

The type of connection (client/server).

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#extensions)`extensions`

List of [ WebsocketExtension](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketExtension.html) objects that are active in the connection.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#io-stream)`io-stream`

The underlying IO stream the WebSocket is communicating over.

The input and output streams must be pollable streams.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#keepalive-interval)`keepalive-interval`

Interval in seconds on when to send a ping message which will serve as a keepalive message.

If set to 0 the keepalive message is disabled.

Readable | Writeable | Construct

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#keepalive-pong-timeout)`keepalive-pong-timeout`

Timeout in seconds for when the absence of a pong from a keepalive ping is assumed to be caused by a faulty connection. The WebSocket will be transitioned to a closed state when this happens.

If set to 0 then the absence of pongs from keepalive pings is ignored.

Readable | Writeable | Construct

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#max-incoming-payload-size)`max-incoming-payload-size`

The maximum payload size for incoming packets, or 0 to not limit it.

Each message may consist of multiple packets, so also refer to
[ max-total-message-size](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#max-total-message-size).

Readable | Writeable | Construct

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#max-total-message-size)`max-total-message-size`

The maximum size for incoming messages.

Set to a value to limit the total message size, or 0 to not limit it.

[ ServerExtManual::add_websocket_handler()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExtManual.html#method.add_websocket_handler) will set this to a nonzero
default value to mitigate denial of service attacks. Clients must
choose their own default if they need to mitigate denial of service
attacks. You also need to set your own default if creating your own
server SoupWebsocketConnection without using SoupServer.

Each message may consist of multiple packets, so also refer to
[ max-incoming-payload-size](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#max-incoming-payload-size).

Readable | Writeable | Construct

upon.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

The current state of the WebSocket.

Readable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#uri)`uri`

The URI of the WebSocket.

For servers this represents the address of the WebSocket, and for clients it is the address connected to.

Readable | Writeable | Construct Only

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#closed)`closed`

Emitted when the connection has completely closed.

This happens either due to an orderly close from the peer, one
initiated via [ WebsocketConnection::close()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#method.close) or a fatal error
condition that caused a close.

This signal will be emitted once.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#closing)`closing`

This signal will be emitted during an orderly close.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#error)`error`

Emitted when an error occurred on the WebSocket.

This may be fired multiple times. Fatal errors will be followed by
the [ closed](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#closed) signal being emitted.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#message)`message`

Emitted when we receive a message from the peer.

As a convenience, the @message data will always be
[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)-terminated, but the NUL byte will not be included in
the length count.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#pong)`pong`

Emitted when we receive a Pong frame (solicited or unsolicited) from the peer.

As a convenience, the @message data will always be
[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)-terminated, but the NUL byte will not be included in
the length count.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], `WebsocketConnectionExtManual`

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

#### pub fn [builder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.builder)() -> [WebsocketConnectionBuilder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/builders/struct.WebsocketConnectionBuilder.html)

Creates a new builder-pattern struct instance to construct [ WebsocketConnection](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html) objects.

This method returns an instance of [ WebsocketConnectionBuilder](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/builders/struct.WebsocketConnectionBuilder.html) which can be used to create

[objects.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html)

`WebsocketConnection`Close the connection in an orderly fashion.

Note that until the [ closed](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#closed) signal fires, the connection
is not yet completely closed. The close message is not even sent until the
main loop runs.

The @code and @data are sent to the peer along with the close request.
If @code is [ WebsocketCloseCode::NoStatus](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.WebsocketCloseCode.html#variant.NoStatus) a close message with no body
(without code and data) is sent.
Note that the @data must be UTF-8 valid.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#code)`code`

close code

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#data)`data`

close data

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# WebsocketExtensionDeflate in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.WebsocketExtensionDeflate.html

`pub struct WebsocketExtensionDeflate { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A SoupWebsocketExtensionDeflate is a [ WebsocketExtension](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketExtension.html)
implementing permessage-deflate (RFC 7692).

This extension is used by default in a [ Session](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html) when

[feature is present, and always used by](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketExtensionManager.html)

`WebsocketExtensionManager`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[ WebsocketExtensionExt](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.WebsocketExtensionExt.html), [

`trait@glib::ObjectExt`]GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# WebsocketExtensionManager in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/struct.WebsocketExtensionManager.html

`pub struct WebsocketExtensionManager { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

SoupWebsocketExtensionManager is the [ SessionFeature](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.SessionFeature.html) that handles WebSockets
extensions for a

[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html)

`Session`A [ WebsocketExtensionManager](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketExtensionManager.html) is added to the session by default, and normally
you don’t need to worry about it at all. However, if you want to
disable WebSocket extensions, you can remove the feature from the
session with

[or disable it on individual requests with](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.SessionExt.html#method.remove_feature_by_type)

`SessionExt::remove_feature_by_type()`[.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.disable_feature)

`Message::disable_feature()`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#implements)Implements

[`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], `SessionFeatureExt`

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# CookieJarAcceptPolicy in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/enum.CookieJarAcceptPolicy.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum CookieJarAcceptPolicy {
    Always,
    Never,
    NoThirdParty,
    GrandfatheredThirdParty,
}
```
## Expand description

The policy for accepting or rejecting cookies returned in responses.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Always)

### Always

accept all cookies unconditionally.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Never)

### Never

reject all cookies unconditionally.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.NoThirdParty)

### NoThirdParty

accept all cookies set by the main
document loaded in the application using libsoup. An example of the most
common case, web browsers, would be: If http://www.example.com is the page
loaded, accept all cookies set by example.com, but if a resource from
http://www.third-party.com is loaded from that page reject any cookie that
it could try to set. For libsoup to be able to tell apart first party
cookies from the rest, the application must call
[ Message::set_first_party()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.set_first_party) on each outgoing

[, setting the](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[of the main document. If no first party is set in a message when this policy is in effect, cookies will be assumed to be third party by default.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/auto/uri/struct.Uri.html)

`glib::Uri`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.GrandfatheredThirdParty)

### GrandfatheredThirdParty

accept all cookies set by
the main document loaded in the application using libsoup, and from domains
that have previously set at least one cookie when loaded as the main
document. An example of the most common case, web browsers, would be: if
http://www.example.com is the page loaded, accept all cookies set by
example.com, but if a resource from http://www.third-party.com is loaded
from that page, reject any cookie that it could try to set unless it
already has a cookie in the cookie jar. For libsoup to be able to tell
apart first party cookies from the rest, the application must call
[ Message::set_first_party()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#method.set_first_party) on each outgoing

[, setting the](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[of the main document. If no first party is set in a message when this policy is in effect, cookies will be assumed to be third party by default.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/auto/uri/struct.Uri.html)

# DateFormat in soup - Rust

#[non_exhaustive]pub enum DateFormat {
    Http,
    Cookie,
}
```
## Expand description

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Http)

### Http

RFC 1123 format, used by the HTTP “Date” header. Eg “Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT”.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Cookie)

### Cookie

The format for the “Expires” timestamp in the Netscape cookie specification. Eg, “Sun, 06-Nov-1994 08:49:37 GMT”.

# MemoryUse in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/enum.MemoryUse.html

Enum MemoryUse   Copy item path  Source  #[non_exhaustive]

pub enum MemoryUse {
    Static,
    Take,
    Copy,
}Expand description The lifetime of the memory being passed.

This enum is marked as non-exhaustive Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

The memory is statically allocated and
constant; libsoup can use the passed-in buffer directly and not
need to worry about it being modified or freed.

The caller has allocated the memory and libsoup
will assume ownership of it and free it with `free()`.

The passed-in data belongs to the caller and
libsoup will copy it into new memory leaving the caller free
to reuse the original memory.

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

Read more Formats the value using the given formatter.

Read more Converts to this type from the input type.

Value type checker.

Get the contained value from a

`Value`.

Read more Preferred value to be used as setter for the associated ParamSpec.

Compares and returns the maximum of two values.

Read more Compares and returns the minimum of two values.

Read more Restrict a value to a certain interval.

#[non_exhaustive]pub enum SameSitePolicy {
    None,
    Lax,
    Strict,
}
```
## Expand description

Represents the same-site policies of a cookie.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.None)

### None

The cookie is exposed with both cross-site and same-site requests

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Lax)

### Lax

The cookie is withheld on cross-site requests but exposed on cross-site navigations

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Strict)

### Strict

The cookie is only exposed for same-site requests

These represent the known HTTP status code values, plus various network and internal errors.

Note that no libsoup functions take or return this type directly; any function that works with status codes will accept unrecognized status codes as well.

#[non_exhaustive]pub enum WebsocketCloseCode {
    Normal,
    GoingAway,
    ProtocolError,
    UnsupportedData,
    NoStatus,
    Abnormal,
    BadData,
    PolicyViolation,
    TooBig,
    NoExtension,
    ServerError,
    TlsHandshake,
}
```
## Expand description

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Normal)

### Normal

a normal, non-error close

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.GoingAway)

### GoingAway

the client/server is going away

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.ProtocolError)

### ProtocolError

a protocol error occurred

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.UnsupportedData)

### UnsupportedData

the endpoint received data of a type that it does not support.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.NoStatus)

### NoStatus

reserved value indicating that no close code was present; must not be sent.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Abnormal)

### Abnormal

reserved value indicating that the connection was closed abnormally; must not be sent.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.BadData)

### BadData

the endpoint received data that was invalid (eg, non-UTF-8 data in a text message).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.PolicyViolation)

### PolicyViolation

generic error code indicating some sort of policy violation.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.TooBig)

### TooBig

the endpoint received a message that is too big to process.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.NoExtension)

### NoExtension

the client is closing the connection because the server failed to negotiate a required extension.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.ServerError)

### ServerError

the server is closing the connection because it was unable to fulfill the request.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.TlsHandshake)

### TlsHandshake

reserved value indicating that the TLS handshake failed; must not be sent.

#[non_exhaustive]pub enum WebsocketError {
    Failed,
    NotWebsocket,
    BadHandshake,
    BadOrigin,
}
```
## Expand description

WebSocket-related errors.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.Failed)

### Failed

a generic error

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.NotWebsocket)

### NotWebsocket

attempted to handshake with a server that does not appear to understand WebSockets.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.BadHandshake)

### BadHandshake

the WebSocket handshake failed because some detail was invalid (eg, incorrect accept key).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#variant.BadOrigin)

### BadOrigin

the WebSocket handshake failed because the “Origin” header was not an allowed value.

# header_g_string_append_param in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/fn.header_g_string_append_param.html

## Expand description

Appends something like `name=value` to @string, taking care to quote @value
if needed, and if so, to escape any quotes or backslashes in @value.

Alternatively, if @value is a non-ASCII UTF-8 string, it will be appended using RFC5987 syntax. Although in theory this is supposed to work anywhere in HTTP that uses this style of parameter, in reality, it can only be used portably with the Content-Disposition “filename” parameter.

If @value is [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), this will just append @name to @string.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#string)`string`

a #GString being used to construct an HTTP header value

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#name)`name`

a parameter name

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#value)`value`

a parameter value, or `None`

# tld_get_base_domain in soup - Rust

Source: https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/Rust/soup3-rs/git/docs/soup/fn.tld_get_base_domain.html

## Expand description

Finds the base domain for a given @hostname

The base domain is composed by the top level domain (such as .org, .com, .co.uk, etc) plus the second level domain, for example for myhost.mydomain.com it will return mydomain.com.

Note that [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) will be returned for private URLs (those not ending
with any well known TLD) because choosing a base domain for them
would be totally arbitrary.

Prior to libsoup 2.46, this function required that @hostname be in UTF-8 if it was an IDN. From 2.46 on, the name can be in either UTF-8 or ASCII format (and the return value will be in the same format).

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#hostname)`hostname`

a hostname

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns)Returns

a pointer to the start of the base domain in @hostname. If
an error occurs, [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) will be returned and @error set.

---

Server header.

If non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), the value to use for the “Server” header on

[s processed by this server.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)

`ServerMessage`The Server header is the server equivalent of the User-Agent header, and provides information about the server and its components. It contains a list of one or more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most significant product token coming first. The tokens must be brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although “-”, “_”, and “.” are also allowed), and may optionally include a “/” followed by a version string. You may also put comments, enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.

Some HTTP server implementations intentionally do not use version numbers in their Server header, so that installations running older versions of the server don’t end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security holes.

As with [ user_agent](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#user_agent), if you set a

[property that has trailing whitespace,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html#server-header)

`server-header`[will append its own product token (eg,](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html)

`Server``libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the header for you.## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#synthetic-implementations)

`v3_6`Timeout in seconds for when the absence of a pong from a keepalive ping is assumed to be caused by a faulty connection. The WebSocket will be transitioned to a closed state when this happens.

If set to 0 then the absence of pongs from keepalive pings is ignored.

#### pub fn [max_total_message_size](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.max_total_message_size)(self, max_total_message_size: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)) -> Self

**crate feature**only.

`v3_8`The maximum size for incoming messages.

Set to a value to limit the total message size, or 0 to not limit it.

[ ServerExtManual::add_websocket_handler()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/prelude/trait.ServerExtManual.html#method.add_websocket_handler) will set this to a nonzero
default value to mitigate denial of service attacks. Clients must
choose their own default if they need to mitigate denial of service
attacks. You also need to set your own default if creating your own
server SoupWebsocketConnection without using SoupServer.

Each message may consist of multiple packets, so also refer to
[ max-incoming-payload-size](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html#max-incoming-payload-size).

#### fn [remove_path](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.remove_path)(&self, path: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Removes @path from @self.

Requests under @path on @self’s server will NOT require authentication.

This is not simply an undo-er for [ add_path()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.AuthDomainExt.html#method.add_path); it
can be used to “carve out” a subtree that does not require
authentication inside a hierarchy that does. Note also that unlike
with

[, this cannot be overridden by adding a filter, as filters can only bypass authentication that would otherwise be required, not require it where it would otherwise be unnecessary.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.AuthDomainExt.html#method.add_path)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/auth_domain.rs.html#269-301)

#### fn [set_filter](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.set_filter)<P: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&[AuthDomain](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html), &[ServerMessage](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) + 'static>(
    &self,
    filter: P,
)

Adds @filter as an authentication filter to @self.

The filter gets a chance to bypass authentication for certain requests that would otherwise require it. Eg, it might check the message’s path in some way that is too complicated to do via the other methods, or it might check the message’s method, and allow GETs but not PUTs.

The filter function returns [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if the request should still
require authentication, or

[if authentication is unnecessary for this request.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`To help prevent security holes, your filter should return [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) by
default, and only return

[under specifically-tested circumstances, rather than the other way around. Eg, in the example above, where you want to authenticate PUTs but not GETs, you should check if the method is GET and return](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`[in that case, and then return](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`[for all other methods (rather than returning](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`[for PUT and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`[for all other methods). This way if it turned out (now or later) that some paths supported additional methods besides GET and PUT, those methods would default to being NOT allowed for unauthenticated users.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`You can also set the filter by setting the SoupAuthDomain:filter
and [ filter-data](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html#filter-data) properties], which can also be
used to set the filter at construct time.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#filter)`filter`

the auth filter for @self

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#filter_data)`filter_data`

data to pass to @filter

## Provided Methods[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#provided-methods)

Constructs a [ glib::List](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/collections/list/struct.List.html) with every cookie inside the @self.

The cookies in the list are a copy of the original, so you have to free them when you are done with them.

For historical reasons this list is in reverse order.

Adds @cookie to @self.

Emits the [ changed](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.CookieJar.html#changed) signal if we are modifying an existing
cookie or adding a valid new cookie (‘valid’ means that the cookie’s expire
date is not in the past).

@first_party will be used to reject cookies coming from third party resources in case such a security policy is set in the @self.

@uri will be used to reject setting or overwriting secure cookies
from insecure origins. [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) is treated as secure.

@cookie will be ‘stolen’ by the jar, so don’t free it afterwards.

Adds an “early” handler to @self for requests prefixed by @path.

Note that “normal” and “early” handlers are matched up together, so if you add a normal handler for “/foo” and an early handler for “/foo/bar”, then a request to “/foo/bar” (or any path below it) will run only the early handler. (But if you add both handlers at the same path, then both will get run.)

For requests under @path (that have not already been assigned a
status code by a [ AuthDomain](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html) or a signal handler), @callback
will be invoked after receiving the request headers, but before
receiving the request body; the message’s method and
request-headers properties will be set.

Early handlers are generally used for processing requests with request bodies
in a streaming fashion. If you determine that the request will contain a
message body, normally you would call [ MessageBody::set_accumulate()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.set_accumulate) on
the message’s request-body to turn off request-body accumulation, and connect
to the message’s

[signal to process each chunk as it comes in.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#got-chunk)

`got-chunk`To complete the message processing after the full message body has
been read, you can either also connect to [ got-body](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#got-body),
or else you can register a non-early handler for @path as well. As
long as you have not set the status-code by the time

[is emitted, the non-early handler will be run as well.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#got-body)

`got-body`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#path)`path`

the toplevel path for the handler

callback to invoke for requests under @path

Adds a handler to @self for requests prefixed by @path.

If @path is [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) or “/”, then this will be the default handler for all
requests that don’t have a more specific handler. (Note though that if you
want to handle requests to the special “

*” URI, you must explicitly register a handler for “*”; the default handler will not be used for that case.)

For requests under @path (that have not already been assigned a
status code by a [ AuthDomain](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.AuthDomain.html), an early server handler, or a
signal handler), @callback will be invoked after receiving the
request body; the

[’s method, request-headers, and request-body properties will be set.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html)

`ServerMessage`After determining what to do with the request, the callback must at a minimum
call [ ServerMessage::set_status()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#method.set_status) on the message to set the response
status code. Additionally, it may set response headers and/or fill in the
response body.

If the callback cannot fully fill in the response before returning
(eg, if it needs to wait for information from a database, or
another network server), it should call [ ServerMessage::pause()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#method.pause)
to tell @self to not send the response right away. When the
response is ready, call

[to cause it to be sent.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#method.unpause)

`ServerMessage::unpause()`To send the response body a bit at a time using “chunked” encoding, first
call [ MessageHeaders::set_encoding()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageHeaders.html#method.set_encoding) to set

[on the response-headers. Then call](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.Encoding.html#variant.Chunked)

`Encoding::Chunked``MessageBody::append()` (or
[)) to append each chunk as it becomes ready, and](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.append_bytes)

`MessageBody::append_bytes()`[to make sure it’s running. (The server will automatically pause the message if it is using chunked encoding but no more chunks are available.) When you are done, call](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html#method.unpause)

`ServerMessage::unpause()`[to indicate that no more chunks are coming.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.MessageBody.html#method.complete)

#### fn [add_websocket_handler](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.add_websocket_handler)<P: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&[Server](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Server.html), &[ServerMessage](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.ServerMessage.html), &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &[WebsocketConnection](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.WebsocketConnection.html)) + 'static>(
    &self,
    path: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
    origin: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
    protocols: &[&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)],
    callback: P,
)

Adds a WebSocket handler to @self for requests prefixed by @path.

If @path is [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) or “/”, then this will be the default handler for all
requests that don’t have a more specific handler.

When a path has a WebSocket handler registered, @self will check incoming requests for WebSocket handshakes after all other handlers have run (unless some earlier handler has already set a status code on the message), and update the request’s status, response headers, and response body accordingly.

If @origin is non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), then only requests containing a matching
“Origin” header will be accepted. If @protocols is non-

[, then only requests containing a compatible “Sec-WebSocket-Protocols” header will be accepted. More complicated requirements can be handled by adding a normal handler to @path, and having it perform whatever checks are needed and setting a failure status code if the handshake should be rejected.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#path-2)`path`

the toplevel path for the handler

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#origin)`origin`

the origin of the connection

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#protocols)`protocols`

the protocols supported by this handler

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#callback-2)`callback`

callback to invoke for successful WebSocket requests under @path

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

#### fn [preconnect_async](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.preconnect_async)<P: [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)([Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>) + 'static>(
    &self,
    msg: &[Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html),
    io_priority: [Priority](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/source/struct.Priority.html),
    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/cancellable/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
    callback: P,
)

Start a preconnection to @msg.

Once the connection is done, it will remain in idle state so that it can be reused by future requests. If there’s already an idle connection for the given @msg host, the operation finishes successfully without creating a new connection. If a new request for the given @msg host is made while the preconnect is still ongoing, the request will take the ownership of the connection and the preconnect operation will finish successfully (if there’s a connection error it will be handled by the request).

The operation finishes when the connection is done or an error occurred.

#### fn [send](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.send)(
    &self,
    msg: &[Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html),
    cancellable: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[Cancellable](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/cancellable/struct.Cancellable.html)>>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[InputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/input_stream/struct.InputStream.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Synchronously sends @msg and waits for the beginning of a response.

On success, a [ gio::InputStream](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/gio/auto/input_stream/struct.InputStream.html) will be returned which you can use to
read the response body. (“Success” here means only that an HTTP
response was received and understood; it does not necessarily mean
that a 2xx class status code was received.)

If non-[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), @cancellable can be used to cancel the request;

[will return a](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.SessionExt.html#method.send)

`send()``G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED` error. Note that
with requests that have side effects (eg, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) it is
possible that you might cancel the request after the server acts on it, but
before it returns a response, leaving the remote resource in an unknown
state.If @msg is requeued due to a redirect or authentication, the
initial (`3xx/401/407`) response body will be suppressed, and
[ send()](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/trait.SessionExt.html#method.send) will only return once a final response has been
received.

Possible error domains include [ SessionError](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/enum.SessionError.html),

`Gio::IOErrorEnum`,
and `Gio::TlsError` which you may want to specifically handle.[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#msg-2)`msg`

a #SoupMessage

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#cancellable-1)`cancellable`

a #GCancellable

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-16)Returns

a #GInputStream for reading the
response body, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on error.

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/session.rs.html#1508-1536)#### fn [connect_request_queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.connect_request_queued)<F: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&Self, &[Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)) + 'static>(
    &self,

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/session.rs.html#1508-1536)

#### fn [connect_request_queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#method.connect_request_queued)<F: [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&Self, &[Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)) + 'static>(
    &self,
    f: F,
) -> [SignalHandlerId](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/signal/struct.SignalHandlerId.html)

Emitted when a request is queued on @session.

When sending a request, first [ request-queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-queued)
is emitted, indicating that the session has become aware of
the request.

After a connection is available to send the request various
[ Message](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html) signals are emitted as the message is
processed. If the message is requeued, it will emit

[, which will then be followed by other](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#restarted)

`restarted`[signals when the message is re-sent.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`Eventually, the message will emit [ finished](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#finished).
Normally, this signals the completion of message
processing. However, it is possible that the application
will requeue the message from the “finished” handler.
In that case the process will loop back.

Eventually, a message will reach “finished” and not be
requeued. At that point, the session will emit
[ request-unqueued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-unqueued) to indicate that it is done
with the message.

To sum up: [ request-queued](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-queued) and

[are guaranteed to be emitted exactly once, but](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Session.html#request-unqueued)

`request-unqueued`[(and all of the other](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html#finished)

`finished`[signals) may be invoked multiple times for a given message.](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/struct.Message.html)

`Message`[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#msg-8)`msg`

the request that was queued

## Provided Methods[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#provided-methods)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/websocket_extension.rs.html#94-113)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/websocket_extension.rs.html#94-113)

Process a message after it’s received.

If the payload isn’t changed the given @payload is just returned, otherwise
`GLib::Bytes::unref()` is called on the given @payload and a new
[ glib::Bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/bytes/struct.Bytes.html) is returned with the new data.

Extensions using reserved bits of the header will reset them in @header.

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#header)`header`

the message header

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#payload)`payload`

the payload data

[§](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#returns-2)Returns

the message payload data, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) in case of error

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/websocket_extension.rs.html#131-150)

[Source](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/src/soup/auto/websocket_extension.rs.html#131-150)

Process a message before it’s sent.

If the payload isn’t changed the given @payload is just returned, otherwise
`Glib::Bytes::unref()` is called on the given @payload and a new
[ glib::Bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/glib/bytes/struct.Bytes.html) is returned with the new data.

Extensions using reserved bits of the header will change them in @header.
