[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// Server-side authentication.
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    ///
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// A [`AuthDomain`][crate::AuthDomain] manages authentication for all or part of a
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server]. To make a server require authentication, first create
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// an appropriate subclass of [`AuthDomain`][crate::AuthDomain], and then add it to the
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// server with [`ServerExt::add_auth_domain()`][crate::prelude::ServerExt::add_auth_domain()].
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    ///
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// In order for an auth domain to have any effect, you must add one or more
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// paths to it (via [`AuthDomainExt::add_path()`][crate::prelude::AuthDomainExt::add_path()]). To require authentication for
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// all ordinary requests, add the path `"/"`. (Note that this does not include
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// the special `"*"` URI (eg, "OPTIONS *"), which must be added as a separate
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// path if you want to cover it.)
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    ///
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// If you need greater control over which requests should and shouldn't be
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// authenticated, add paths covering everything you *might* want authenticated,
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// and then use a filter ([`AuthDomainExt::set_filter()`][crate::prelude::AuthDomainExt::set_filter()] to bypass
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// authentication for those requests that don't need it.
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    ///
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    ///
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// ## Properties
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    ///
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    ///
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// #### `filter`

[214](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#214)    /// Removes @path from @self.
[215](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#215)    ///
[216](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#216)    /// Requests under @path on @self's server will NOT require
[217](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#217)    /// authentication.
[218](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#218)    ///
[219](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#219)    /// This is not simply an undo-er for [`add_path()`][Self::add_path()]; it
[220](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#220)    /// can be used to "carve out" a subtree that does not require
[221](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#221)    /// authentication inside a hierarchy that does. Note also that unlike
[222](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#222)    /// with [`add_path()`][Self::add_path()], this cannot be overridden by
[223](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#223)    /// adding a filter, as filters can only bypass authentication that
[224](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#224)    /// would otherwise be required, not require it where it would
[225](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#225)    /// otherwise be unnecessary.
[226](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#226)    /// ## `path`
[227](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#227)    /// the path to remove from @self

[232](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#232)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[233](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#233)                path.to_glib_none().0,

[237](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#237)
[238](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#238)    /// Adds @filter as an authentication filter to @self.
[239](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#239)    ///
[240](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#240)    /// The filter gets a chance to bypass authentication for certain requests that
[241](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#241)    /// would otherwise require it. Eg, it might check the message's path in some way
[242](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#242)    /// that is too complicated to do via the other methods, or it might check the
[243](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#243)    /// message's method, and allow GETs but not PUTs.
[244](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#244)    ///
[245](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#245)    /// The filter function returns [`true`] if the request should still
[246](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#246)    /// require authentication, or [`false`] if authentication is unnecessary
[247](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#247)    /// for this request.
[248](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#248)    ///
[249](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#249)    /// To help prevent security holes, your filter should return [`true`] by
[250](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#250)    /// default, and only return [`false`] under specifically-tested
[251](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#251)    /// circumstances, rather than the other way around. Eg, in the example
[252](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#252)    /// above, where you want to authenticate PUTs but not GETs, you should
[253](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#253)    /// check if the method is GET and return [`false`] in that case, and then
[254](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#254)    /// return [`true`] for all other methods (rather than returning [`true`] for
[255](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#255)    /// PUT and [`false`] for all other methods). This way if it turned out
[256](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#256)    /// (now or later) that some paths supported additional methods besides
[257](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#257)    /// GET and PUT, those methods would default to being NOT allowed for
[258](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#258)    /// unauthenticated users.
[259](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#259)    ///
[260](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#260)    /// You can also set the filter by setting the SoupAuthDomain:filter
[261](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#261)    /// and [`filter-data`][struct@crate::AuthDomain#filter-data] properties], which can also be
[262](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#262)    /// used to set the filter at construct time.
[263](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#263)    /// ## `filter`
[264](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#264)    /// the auth filter for @self
[265](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#265)    /// ## `filter_data`
[266](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#266)    /// data to pass to @filter
[267](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#267)    #[doc(alias = "soup_auth_domain_set_filter")]
[268](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#268)    #[doc(alias = "filter")]
[269](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#269)    fn set_filter<P: Fn(&AuthDomain, &ServerMessage) -> bool + 'static>(&self, filter: P) {
[270](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#270)        let filter_data: Box_<P> = Box_::new(filter);
[271](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#271)        unsafe extern "C" fn filter_func<P: Fn(&AuthDomain, &ServerMessage) -> bool + 'static>(
[272](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#272)            domain: *mut ffi::SoupAuthDomain,
[273](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#273)            msg: *mut ffi::SoupServerMessage,
[274](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#274)            user_data: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[275](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#275)        ) -> glib::ffi::gboolean {
[276](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#276)            unsafe {
[277](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#277)                let domain = from_glib_borrow(domain);
[278](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#278)                let msg = from_glib_borrow(msg);
[279](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#279)                let callback = &*(user_data as *mut P);
[280](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#280)                (*callback)(&domain, &msg).into_glib()
[281](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#281)            }
[282](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#282)        }
[283](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#283)        let filter = Some(filter_func::<P> as _);
[284](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#284)        unsafe extern "C" fn dnotify_func<P: Fn(&AuthDomain, &ServerMessage) -> bool + 'static>(
[285](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#285)            data: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[286](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#286)        ) {
[287](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#287)            unsafe {
[288](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#288)                let _callback = Box_::from_raw(data as *mut P);
[289](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#289)            }
[290](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#290)        }
[291](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#291)        let destroy_call3 = Some(dnotify_func::<P> as _);
[292](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#292)        let super_callback0: Box_<P> = filter_data;
[293](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#293)        unsafe {
[294](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#294)            ffi::soup_auth_domain_set_filter(
[295](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#295)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[296](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#296)                filter,
[297](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#297)                Box_::into_raw(super_callback0) as *mut _,
[298](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#298)                destroy_call3,
[299](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#299)            );
[300](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#300)        }
[301](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#301)    }
[302](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#302)
[303](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#303)    /// Sets @auth_callback as an authentication-handling callback for @self.
[304](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#304)    ///
[305](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#305)    /// Whenever a request comes in to @self which cannot be authenticated via a
[306](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#306)    /// domain-specific auth callback (eg, `callback::AuthDomainDigestAuthCallback),
[307](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#307)    /// the generic auth callback will be invoked. See
[308](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#308)    /// `callback::AuthDomainGenericAuthCallback for information on what the callback
[309](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#309)    /// should do.
[310](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#310)    /// ## `auth_callback`
[311](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#311)    /// the auth callback

[165](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#165)    //}
[166](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#166)
[167](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#167)    /// Encodes the username/realm/password triplet for Digest
[168](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#168)    /// authentication.
[169](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#169)    ///
[170](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#170)    /// That is, it returns a stringified MD5 hash of
[171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#171)    /// @username, @realm, and @password concatenated together. This is
[172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#172)    /// the form that is needed as the return value of
[173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#173)    /// [`AuthDomainDigest`][crate::AuthDomainDigest]'s auth handler.
[174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#174)    ///
[175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#175)    /// For security reasons, you should store the encoded hash, rather
[176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#176)    /// than storing the cleartext password itself and calling this method
[177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#177)    /// only when you need to verify it. This way, if your server is
[178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#178)    /// compromised, the attackers will not gain access to cleartext
[179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#179)    /// passwords which might also be usable at other sites. (Note also
[180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#180)    /// that the encoded password returned by this method is identical to
[181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#181)    /// the encoded password stored in an Apache .htdigest file.)
[182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#182)    /// ## `username`
[183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#183)    /// a username
[184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#184)    /// ## `realm`
[185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#185)    /// an auth realm name
[186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#186)    /// ## `password`
[187](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#187)    /// the password for @username in @realm
[188](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#188)    ///
[189](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#189)    /// # Returns
[190](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#190)    ///
[191](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#191)    /// the encoded password
[192](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#192)    #[doc(alias = "soup_auth_domain_digest_encode_password")]
[193](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#193)    pub fn encode_password(username: &str, realm: &str, password: &str) -> Option<glib::GString> {
[194](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#194)        assert_initialized_main_thread!();
[195](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#195)        unsafe {
[196](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#196)            from_glib_full(ffi::soup_auth_domain_digest_encode_password(
[197](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#197)                username.to_glib_none().0,
[198](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#198)                realm.to_glib_none().0,

[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    ///
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    /// [`ContentDecoder`][crate::ContentDecoder] handles adding the "Accept-Encoding" header on
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    /// outgoing messages, and processing the "Content-Encoding" header on
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// incoming ones. Currently it supports the "gzip", "deflate", and "br"
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// content codings.
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    ///
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// A [`ContentDecoder`][crate::ContentDecoder] will automatically be
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// added to the session by default. (You can use
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// [`SessionExt::remove_feature_by_type()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::remove_feature_by_type()] if you don't
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// want this.)
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// If [`ContentDecoder`][crate::ContentDecoder] successfully decodes the Content-Encoding,
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// the message body will contain the decoded data; however, the message headers
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// will be unchanged (and so "Content-Encoding" will still be present,
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// "Content-Length" will describe the original encoded length, etc).
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    ///
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// If "Content-Encoding" contains any encoding types that
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// [`ContentDecoder`][crate::ContentDecoder] doesn't recognize, then none of the encodings
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// will be decoded.
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    ///
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// (Note that currently there is no way to (automatically) use
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// Content-Encoding when sending a request body, or to pick specific
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// encoding types to support.)

[1](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1)// This file was generated by gir (https://github.com/gtk-rs/gir)

[9](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#9)glib::wrapper! {
[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    /// Implements HTTP cookies, as described by
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    /// [RFC 6265](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265.txt).
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    ///
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// To have a [`Session`][crate::Session] handle cookies for your appliction
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// automatically, use a [`CookieJar`][crate::CookieJar].
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    ///
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// @name and @value will be set for all cookies. If the cookie is
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// generated from a string that appears to have no name, then @name
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// will be the empty string.
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    ///
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// @domain and @path give the host or domain, and path within that
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// host/domain, to restrict this cookie to. If @domain starts with
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// ".", that indicates a domain (which matches the string after the
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// ".", or any hostname that has @domain as a suffix). Otherwise, it
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// is a hostname and must match exactly.
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    ///
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// @expires will be non-[`None`] if the cookie uses either the original
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// "expires" attribute, or the newer "max-age" attribute. If @expires
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// is [`None`], it indicates that neither "expires" nor "max-age" was
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// specified, and the cookie expires at the end of the session.
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    ///
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// If @http_only is set, the cookie should not be exposed to untrusted
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// code (eg, javascript), so as to minimize the danger posed by
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// cross-site scripting attacks.
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    #[derive(Debug, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    pub struct Cookie(Boxed<ffi::SoupCookie>);
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)

[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)        free => |ptr| ffi::soup_cookie_free(ptr),
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)        type_ => || ffi::soup_cookie_get_type(),
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    }
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)}
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)impl Cookie {
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    /// Creates a new [`Cookie`][crate::Cookie] with the given attributes.
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    ///
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    /// Use [`set_secure()`][Self::set_secure()] and [`set_http_only()`][Self::set_http_only()] if you
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    /// need to set those attributes on the returned cookie.
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    ///
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)    /// If @domain starts with ".", that indicates a domain (which matches
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)    /// the string after the ".", or any hostname that has @domain as a
[52](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#52)    /// suffix). Otherwise, it is a hostname and must match exactly.
[53](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#53)    ///
[54](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#54)    /// @max_age is used to set the "expires" attribute on the cookie; pass
[55](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#55)    /// -1 to not include the attribute (indicating that the cookie expires
[56](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#56)    /// with the current session), 0 for an already-expired cookie, or a
[57](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#57)    /// lifetime in seconds. You can use the constants
[58](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#58)    /// `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_HOUR`, `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_DAY`,
[59](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#59)    /// `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_WEEK` and `SOUP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_ONE_YEAR` (or
[60](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#60)    /// multiples thereof) to calculate this value. (If you really care
[61](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#61)    /// about setting the exact time that the cookie will expire, use
[62](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#62)    /// [`set_expires()`][Self::set_expires()].)
[63](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#63)    ///
[64](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#64)    /// As of version 3.4.0 the default value of a cookie's same-site-policy
[65](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#65)    /// is [`SameSitePolicy::Lax`][crate::SameSitePolicy::Lax].
[66](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#66)    /// ## `name`

[68](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#68)    /// ## `value`

[70](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#70)    /// ## `domain`

[72](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#72)    /// ## `path`
[73](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#73)    /// cookie path, or [`None`]
[74](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#74)    /// ## `max_age`
[75](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#75)    /// max age of the cookie, or -1 for a session cookie

[376](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#376)    /// Emitted when @jar changes.
[377](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#377)    ///
[378](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#378)    /// If a cookie has been added,
[379](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#379)    /// @new_cookie will contain the newly-added cookie and
[380](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#380)    /// @old_cookie will be [`None`]. If a cookie has been deleted,
[381](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#381)    /// @old_cookie will contain the to-be-deleted cookie and
[382](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#382)    /// @new_cookie will be [`None`]. If a cookie has been changed,
[383](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#383)    /// @old_cookie will contain its old value, and @new_cookie its
[384](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#384)    /// new value.
[385](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#385)    /// ## `old_cookie`
[386](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#386)    /// the old #SoupCookie value
[387](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#387)    /// ## `new_cookie`
[388](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#388)    /// the new #SoupCookie value
[389](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#389)    #[doc(alias = "changed")]
[390](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#390)    fn connect_changed<F: Fn(&Self, Option<&Cookie>, Option<&Cookie>) + 'static>(
[391](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#391)        &self,
[392](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#392)        f: F,
[393](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#393)    ) -> SignalHandlerId {
[394](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#394)        unsafe extern "C" fn changed_trampoline<
[395](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#395)            P: IsA<CookieJar>,
[396](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#396)            F: Fn(&P, Option<&Cookie>, Option<&Cookie>) + 'static,
[397](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#397)        >(
[398](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#398)            this: *mut ffi::SoupCookieJar,
[399](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#399)            old_cookie: *mut ffi::SoupCookie,
[400](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#400)            new_cookie: *mut ffi::SoupCookie,
[401](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#401)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[402](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#402)        ) {
[403](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#403)            unsafe {
[404](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#404)                let f: &F = &*(f as *const F);
[405](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#405)                f(
[406](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#406)                    CookieJar::from_glib_borrow(this).unsafe_cast_ref(),
[407](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#407)                    Option::<Cookie>::from_glib_borrow(old_cookie)
[408](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#408)                        .as_ref()
[409](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#409)                        .as_ref(),
[410](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#410)                    Option::<Cookie>::from_glib_borrow(new_cookie)
[411](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#411)                        .as_ref()
[412](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#412)                        .as_ref(),
[413](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#413)                )
[414](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#414)            }
[415](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#415)        }
[416](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#416)        unsafe {
[417](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#417)            let f: Box_<F> = Box_::new(f);
[418](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#418)            connect_raw(
[419](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#419)                self.as_ptr() as *mut _,
[420](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#420)                c"changed".as_ptr(),
[421](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#421)                Some(std::mem::transmute::<*const (), unsafe extern "C" fn()>(
[422](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#422)                    changed_trampoline::<Self, F> as *const (),
[423](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#423)                )),
[424](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#424)                Box_::into_raw(f),
[425](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#425)            )
[426](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#426)        }
[427](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#427)    }
[428](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#428)
[429](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#429)    #[doc(alias = "accept-policy")]
[430](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#430)    fn connect_accept_policy_notify<F: Fn(&Self) + 'static>(&self, f: F) -> SignalHandlerId {
[431](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#431)        unsafe extern "C" fn notify_accept_policy_trampoline<
[432](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#432)            P: IsA<CookieJar>,
[433](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#433)            F: Fn(&P) + 'static,
[434](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#434)        >(
[435](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#435)            this: *mut ffi::SoupCookieJar,
[436](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#436)            _param_spec: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[437](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#437)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,

[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// Automatic HTTP Strict Transport Security enforcing for [`Session`][crate::Session].
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    ///
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// A [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] stores HSTS policies and enforces them when
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// required. [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] implements [`SessionFeature`][crate::SessionFeature], so you
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// can add an HSTS enforcer to a session with
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// [`SessionExt::add_feature()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::add_feature()] or [`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()].
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    ///
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] keeps track of all the HTTPS destinations that,
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// when connected to, return the Strict-Transport-Security header with
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// valid values. [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] will forget those destinations
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// upon expiry or when the server requests it.
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    ///
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// When the [`Session`][crate::Session] the [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] is attached to queues or
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// restarts a message, the [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] will rewrite the URI to HTTPS if
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// the destination is a known HSTS host and is contacted over an insecure
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// transport protocol (HTTP). Users of [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] are advised to listen
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// to changes in the [`uri`][struct@crate::Message#uri] property in order to be aware of
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// changes in the message URI.
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    ///
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// Note that [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] does not support any form of long-term
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    /// HSTS policy persistence. See [`HSTSEnforcerDB`][crate::HSTSEnforcerDB] for a persistent
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    /// enforcer.
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    ///
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    /// ## Signals
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    ///
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    ///
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    /// #### `changed`
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    ///  Emitted when @hsts_enforcer changes.
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    ///
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    /// If a policy has been added,
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    /// @new_policy will contain the newly-added policy and
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    /// @old_policy will be [`None`]. If a policy has been deleted,
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    /// @old_policy will contain the to-be-deleted policy and
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    /// @new_policy will be [`None`]. If a policy has been changed,
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)    /// @old_policy will contain its old value, and @new_policy its
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)    /// new value.

[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)glib::wrapper! {
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// Soup session state object.
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    ///
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// [`Session`][crate::Session] is the object that controls client-side HTTP. A
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// [`Session`][crate::Session] encapsulates all of the state that libsoup is keeping
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// on behalf of your program; cached HTTP connections, authentication
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// information, etc. It also keeps track of various global options
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// and features that you are using.
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    ///
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// Most applications will only need a single [`Session`][crate::Session]; the primary
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// reason you might need multiple sessions is if you need to have
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// multiple independent authentication contexts. (Eg, you are
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// connecting to a server and authenticating as two different users at
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// different times; the easiest way to ensure that each [`Message`][crate::Message]
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// is sent with the authentication information you intended is to use
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// one session for the first user, and a second session for the other
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// user.)
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    ///
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// Additional [`Session`][crate::Session] functionality is provided by
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// [`SessionFeature`][crate::SessionFeature] objects, which can be added to a session with
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// [`SessionExt::add_feature()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::add_feature()] or [`SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::add_feature_by_type()]
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    /// For example, [`Logger`][crate::Logger] provides support for
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    /// logging HTTP traffic, [`ContentDecoder`][crate::ContentDecoder] provides support for
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// compressed response handling, and [`ContentSniffer`][crate::ContentSniffer] provides
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    /// support for HTML5-style response body content sniffing.
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    /// Additionally, subtypes of [`Auth`][crate::Auth] can be added
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    /// as features, to add support for additional authentication types.
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    ///
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    /// All `SoupSession`s are created with a [`AuthManager`][crate::AuthManager], and support
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    /// for `SOUP_TYPE_AUTH_BASIC` and `SOUP_TYPE_AUTH_DIGEST`. Additionally,
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    /// sessions using the plain [`Session`][crate::Session] class (rather than one of its deprecated
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    /// subtypes) have a [`ContentDecoder`][crate::ContentDecoder] by default.
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    ///
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    /// Note that all async methods will invoke their callbacks on the thread-default
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    /// context at the time of the function call.
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)    ///
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)    /// ## Properties
[52](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#52)    ///
[53](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#53)    ///
[54](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#54)    /// #### `accept-language`
[55](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#55)    ///  If non-[`None`], the value to use for the "Accept-Language" header
[56](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#56)    /// on [`Message`][crate::Message]s sent from this session.
[57](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#57)    ///
[58](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#58)    /// Setting this will disable [`accept-language-auto`][struct@crate::Session#accept-language-auto].
[59](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#59)    ///
[60](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#60)    /// Readable | Writeable
[61](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#61)    ///
[62](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#62)    ///
[63](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#63)    /// #### `accept-language-auto`
[64](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#64)    ///  If [`true`], [`Session`][crate::Session] will automatically set the string
[65](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#65)    /// for the "Accept-Language" header on every [`Message`][crate::Message]
[66](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#66)    /// sent, based on the return value of `get_language_names()`.
[67](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#67)    ///
[68](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#68)    /// Setting this will override any previous value of
[69](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#69)    /// [`accept-language`][struct@crate::Session#accept-language].
[70](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#70)    ///
[71](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#71)    /// Readable | Writeable
[72](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#72)    ///
[73](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#73)    ///
[74](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#74)    /// #### `idle-timeout`
[75](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#75)    ///  Connection lifetime (in seconds) when idle. Any connection
[76](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#76)    /// left idle longer than this will be closed.
[77](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#77)    ///
[78](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#78)    /// Although you can change this property at any time, it will
[79](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#79)    /// only affect newly-created connections, not currently-open
[80](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#80)    /// ones. You can call [`SessionExt::abort()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::abort()] after setting this
[81](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#81)    /// if you want to ensure that all future connections will have
[82](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#82)    /// this timeout value.
[83](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#83)    ///
[84](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#84)    /// Readable | Writeable
[85](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#85)    ///
[86](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#86)    ///
[87](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#87)    /// #### `local-address`
[88](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#88)    ///  Sets the [`gio::InetSocketAddress`][crate::gio::InetSocketAddress] to use for the client side of
[89](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#89)    /// the connection.
[90](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#90)    ///
[91](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#91)    /// Use this property if you want for instance to bind the
[92](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#92)    /// local socket to a specific IP address.
[93](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#93)    ///
[94](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#94)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct Only
[95](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#95)    ///
[96](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#96)    ///
[97](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#97)    /// #### `max-conns`
[98](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#98)    ///  The maximum number of connections that the session can open at once.
[99](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#99)    ///
[100](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#100)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct Only
[101](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#101)    ///
[102](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#102)    ///
[103](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#103)    /// #### `max-conns-per-host`
[104](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#104)    ///  The maximum number of connections that the session can open at once
[105](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#105)    /// to a given host.
[106](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#106)    ///
[107](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#107)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct Only
[108](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#108)    ///
[109](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#109)    ///
[110](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#110)    /// #### `proxy-resolver`
[111](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#111)    ///  A [`gio::ProxyResolver`][crate::gio::ProxyResolver] to use with this session.
[112](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#112)    ///
[113](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#113)    /// If no proxy resolver is set, then the default proxy resolver
[114](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#114)    /// will be used. See [`gio::ProxyResolver::default()`][crate::gio::ProxyResolver::default()].
[115](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#115)    /// You can set it to [`None`] if you don't want to use proxies, or
[116](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#116)    /// set it to your own [`gio::ProxyResolver`][crate::gio::ProxyResolver] if you want to control
[117](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#117)    /// what proxies get used.
[118](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#118)    ///
[119](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#119)    /// Readable | Writeable
[120](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#120)    ///
[121](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#121)    ///
[122](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#122)    /// #### `remote-connectable`
[123](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#123)    ///  Sets a socket to make outgoing connections on. This will override the default
[124](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#124)    /// behaviour of opening TCP/IP sockets to the hosts specified in the URIs.
[125](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#125)    ///
[126](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#126)    /// This function is not required for common HTTP usage, but only when connecting
[127](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#127)    /// to a HTTP service that is not using standard TCP/IP sockets. An example of
[128](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#128)    /// this is a local service that uses HTTP over UNIX-domain sockets, in that case
[129](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#129)    /// a `Gio::UnixSocketAddress` can be passed to this function.
[130](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#130)    ///
[131](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#131)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct Only
[132](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#132)    ///
[133](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#133)    ///
[134](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#134)    /// #### `timeout`
[135](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#135)    ///  The timeout (in seconds) for socket I/O operations
[136](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#136)    /// (including connecting to a server, and waiting for a reply
[137](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#137)    /// to an HTTP request).
[138](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#138)    ///
[139](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#139)    /// Although you can change this property at any time, it will
[140](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#140)    /// only affect newly-created connections, not currently-open
[141](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#141)    /// ones. You can call [`SessionExt::abort()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::abort()] after setting this
[142](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#142)    /// if you want to ensure that all future connections will have
[143](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#143)    /// this timeout value.
[144](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#144)    ///
[145](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#145)    /// Not to be confused with [`idle-timeout`][struct@crate::Session#idle-timeout] (which is
[146](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#146)    /// the length of time that idle persistent connections will be
[147](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#147)    /// kept open).
[148](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#148)    ///
[149](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#149)    /// Readable | Writeable
[150](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#150)    ///
[151](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#151)    ///
[152](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#152)    /// #### `tls-database`
[153](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#153)    ///  Sets the [`gio::TlsDatabase`][crate::gio::TlsDatabase] to use for validating SSL/TLS
[154](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#154)    /// certificates.
[155](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#155)    ///
[156](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#156)    /// If no certificate database is set, then the default database will be
[157](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#157)    /// used. See `Gio::TlsBackend::get_default_database()`.
[158](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#158)    ///
[159](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#159)    /// Readable | Writeable
[160](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#160)    ///
[161](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#161)    ///
[162](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#162)    /// #### `tls-interaction`
[163](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#163)    ///  A [`gio::TlsInteraction`][crate::gio::TlsInteraction] object that will be passed on to any
[164](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#164)    /// `Gio::TlsConnection`s created by the session.
[165](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#165)    ///
[166](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#166)    /// This can be used to provide client-side certificates, for example.
[167](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#167)    ///
[168](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#168)    /// Readable | Writeable
[169](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#169)    ///
[170](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#170)    ///
[171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#171)    /// #### `user-agent`
[172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#172)    ///  User-Agent string.
[173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#173)    ///
[174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#174)    /// If non-[`None`], the value to use for the "User-Agent" header
[175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#175)    /// on [`Message`][crate::Message]s sent from this session.
[176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#176)    ///
[177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#177)    /// RFC 2616 says: "The User-Agent request-header field
[178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#178)    /// contains information about the user agent originating the
[179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#179)    /// request. This is for statistical purposes, the tracing of
[180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#180)    /// protocol violations, and automated recognition of user
[181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#181)    /// agents for the sake of tailoring responses to avoid
[182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#182)    /// particular user agent limitations. User agents SHOULD
[183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#183)    /// include this field with requests."
[184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#184)    ///
[185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#185)    /// The User-Agent header contains a list of one or more
[186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#186)    /// product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most
[187](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#187)    /// significant product token coming first. The tokens must be
[188](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#188)    /// brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although "-", "_",
[189](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#189)    /// and "." are also allowed), and may optionally include a "/"
[190](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#190)    /// followed by a version string. You may also put comments,
[191](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#191)    /// enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.
[192](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#192)    ///
[193](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#193)    /// If you set a [`user-agent`][struct@crate::Session#user-agent] property that has trailing
[194](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#194)    /// whitespace, [`Session`][crate::Session] will append its own product token
[195](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#195)    /// (eg, `libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the
[196](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#196)    /// header for you.
[197](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#197)    ///
[198](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#198)    /// Readable | Writeable
[199](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#199)    ///
[200](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#200)    /// ## Signals
[201](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#201)    ///
[202](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#202)    ///
[203](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#203)    /// #### `request-queued`
[204](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#204)    ///  Emitted when a request is queued on @session.
[205](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#205)    ///
[206](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#206)    /// When sending a request, first [`request-queued`][struct@crate::Session#request-queued]
[207](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#207)    /// is emitted, indicating that the session has become aware of
[208](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#208)    /// the request.
[209](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#209)    ///
[210](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#210)    /// After a connection is available to send the request various
[211](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#211)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message] signals are emitted as the message is
[212](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#212)    /// processed. If the message is requeued, it will emit
[213](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#213)    /// [`restarted`][struct@crate::Message#restarted], which will then be followed by other
[214](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#214)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message] signals when the message is re-sent.
[215](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#215)    ///
[216](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#216)    /// Eventually, the message will emit [`finished`][struct@crate::Message#finished].
[217](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#217)    /// Normally, this signals the completion of message
[218](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#218)    /// processing. However, it is possible that the application
[219](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#219)    /// will requeue the message from the "finished" handler.
[220](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#220)    /// In that case the process will loop back.
[221](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#221)    ///
[222](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#222)    /// Eventually, a message will reach "finished" and not be
[223](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#223)    /// requeued. At that point, the session will emit
[224](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#224)    /// [`request-unqueued`][struct@crate::Session#request-unqueued] to indicate that it is done
[225](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#225)    /// with the message.
[226](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#226)    ///
[227](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#227)    /// To sum up: [`request-queued`][struct@crate::Session#request-queued] and
[228](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#228)    /// [`request-unqueued`][struct@crate::Session#request-unqueued] are guaranteed to be emitted
[229](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#229)    /// exactly once, but [`finished`][struct@crate::Message#finished] (and all of the other
[230](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#230)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message] signals) may be invoked multiple times for a given
[231](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#231)    /// message.
[232](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#232)    ///
[233](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#233)    ///
[234](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#234)    ///
[235](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#235)    ///
[236](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#236)    /// #### `request-unqueued`
[237](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#237)    ///  Emitted when a request is removed from @session's queue,
[238](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#238)    /// indicating that @session is done with it.
[239](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#239)    ///
[240](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#240)    /// See [`request-queued`][struct@crate::Session#request-queued] for a detailed description of
[241](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#241)    /// the message lifecycle within a session.
[242](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#242)    ///
[243](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#243)    ///
[244](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#244)    ///
[245](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#245)    /// # Implements
[246](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#246)    ///
[247](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#247)    /// [`SessionExt`][trait@crate::prelude::SessionExt], [`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], [`SessionExtManual`][trait@crate::prelude::SessionExtManual]
[248](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#248)    #[doc(alias = "SoupSession")]
[249](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#249)    pub struct Session(Object<ffi::SoupSession, ffi::SoupSessionClass>);

[451](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#451)    /// User-Agent string.
[452](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#452)    ///
[453](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#453)    /// If non-[`None`], the value to use for the "User-Agent" header
[454](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#454)    /// on [`Message`][crate::Message]s sent from this session.
[455](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#455)    ///
[456](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#456)    /// RFC 2616 says: "The User-Agent request-header field
[457](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#457)    /// contains information about the user agent originating the
[458](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#458)    /// request. This is for statistical purposes, the tracing of
[459](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#459)    /// protocol violations, and automated recognition of user
[460](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#460)    /// agents for the sake of tailoring responses to avoid
[461](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#461)    /// particular user agent limitations. User agents SHOULD
[462](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#462)    /// include this field with requests."
[463](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#463)    ///
[464](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#464)    /// The User-Agent header contains a list of one or more
[465](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#465)    /// product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most
[466](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#466)    /// significant product token coming first. The tokens must be
[467](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#467)    /// brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although "-", "_",
[468](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#468)    /// and "." are also allowed), and may optionally include a "/"
[469](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#469)    /// followed by a version string. You may also put comments,
[470](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#470)    /// enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.
[471](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#471)    ///
[472](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#472)    /// If you set a [`user-agent`][struct@crate::Session#user-agent] property that has trailing
[473](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#473)    /// whitespace, [`Session`][crate::Session] will append its own product token
[474](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#474)    /// (eg, `libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the
[475](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#475)    /// header for you.
[476](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#476)    pub fn user_agent(self, user_agent: impl Into<glib::GString>) -> Self {
[477](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#477)        Self {
[478](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#478)            builder: self.builder.property("user-agent", user_agent.into()),
[479](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#479)        }
[480](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#480)    }
[481](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#481)
[482](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#482)    // rustdoc-stripper-ignore-next
[483](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#483)    /// Build the [`Session`].
[484](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#484)    #[must_use = "Building the object from the builder is usually expensive and is not expected to have side effects"]
[485](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#485)    pub fn build(self) -> Session {
[486](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#486)        assert_initialized_main_thread!();
[487](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#487)        self.builder.build()
[488](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#488)    }

[490](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#490)
[491](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#491)/// Trait containing all [`struct@Session`] methods.
[492](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#492)///
[493](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#493)/// # Implementors
[494](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#494)///
[495](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#495)/// [`Session`][struct@crate::Session]
[496](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#496)pub trait SessionExt: IsA<Session> + 'static {
[497](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#497)    /// Cancels all pending requests in @self and closes all idle
[498](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#498)    /// persistent connections.
[499](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#499)    #[doc(alias = "soup_session_abort")]
[500](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#500)    fn abort(&self) {
[501](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#501)        unsafe {
[502](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#502)            ffi::soup_session_abort(self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0);
[503](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#503)        }
[504](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#504)    }
[505](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#505)
[506](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#506)    /// Adds @feature's functionality to @self. You cannot add multiple
[507](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#507)    /// features of the same `alias::GObject.Type` to a session.
[508](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#508)    ///
[509](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#509)    /// See the main [`Session`][crate::Session] documentation for information on what
[510](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#510)    /// features are present in sessions by default.
[511](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#511)    /// ## `feature`
[512](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#512)    /// an object that implements #SoupSessionFeature
[513](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#513)    #[doc(alias = "soup_session_add_feature")]
[514](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#514)    fn add_feature(&self, feature: &impl IsA<SessionFeature>) {
[515](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#515)        unsafe {
[516](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#516)            ffi::soup_session_add_feature(
[517](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#517)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[518](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#518)                feature.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[519](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#519)            );
[520](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#520)        }
[521](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#521)    }
[522](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#522)
[523](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#523)    /// If @feature_type is the type of a class that implements
[524](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#524)    /// [`SessionFeature`][crate::SessionFeature], this creates a new feature of that type and
[525](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#525)    /// adds it to @self as with [`add_feature()`][Self::add_feature()]. You can use
[526](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#526)    /// this when you don't need to customize the new feature in any way.
[527](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#527)    /// Adding multiple features of the same @feature_type is not allowed.
[528](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#528)    ///
[529](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#529)    /// If @feature_type is not a [`SessionFeature`][crate::SessionFeature] type, this gives each
[530](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#530)    /// existing feature on @self the chance to accept @feature_type as
[531](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#531)    /// a "subfeature". This can be used to add new [`Auth`][crate::Auth] types, for instance.
[532](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#532)    ///
[533](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#533)    /// See the main [`Session`][crate::Session] documentation for information on what
[534](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#534)    /// features are present in sessions by default.
[535](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#535)    /// ## `feature_type`

[809](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#809)            from_glib(ffi::soup_session_has_feature(
[810](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#810)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,

[812](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#812)            ))

[816](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#816)    /// Start a preconnection to @msg.
[817](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#817)    ///
[818](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#818)    /// Once the connection is done, it will remain in idle state so that it can be
[819](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#819)    /// reused by future requests. If there's already an idle connection for the
[820](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#820)    /// given @msg host, the operation finishes successfully without creating a new
[821](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#821)    /// connection. If a new request for the given @msg host is made while the
[822](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#822)    /// preconnect is still ongoing, the request will take the ownership of the
[823](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#823)    /// connection and the preconnect operation will finish successfully (if there's
[824](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#824)    /// a connection error it will be handled by the request).
[825](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#825)    ///
[826](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#826)    /// The operation finishes when the connection is done or an error occurred.
[827](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#827)    /// ## `msg`
[828](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#828)    /// a #SoupMessage
[829](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#829)    /// ## `io_priority`
[830](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#830)    /// the I/O priority of the request
[831](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#831)    /// ## `cancellable`
[832](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#832)    /// a #GCancellable
[833](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#833)    /// ## `callback`
[834](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#834)    /// the callback to invoke when the operation finishes
[835](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#835)    #[doc(alias = "soup_session_preconnect_async")]
[836](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#836)    fn preconnect_async<P: FnOnce(Result<(), glib::Error>) + 'static>(
[837](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#837)        &self,
[838](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#838)        msg: &Message,
[839](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#839)        io_priority: glib::Priority,
[840](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#840)        cancellable: Option<&impl IsA<gio::Cancellable>>,
[841](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#841)        callback: P,
[842](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#842)    ) {
[843](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#843)        let main_context = glib::MainContext::ref_thread_default();
[844](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#844)        let is_main_context_owner = main_context.is_owner();
[845](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#845)        let has_acquired_main_context = (!is_main_context_owner)
[846](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#846)            .then(|| main_context.acquire().ok())
[847](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#847)            .flatten();
[848](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#848)        assert!(
[849](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#849)            is_main_context_owner || has_acquired_main_context.is_some(),
[850](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#850)            "Async operations only allowed if the thread is owning the MainContext"
[851](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#851)        );
[852](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#852)
[853](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#853)        let user_data: Box_<glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard<P>> =
[854](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#854)            Box_::new(glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard::new(callback));
[855](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#855)        unsafe extern "C" fn preconnect_async_trampoline<
[856](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#856)            P: FnOnce(Result<(), glib::Error>) + 'static,
[857](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#857)        >(
[858](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#858)            _source_object: *mut glib::gobject_ffi::GObject,
[859](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#859)            res: *mut gio::ffi::GAsyncResult,
[860](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#860)            user_data: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[861](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#861)        ) {
[862](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#862)            unsafe {
[863](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#863)                let mut error = std::ptr::null_mut();
[864](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#864)                ffi::soup_session_preconnect_finish(_source_object as *mut _, res, &mut error);
[865](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#865)                let result = if error.is_null() {
[866](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#866)                    Ok(())
[867](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#867)                } else {
[868](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#868)                    Err(from_glib_full(error))
[869](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#869)                };
[870](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#870)                let callback: Box_<glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard<P>> =
[871](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#871)                    Box_::from_raw(user_data as *mut _);
[872](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#872)                let callback: P = callback.into_inner();
[873](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#873)                callback(result);
[874](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#874)            }
[875](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#875)        }
[876](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#876)        let callback = preconnect_async_trampoline::<P>;
[877](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#877)        unsafe {
[878](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#878)            ffi::soup_session_preconnect_async(
[879](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#879)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[880](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#880)                msg.to_glib_none().0,
[881](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#881)                io_priority.into_glib(),
[882](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#882)                cancellable.map(|p| p.as_ref()).to_glib_none().0,
[883](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#883)                Some(callback),
[884](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#884)                Box_::into_raw(user_data) as *mut _,
[885](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#885)            );
[886](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#886)        }
[887](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#887)    }
[888](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#888)
[889](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#889)    fn preconnect_future(
[890](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#890)        &self,
[891](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#891)        msg: &Message,
[892](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#892)        io_priority: glib::Priority,
[893](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#893)    ) -> Pin<Box_<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<(), glib::Error>> + 'static>> {
[894](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#894)        let msg = msg.clone();
[895](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#895)        Box_::pin(gio::GioFuture::new(self, move |obj, cancellable, send| {
[896](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#896)            obj.preconnect_async(&msg, io_priority, Some(cancellable), move |res| {
[897](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#897)                send.resolve(res);
[898](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#898)            });
[899](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#899)        }))
[900](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#900)    }

[929](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#929)    /// Synchronously sends @msg and waits for the beginning of a response.
[930](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#930)    ///
[931](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#931)    /// On success, a [`gio::InputStream`][crate::gio::InputStream] will be returned which you can use to
[932](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#932)    /// read the response body. ("Success" here means only that an HTTP
[933](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#933)    /// response was received and understood; it does not necessarily mean
[934](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#934)    /// that a 2xx class status code was received.)
[935](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#935)    ///
[936](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#936)    /// If non-[`None`], @cancellable can be used to cancel the request;
[937](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#937)    /// [`send()`][Self::send()] will return a `G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED` error. Note that
[938](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#938)    /// with requests that have side effects (eg, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) it is
[939](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#939)    /// possible that you might cancel the request after the server acts on it, but
[940](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#940)    /// before it returns a response, leaving the remote resource in an unknown
[941](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#941)    /// state.
[942](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#942)    ///
[943](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#943)    /// If @msg is requeued due to a redirect or authentication, the
[944](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#944)    /// initial (`3xx/401/407`) response body will be suppressed, and
[945](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#945)    /// [`send()`][Self::send()] will only return once a final response has been
[946](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#946)    /// received.
[947](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#947)    ///
[948](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#948)    /// Possible error domains include [`SessionError`][crate::SessionError], `Gio::IOErrorEnum`,
[949](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#949)    /// and `Gio::TlsError` which you may want to specifically handle.
[950](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#950)    /// ## `msg`
[951](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#951)    /// a #SoupMessage
[952](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#952)    /// ## `cancellable`
[953](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#953)    /// a #GCancellable
[954](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#954)    ///
[955](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#955)    /// # Returns
[956](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#956)    ///
[957](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#957)    /// a #GInputStream for reading the
[958](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#958)    ///   response body, or [`None`] on error.
[959](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#959)    #[doc(alias = "soup_session_send")]
[960](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#960)    fn send(
[961](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#961)        &self,
[962](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#962)        msg: &Message,
[963](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#963)        cancellable: Option<&impl IsA<gio::Cancellable>>,
[964](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#964)    ) -> Result<gio::InputStream, glib::Error> {
[965](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#965)        unsafe {
[966](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#966)            let mut error = std::ptr::null_mut();
[967](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#967)            let ret = ffi::soup_session_send(
[968](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#968)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[969](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#969)                msg.to_glib_none().0,
[970](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#970)                cancellable.map(|p| p.as_ref()).to_glib_none().0,
[971](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#971)                &mut error,
[972](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#972)            );
[973](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#973)            if error.is_null() {
[974](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#974)                Ok(from_glib_full(ret))
[975](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#975)            } else {
[976](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#976)                Err(from_glib_full(error))
[977](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#977)            }
[978](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#978)        }
[979](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#979)    }
[980](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#980)
[981](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#981)    /// Synchronously sends @msg and reads the response body.
[982](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#982)    ///
[983](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#983)    /// On success, a [`glib::Bytes`][crate::glib::Bytes] will be returned with the response body.
[984](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#984)    /// This function should only be used when the resource to be retrieved
[985](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#985)    /// is not too long and can be stored in memory.
[986](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#986)    ///

[992](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#992)    ///
[993](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#993)    /// # Returns
[994](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#994)    ///
[995](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#995)    /// a #GBytes, or [`None`] on error.
[996](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#996)    #[doc(alias = "soup_session_send_and_read")]
[997](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#997)    fn send_and_read(

[999](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#999)        msg: &Message,

[1006](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1006)                msg.to_glib_none().0,

[1014](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1014)            }
[1015](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1015)        }

[1017](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1017)
[1018](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1018)    /// Asynchronously sends @msg and reads the response body.
[1019](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1019)    ///
[1020](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1020)    /// When @callback is called, then either @msg has been sent, and its response
[1021](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1021)    /// body read, or else an error has occurred. This function should only be used
[1022](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1022)    /// when the resource to be retrieved is not too long and can be stored in
[1023](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1023)    /// memory. Call `Session::send_and_read_finish()` to get a
[1024](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1024)    /// [`glib::Bytes`][crate::glib::Bytes] with the response body.
[1025](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1025)    ///
[1026](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1026)    /// See [`send()`][Self::send()] for more details on the general semantics.
[1027](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1027)    /// ## `msg`
[1028](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1028)    /// a #SoupMessage
[1029](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1029)    /// ## `io_priority`
[1030](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1030)    /// the I/O priority of the request
[1031](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1031)    /// ## `cancellable`
[1032](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1032)    /// a #GCancellable
[1033](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1033)    /// ## `callback`
[1034](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1034)    /// the callback to invoke
[1035](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1035)    #[doc(alias = "soup_session_send_and_read_async")]
[1036](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1036)    fn send_and_read_async<P: FnOnce(Result<glib::Bytes, glib::Error>) + 'static>(
[1037](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1037)        &self,
[1038](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1038)        msg: &Message,
[1039](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1039)        io_priority: glib::Priority,
[1040](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1040)        cancellable: Option<&impl IsA<gio::Cancellable>>,
[1041](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1041)        callback: P,
[1042](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1042)    ) {
[1043](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1043)        let main_context = glib::MainContext::ref_thread_default();
[1044](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1044)        let is_main_context_owner = main_context.is_owner();
[1045](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1045)        let has_acquired_main_context = (!is_main_context_owner)
[1046](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1046)            .then(|| main_context.acquire().ok())
[1047](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1047)            .flatten();
[1048](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1048)        assert!(
[1049](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1049)            is_main_context_owner || has_acquired_main_context.is_some(),
[1050](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1050)            "Async operations only allowed if the thread is owning the MainContext"
[1051](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1051)        );
[1052](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1052)
[1053](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1053)        let user_data: Box_<glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard<P>> =
[1054](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1054)            Box_::new(glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard::new(callback));
[1055](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1055)        unsafe extern "C" fn send_and_read_async_trampoline<
[1056](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1056)            P: FnOnce(Result<glib::Bytes, glib::Error>) + 'static,
[1057](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1057)        >(
[1058](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1058)            _source_object: *mut glib::gobject_ffi::GObject,
[1059](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1059)            res: *mut gio::ffi::GAsyncResult,
[1060](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1060)            user_data: glib::ffi::gpointer,

[1314](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1314)        unsafe {
[1315](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1315)            ffi::soup_session_send_async(
[1316](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1316)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[1317](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1317)                msg.to_glib_none().0,
[1318](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1318)                io_priority.into_glib(),
[1319](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1319)                cancellable.map(|p| p.as_ref()).to_glib_none().0,
[1320](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1320)                Some(callback),
[1321](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1321)                Box_::into_raw(user_data) as *mut _,
[1322](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1322)            );
[1323](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1323)        }
[1324](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1324)    }

[1326](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1326)    fn send_future(
