[1476](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1476)
[1477](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1477)    /// Emitted when a request is queued on @session.
[1478](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1478)    ///
[1479](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1479)    /// When sending a request, first [`request-queued`][struct@crate::Session#request-queued]
[1480](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1480)    /// is emitted, indicating that the session has become aware of
[1481](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1481)    /// the request.
[1482](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1482)    ///
[1483](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1483)    /// After a connection is available to send the request various
[1484](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1484)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message] signals are emitted as the message is
[1485](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1485)    /// processed. If the message is requeued, it will emit
[1486](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1486)    /// [`restarted`][struct@crate::Message#restarted], which will then be followed by other
[1487](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1487)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message] signals when the message is re-sent.
[1488](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1488)    ///
[1489](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1489)    /// Eventually, the message will emit [`finished`][struct@crate::Message#finished].
[1490](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1490)    /// Normally, this signals the completion of message
[1491](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1491)    /// processing. However, it is possible that the application
[1492](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1492)    /// will requeue the message from the "finished" handler.
[1493](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1493)    /// In that case the process will loop back.
[1494](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1494)    ///
[1495](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1495)    /// Eventually, a message will reach "finished" and not be
[1496](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1496)    /// requeued. At that point, the session will emit
[1497](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1497)    /// [`request-unqueued`][struct@crate::Session#request-unqueued] to indicate that it is done
[1498](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1498)    /// with the message.
[1499](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1499)    ///
[1500](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1500)    /// To sum up: [`request-queued`][struct@crate::Session#request-queued] and
[1501](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1501)    /// [`request-unqueued`][struct@crate::Session#request-unqueued] are guaranteed to be emitted
[1502](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1502)    /// exactly once, but [`finished`][struct@crate::Message#finished] (and all of the other
[1503](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1503)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message] signals) may be invoked multiple times for a given
[1504](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1504)    /// message.
[1505](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1505)    /// ## `msg`
[1506](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1506)    /// the request that was queued
[1507](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1507)    #[doc(alias = "request-queued")]
[1508](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1508)    fn connect_request_queued<F: Fn(&Self, &Message) + 'static>(&self, f: F) -> SignalHandlerId {
[1509](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1509)        unsafe extern "C" fn request_queued_trampoline<
[1510](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1510)            P: IsA<Session>,
[1511](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1511)            F: Fn(&P, &Message) + 'static,
[1512](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1512)        >(
[1513](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1513)            this: *mut ffi::SoupSession,
[1514](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1514)            msg: *mut ffi::SoupMessage,
[1515](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1515)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[1516](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1516)        ) {
[1517](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1517)            unsafe {
[1518](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1518)                let f: &F = &*(f as *const F);
[1519](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1519)                f(
[1520](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1520)                    Session::from_glib_borrow(this).unsafe_cast_ref(),
[1521](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1521)                    &from_glib_borrow(msg),
[1522](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1522)                )
[1523](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1523)            }
[1524](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1524)        }
[1525](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1525)        unsafe {
[1526](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1526)            let f: Box_<F> = Box_::new(f);
[1527](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1527)            connect_raw(
[1528](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1528)                self.as_ptr() as *mut _,
[1529](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1529)                c"request-queued".as_ptr(),
[1530](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1530)                Some(std::mem::transmute::<*const (), unsafe extern "C" fn()>(
[1531](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1531)                    request_queued_trampoline::<Self, F> as *const (),
[1532](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1532)                )),
[1533](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1533)                Box_::into_raw(f),
[1534](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1534)            )
[1535](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1535)        }
[1536](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1536)    }

[1538](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1538)    /// Emitted when a request is removed from @session's queue,
[1539](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1539)    /// indicating that @session is done with it.
[1540](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1540)    ///
[1541](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1541)    /// See [`request-queued`][struct@crate::Session#request-queued] for a detailed description of

[1545](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1545)    #[doc(alias = "request-unqueued")]
[1546](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1546)    fn connect_request_unqueued<F: Fn(&Self, &Message) + 'static>(&self, f: F) -> SignalHandlerId {
[1547](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1547)        unsafe extern "C" fn request_unqueued_trampoline<
[1548](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1548)            P: IsA<Session>,
[1549](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1549)            F: Fn(&P, &Message) + 'static,
[1550](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1550)        >(
[1551](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1551)            this: *mut ffi::SoupSession,
[1552](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1552)            msg: *mut ffi::SoupMessage,
[1553](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1553)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[1554](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1554)        ) {

[25](#25)        let has_acquired_main_context = (!is_main_context_owner)
[26](#26)            .then(|| main_context.acquire().ok())
[27](#27)            .flatten();
[28](#28)        assert!(
[29](#29)            is_main_context_owner || has_acquired_main_context.is_some(),
[30](#30)            "Async operations only allowed if the thread is owning the MainContext"
[31](#31)        );
[32](#32)
[33](#33)        let user_data: Box_<glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard<P>> =
[34](#34)            Box_::new(glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard::new(callback));

[49](#49)                let result = if error.is_null() {

[53](#53)                };
[54](#54)                let callback: Box_<glib::thread_guard::ThreadGuard<P>> =
[55](#55)                    Box_::from_raw(user_data as *mut _);
[56](#56)                let callback = callback.into_inner();
[57](#57)                callback(result);
[58](#58)            }
[59](#59)        }
[60](#60)        let callback = websocket_connect_async_trampoline::<P>;

[83](#83)    > {

[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    /// [`HSTSPolicy`][crate::HSTSPolicy] implements HTTP policies, as described by
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    /// [RFC 6797](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6797).
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    ///
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// @domain represents the host that this policy applies to. The domain
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// must be IDNA-canonicalized. `HSTSPolicy::new()` and related methods
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// will do this for you.
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    ///
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// @max_age contains the 'max-age' value from the Strict Transport
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// Security header and indicates the time to live of this policy,
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// in seconds.
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// @expires will be non-[`None`] if the policy has been set by the host and
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// hence has an expiry time. If @expires is [`None`], it indicates that the
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// policy is a permanent session policy set by the user agent.
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    ///
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// If @include_subdomains is [`true`], the Strict Transport Security policy
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// must also be enforced on subdomains of @domain.

[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// Debug logging support
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    ///
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// [`Logger`][crate::Logger] watches a [`Session`][crate::Session] and logs the HTTP traffic that
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// it generates, for debugging purposes. Many applications use an
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// environment variable to determine whether or not to use
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// [`Logger`][crate::Logger], and to determine the amount of debugging output.
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    ///
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// To use [`Logger`][crate::Logger], first create a logger with [`new()`][Self::new()], optionally
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// configure it with [`set_request_filter()`][Self::set_request_filter()],
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// [`set_response_filter()`][Self::set_response_filter()], and [`set_printer()`][Self::set_printer()], and
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// then attach it to a session (or multiple sessions) with
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// [`SessionExt::add_feature()`][crate::prelude::SessionExt::add_feature()].
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    ///
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// By default, the debugging output is sent to `stdout`, and looks something
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// like:
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    ///
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// ```text
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// > POST /unauth HTTP/1.1
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// > Soup-Debug-Timestamp: 1200171744
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// > Soup-Debug: SoupSession 1 (0x612190), SoupMessage 1 (0x617000), GSocket 1 (0x612220)
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// > Host: localhost
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    /// > Content-Type: text/plain
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    /// > Connection: close
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    ///
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    /// < HTTP/1.1 201 Created
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    /// < Soup-Debug-Timestamp: 1200171744
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    /// < Soup-Debug: SoupMessage 1 (0x617000)
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    /// < Date: Sun, 12 Jan 2008 21:02:24 GMT
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    /// < Content-Length: 0
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    /// ```
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    ///
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    /// The `Soup-Debug-Timestamp` line gives the time (as a `time_t`) when the
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    /// request was sent, or the response fully received.
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    ///
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    /// The `Soup-Debug` line gives further debugging information about the
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)    /// [`Session`][crate::Session], [`Message`][crate::Message], and [`gio::Socket`][crate::gio::Socket] involved; the hex
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)    /// numbers are the addresses of the objects in question (which may be useful if
[52](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#52)    /// you are running in a debugger). The decimal IDs are simply counters that
[53](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#53)    /// uniquely identify objects across the lifetime of the [`Logger`][crate::Logger]. In
[54](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#54)    /// particular, this can be used to identify when multiple messages are sent
[55](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#55)    /// across the same connection.
[56](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#56)    ///
[57](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#57)    /// Currently, the request half of the message is logged just before
[58](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#58)    /// the first byte of the request gets written to the network (from the
[59](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#59)    /// [`starting`][struct@crate::Message#starting] signal).
[60](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#60)    ///
[61](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#61)    /// The response is logged just after the last byte of the response body is read
[62](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#62)    /// from the network (from the [`got-body`][struct@crate::Message#got-body] or
[63](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#63)    /// [`got-informational`][struct@crate::Message#got-informational] signal), which means that the
[64](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#64)    /// [`got-headers`][struct@crate::Message#got-headers] signal, and anything triggered off it (such as
[65](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#65)    /// [`authenticate`][struct@crate::Message#authenticate]) will be emitted *before* the response headers are
[66](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#66)    /// actually logged.
[67](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#67)    ///
[68](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#68)    /// If the response doesn't happen to trigger the [`got-body`][struct@crate::Message#got-body] nor
[69](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#69)    /// [`got-informational`][struct@crate::Message#got-informational] signals due to, for example, a
[70](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#70)    /// cancellation before receiving the last byte of the response body, the
[71](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#71)    /// response will still be logged on the event of the [`finished`][struct@crate::Message#finished]
[72](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#72)    /// signal.
[73](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#73)    ///
[74](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#74)    /// ## Properties
[75](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#75)    ///
[76](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#76)    ///
[77](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#77)    /// #### `level`
[78](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#78)    ///  The level of logging output.
[79](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#79)    ///
[80](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#80)    /// Readable | Writeable
[81](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#81)    ///
[82](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#82)    ///
[83](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#83)    /// #### `max-body-size`
[84](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#84)    ///  If [`level`][struct@crate::Logger#level] is [`LoggerLogLevel::Body`][crate::LoggerLogLevel::Body], this gives
[85](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#85)    /// the maximum number of bytes of the body that will be logged.
[86](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#86)    /// (-1 means "no limit".)
[87](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#87)    ///
[88](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#88)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct
[89](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#89)    ///

[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// Represents an HTTP message being sent or received.
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// A [`Message`][crate::Message] represents an HTTP message that is being sent or
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// received.
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    ///
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// You would create a [`Message`][crate::Message] with [`new()`][Self::new()] or
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// [`from_uri()`][Self::from_uri()], set up its fields appropriately, and send it.
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    ///
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// [`status-code`][struct@crate::Message#status-code] will normally be a [`Status`][crate::Status] value, eg,
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// [`Status::Ok`][crate::Status::Ok], though of course it might actually be an unknown status
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// code. [`reason-phrase`][struct@crate::Message#reason-phrase] is the actual text returned from the
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// server, which may or may not correspond to the "standard" description of
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// @status_code. At any rate, it is almost certainly not localized, and not very
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// descriptive even if it is in the user's language; you should not use
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// [`reason-phrase`][struct@crate::Message#reason-phrase] in user-visible messages. Rather, you should
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// look at [`status-code`][struct@crate::Message#status-code], and determine an end-user-appropriate
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// message based on that and on what you were trying to do.
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    ///
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    /// Note that libsoup's terminology here does not quite match the HTTP
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// specification: in RFC 2616, an "HTTP-message" is *either* a Request, *or* a
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    /// Response. In libsoup, a [`Message`][crate::Message] combines both the request and the
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    /// response.
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    ///
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    /// ## Properties
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    ///
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    ///
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    /// #### `first-party`
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    ///  The [`glib::Uri`][crate::glib::Uri] loaded in the application when the message was
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    /// queued.
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    ///
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    /// Readable | Writeable

[160](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#160)    /// ## Signals
[161](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#161)    ///
[162](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#162)    ///
[163](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#163)    /// #### `accept-certificate`
[164](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#164)    ///  Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake
[165](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#165)    /// after an unacceptable TLS certificate has been received.
[166](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#166)    ///
[167](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#167)    /// You can return [`true`] to accept @tls_certificate despite
[168](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#168)    /// @tls_errors.
[169](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#169)    ///
[170](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#170)    ///
[171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#171)    ///
[172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#172)    ///
[173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#173)    /// #### `authenticate`
[174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#174)    ///  Emitted when the message requires authentication.
[175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#175)    ///
[176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#176)    /// If credentials are available call [`AuthExt::authenticate()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::authenticate()] on
[177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#177)    /// @auth. If these credentials fail, the signal will be emitted again,
[178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#178)    /// with @retrying set to [`true`], which will continue until you return
[179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#179)    /// without calling [`AuthExt::authenticate()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::authenticate()] on @auth.
[180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#180)    ///
[181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#181)    /// Note that this may be emitted before @msg's body has been
[182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#182)    /// fully read.
[183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#183)    ///
[184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#184)    /// You can authenticate @auth asynchronously by calling
[185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#185)    /// `GObject::Object::ref()` on @auth and returning [`true`]. The operation will
[186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#186)    /// complete once either [`AuthExt::authenticate()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::authenticate()] or
[187](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#187)    /// [`AuthExt::cancel()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::cancel()] are called.
[188](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#188)    ///
[189](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#189)    ///
[190](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#190)    ///
[191](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#191)    ///
[192](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#192)    /// #### `content-sniffed`
[193](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#193)    ///  This signal is emitted after [`got-headers`][struct@crate::Message#got-headers].
[194](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#194)    ///
[195](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#195)    /// If content sniffing is disabled, or no content sniffing will be
[196](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#196)    /// performed, due to the sniffer deciding to trust the
[197](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#197)    /// Content-Type sent by the server, this signal is emitted
[198](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#198)    /// immediately after [`got-headers`][struct@crate::Message#got-headers], and @type_ is
[199](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#199)    /// [`None`].
[200](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#200)    ///
[201](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#201)    ///
[202](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#202)    ///
[203](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#203)    ///
[204](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#204)    /// #### `finished`
[205](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#205)    ///  Emitted when all HTTP processing is finished for a message.
[206](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#206)    ///
[207](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#207)    /// (After [`got_body`][struct@crate::Message#got_body]).
[208](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#208)    ///
[209](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#209)    ///
[210](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#210)    ///
[211](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#211)    ///
[212](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#212)    /// #### `got-body`
[213](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#213)    ///  Emitted after receiving the complete message response body.
[214](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#214)    ///
[215](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#215)    ///
[216](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#216)    ///
[217](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#217)    ///
[218](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#218)    /// #### `got-body-data`
[219](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#219)    ///  Emitted after reading a portion of the message
[220](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#220)    /// body from the network.
[221](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#221)    ///
[222](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#222)    ///
[223](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#223)    ///
[224](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#224)    ///
[225](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#225)    /// #### `got-headers`
[226](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#226)    ///  Emitted after receiving the Status-Line and response headers.
[227](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#227)    ///
[228](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#228)    /// See also `Message::add_header_handler()` and
[229](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#229)    /// `Message::add_status_code_handler()`, which can be used to
[230](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#230)    /// connect to a subset of emissions of this signal.
[231](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#231)    ///
[232](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#232)    /// If you cancel or requeue @msg while processing this signal,
[233](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#233)    /// then the current HTTP I/O will be stopped after this signal
[234](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#234)    /// emission finished, and @msg's connection will be closed.
[235](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#235)    /// (If you need to requeue a message--eg, after handling
[236](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#236)    /// authentication or redirection--it is usually better to
[237](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#237)    /// requeue it from a [`got-body`][struct@crate::Message#got-body] handler rather
[238](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#238)    /// than a [`got_headers`][struct@crate::Message#got_headers] handler, so that the
[239](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#239)    /// existing HTTP connection can be reused.)
[240](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#240)    ///
[241](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#241)    ///
[242](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#242)    ///
[243](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#243)    ///
[244](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#244)    /// #### `got-informational`
[245](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#245)    ///  Emitted after receiving a 1xx (Informational) response for
[246](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#246)    /// a (client-side) message.
[247](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#247)    ///
[248](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#248)    /// The response_headers will be filled in with the headers associated
[249](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#249)    /// with the informational response; however, those header values will be
[250](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#250)    /// erased after this signal is done.
[251](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#251)    ///
[252](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#252)    /// If you cancel or requeue @msg while processing this signal,
[253](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#253)    /// then the current HTTP I/O will be stopped after this signal
[254](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#254)    /// emission finished, and @msg's connection will be closed.
[255](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#255)    ///
[256](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#256)    ///
[257](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#257)    ///
[258](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#258)    ///
[259](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#259)    /// #### `hsts-enforced`
[260](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#260)    ///  Emitted when [`HSTSEnforcer`][crate::HSTSEnforcer] has upgraded the protocol
[261](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#261)    /// for @msg to HTTPS as a result of matching its domain with
[262](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#262)    /// a HSTS policy.
[263](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#263)    ///
[264](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#264)    ///
[265](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#265)    ///
[266](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#266)    ///
[267](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#267)    /// #### `network-event`
[268](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#268)    ///  Emitted to indicate that some network-related event
[269](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#269)    /// related to @msg has occurred.
[270](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#270)    ///
[271](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#271)    /// This essentially proxies the [`event`][struct@crate::Gio::SocketClient#event] signal,
[272](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#272)    /// but only for events that occur while @msg "owns" the connection; if
[273](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#273)    /// @msg is sent on an existing persistent connection, then this signal
[274](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#274)    /// will not be emitted. (If you want to force the message to be sent on
[275](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#275)    /// a new connection, set the [`MessageFlags::NEW_CONNECTION`][crate::MessageFlags::NEW_CONNECTION] flag on it.)
[276](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#276)    ///
[277](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#277)    /// See [`event`][struct@crate::Gio::SocketClient#event] for more information on what
[278](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#278)    /// the different values of @event correspond to, and what
[279](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#279)    /// @connection will be in each case.
[280](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#280)    ///
[281](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#281)    ///
[282](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#282)    ///
[283](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#283)    ///
[284](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#284)    /// #### `request-certificate`
[285](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#285)    ///  Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake when
[286](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#286)    /// @tls_connection requests a certificate from the client.
[287](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#287)    ///
[288](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#288)    /// You can set the client certificate by calling
[289](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#289)    /// [`Message::set_tls_client_certificate()`][crate::Message::set_tls_client_certificate()] and returning [`true`]. It's
[290](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#290)    /// possible to handle the request asynchornously by returning [`true`] and
[291](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#291)    /// call [`Message::set_tls_client_certificate()`][crate::Message::set_tls_client_certificate()] later once the
[292](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#292)    /// certificate is available. Note that this signal is not emitted if
[293](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#293)    /// [`tls-interaction`][struct@crate::Session#tls-interaction] was set, or if
[294](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#294)    /// [`Message::set_tls_client_certificate()`][crate::Message::set_tls_client_certificate()] was called before the
[295](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#295)    /// connection TLS handshake started.
[296](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#296)    ///
[297](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#297)    ///
[298](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#298)    ///
[299](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#299)    ///
[300](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#300)    /// #### `request-certificate-password`
[301](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#301)    ///  Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake when
[302](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#302)    /// @tls_connection requests a certificate password from the client.
[303](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#303)    ///
[304](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#304)    /// You can set the certificate password on @password, then call
[305](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#305)    /// [`Message::tls_client_certificate_password_request_complete()`][crate::Message::tls_client_certificate_password_request_complete()] and
[306](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#306)    /// return [`true`] to handle the signal synchronously. It's possible to
[307](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#307)    /// handle the request asynchornously by calling
[308](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#308)    /// `GObject::Object::ref()` on @password, then returning [`true`] and
[309](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#309)    /// call
[310](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#310)    /// [`Message::tls_client_certificate_password_request_complete()`][crate::Message::tls_client_certificate_password_request_complete()]
[311](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#311)    /// later after setting the password on @password. Note that this signal
[312](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#312)    /// is not emitted if [`tls-interaction`][struct@crate::Session#tls-interaction] was set.
[313](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#313)    ///
[314](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#314)    ///
[315](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#315)    ///
[316](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#316)    ///
[317](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#317)    /// #### `restarted`
[318](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#318)    ///  Emitted when a request that was already sent once is now
[319](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#319)    /// being sent again.
[320](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#320)    ///
[321](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#321)    /// e.g. because the first attempt received a
[322](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#322)    /// redirection response, or because we needed to use
[323](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#323)    /// authentication.
[324](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#324)    ///
[325](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#325)    ///
[326](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#326)    ///
[327](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#327)    ///
[328](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#328)    /// #### `starting`
[329](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#329)    ///  Emitted just before a message is sent.
[330](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#330)    ///
[331](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#331)    ///
[332](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#332)    ///
[333](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#333)    ///
[334](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#334)    /// #### `wrote-body`
[335](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#335)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing the complete body for a
[336](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#336)    /// message.
[337](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#337)    ///
[338](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#338)    ///
[339](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#339)    ///
[340](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#340)    ///
[341](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#341)    /// #### `wrote-body-data`
[342](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#342)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing a portion of the message

[344](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#344)    ///
[345](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#345)    ///

[366](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#366)    /// Creates a new empty [`Message`][crate::Message], which will connect to @uri.
[367](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#367)    /// ## `method`
[368](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#368)    /// the HTTP method for the created request
[369](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#369)    /// ## `uri_string`
[370](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#370)    /// the destination endpoint (as a string)
[371](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#371)    ///
[372](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#372)    /// # Returns
[373](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#373)    ///
[374](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#374)    /// the new #SoupMessage (or [`None`] if @uri
[375](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#375)    ///   could not be parsed).
[376](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#376)    #[doc(alias = "soup_message_new")]
[377](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#377)    pub fn new(method: &str, uri_string: &str) -> Result<Message, glib::BoolError> {
[378](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#378)        assert_initialized_main_thread!();
[379](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#379)        unsafe {
[380](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#380)            Option::<_>::from_glib_full(ffi::soup_message_new(
[381](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#381)                method.to_glib_none().0,
[382](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#382)                uri_string.to_glib_none().0,
[383](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#383)            ))
[384](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#384)            .ok_or_else(|| glib::bool_error!("Invalid URL"))
[385](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#385)        }
[386](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#386)    }
[387](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#387)
[388](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#388)    /// Creates a new [`Message`][crate::Message] and sets it up to send the given @encoded_form
[389](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#389)    /// to @uri via @method. If @method is "GET", it will include the form data
[390](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#390)    /// into @uri's query field, and if @method is "POST" or "PUT", it will be set as
[391](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#391)    /// request body.
[392](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#392)    ///
[393](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#393)    /// This function takes the ownership of @encoded_form, that will be released
[394](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#394)    /// with `free()` when no longer in use. See also `form_encode()`,
[395](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#395)    /// `form_encode_hash()` and `form_encode_datalist()`.
[396](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#396)    /// ## `method`
[397](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#397)    /// the HTTP method for the created request (GET, POST or PUT)
[398](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#398)    /// ## `uri_string`
[399](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#399)    /// the destination endpoint (as a string)
[400](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#400)    /// ## `encoded_form`
[401](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#401)    /// a encoded form
[402](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#402)    ///
[403](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#403)    /// # Returns
[404](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#404)    ///
[405](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#405)    /// the new #SoupMessage, or [`None`] if
[406](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#406)    ///   @uri_string could not be parsed or @method is not "GET, "POST" or "PUT"
[407](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#407)    #[doc(alias = "soup_message_new_from_encoded_form")]
[408](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#408)    #[doc(alias = "new_from_encoded_form")]
[409](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#409)    pub fn from_encoded_form(
[410](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#410)        method: &str,
[411](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#411)        uri_string: &str,
[412](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#412)        encoded_form: glib::GString,
[413](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#413)    ) -> Result<Message, glib::BoolError> {
[414](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#414)        assert_initialized_main_thread!();
[415](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#415)        unsafe {

[521](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#521)    ///
[522](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#522)    /// @self is processed as though the feature(s) hadn't been added to the
[523](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#523)    /// session. Eg, passing #SOUP_TYPE_CONTENT_SNIFFER for @feature_type

[526](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#526)    /// You must call this before queueing @self on a session; calling it on
[527](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#527)    /// a message that has already been queued is undefined. In particular,
[528](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#528)    /// you cannot call this on a message that is being requeued after a
[529](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#529)    /// redirect or authentication.
[530](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#530)    /// ## `feature_type`

[535](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#535)            ffi::soup_message_disable_feature(self.to_glib_none().0, feature_type.into_glib());

[537](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#537)    }

[984](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#984)    /// semi-randomly by thread scheduling.

[1113](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1113)    /// Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake
[1114](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1114)    /// after an unacceptable TLS certificate has been received.
[1115](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1115)    ///
[1116](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1116)    /// You can return [`true`] to accept @tls_certificate despite
[1117](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1117)    /// @tls_errors.
[1118](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1118)    /// ## `tls_peer_certificate`

[1120](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1120)    /// ## `tls_peer_errors`
[1121](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1121)    /// the tls errors of @tls_certificate
[1122](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1122)    ///
[1123](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1123)    /// # Returns
[1124](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1124)    ///
[1125](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1125)    /// [`true`] to accept the TLS certificate and stop other
[1126](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1126)    ///   handlers from being invoked, or [`false`] to propagate the
[1127](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1127)    ///   event further.
[1128](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1128)    #[doc(alias = "accept-certificate")]
[1129](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1129)    pub fn connect_accept_certificate<
[1130](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1130)        F: Fn(&Self, &gio::TlsCertificate, gio::TlsCertificateFlags) -> bool + 'static,
[1131](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1131)    >(
[1132](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1132)        &self,
[1133](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1133)        f: F,
[1134](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1134)    ) -> SignalHandlerId {
[1135](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1135)        unsafe extern "C" fn accept_certificate_trampoline<
[1136](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1136)            F: Fn(&Message, &gio::TlsCertificate, gio::TlsCertificateFlags) -> bool + 'static,
[1137](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1137)        >(
[1138](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1138)            this: *mut ffi::SoupMessage,
[1139](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1139)            tls_peer_certificate: *mut gio::ffi::GTlsCertificate,
[1140](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1140)            tls_peer_errors: gio::ffi::GTlsCertificateFlags,
[1141](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1141)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[1142](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1142)        ) -> glib::ffi::gboolean {
[1143](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1143)            unsafe {
[1144](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1144)                let f: &F = &*(f as *const F);
[1145](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1145)                f(
[1146](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1146)                    &from_glib_borrow(this),
[1147](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1147)                    &from_glib_borrow(tls_peer_certificate),
[1148](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1148)                    from_glib(tls_peer_errors),
[1149](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1149)                )
[1150](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1150)                .into_glib()
[1151](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1151)            }
[1152](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1152)        }
[1153](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1153)        unsafe {
[1154](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1154)            let f: Box_<F> = Box_::new(f);
[1155](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1155)            connect_raw(
[1156](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1156)                self.as_ptr() as *mut _,
[1157](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1157)                c"accept-certificate".as_ptr(),
[1158](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1158)                Some(std::mem::transmute::<*const (), unsafe extern "C" fn()>(
[1159](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1159)                    accept_certificate_trampoline::<F> as *const (),
[1160](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1160)                )),
[1161](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1161)                Box_::into_raw(f),
[1162](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1162)            )
[1163](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1163)        }
[1164](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1164)    }
[1165](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1165)
[1166](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1166)    /// Emitted when the message requires authentication.
[1167](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1167)    ///
[1168](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1168)    /// If credentials are available call [`AuthExt::authenticate()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::authenticate()] on
[1169](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1169)    /// @auth. If these credentials fail, the signal will be emitted again,
[1170](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1170)    /// with @retrying set to [`true`], which will continue until you return
[1171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1171)    /// without calling [`AuthExt::authenticate()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::authenticate()] on @auth.
[1172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1172)    ///
[1173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1173)    /// Note that this may be emitted before @msg's body has been
[1174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1174)    /// fully read.
[1175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1175)    ///
[1176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1176)    /// You can authenticate @auth asynchronously by calling
[1177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1177)    /// `GObject::Object::ref()` on @auth and returning [`true`]. The operation will
[1178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1178)    /// complete once either [`AuthExt::authenticate()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::authenticate()] or
[1179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1179)    /// [`AuthExt::cancel()`][crate::prelude::AuthExt::cancel()] are called.
[1180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1180)    /// ## `auth`
[1181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1181)    /// the #SoupAuth to authenticate
[1182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1182)    /// ## `retrying`
[1183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1183)    /// [`true`] if this is the second (or later) attempt
[1184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1184)    ///
[1185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1185)    /// # Returns
[1186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1186)    ///

[1463](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1463)    /// Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake when

[1465](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1465)    ///
[1466](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1466)    /// You can set the client certificate by calling
[1467](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1467)    /// [`set_tls_client_certificate()`][Self::set_tls_client_certificate()] and returning [`true`]. It's
[1468](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1468)    /// possible to handle the request asynchornously by returning [`true`] and
[1469](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1469)    /// call [`set_tls_client_certificate()`][Self::set_tls_client_certificate()] later once the
[1470](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1470)    /// certificate is available. Note that this signal is not emitted if
[1471](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1471)    /// [`tls-interaction`][struct@crate::Session#tls-interaction] was set, or if

[1478](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1478)    ///
[1479](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1479)    /// [`true`] to handle the request, or [`false`] to make the connection
[1480](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1480)    ///   fail with `G_TLS_ERROR_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED`.

[2171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2171)/// A [builder-pattern] type to construct [`Message`] objects.
[2172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2172)///
[2173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2173)/// [builder-pattern]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.0.0/style/ownership/builders.html
[2174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2174)#[must_use = "The builder must be built to be used"]
[2175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2175)pub struct MessageBuilder {
[2176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2176)    builder: glib::object::ObjectBuilder<'static, Message>,
[2177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2177)}

[2179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2179)impl MessageBuilder {

[2182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2182)            builder: glib::object::Object::builder(),

[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    /// [`Message`][crate::Message].
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    ///
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// Note that while @length always reflects the full length of the
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// message body, @data is normally [`None`], and will only be filled in
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// after [`flatten()`][Self::flatten()] is called. For client-side
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// messages, this automatically happens for the response body after it
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// has been fully read. Likewise, for server-side
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// messages, the request body is automatically filled in after being
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// read.
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///

[232](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#232)    /// Gets the value of header @name in @self.

[234](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#234)    /// Use this for headers whose values are comma-delimited lists, and which are
[235](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#235)    /// therefore allowed to appear multiple times in the headers. For
[236](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#236)    /// non-list-valued headers, use [`one()`][Self::one()].
[237](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#237)    ///
[238](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#238)    /// If @name appears multiple times in @self,
[239](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#239)    /// [`list()`][Self::list()] will concatenate all of the values
[240](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#240)    /// together, separated by commas. This is sometimes awkward to parse
[241](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#241)    /// (eg, WWW-Authenticate, Set-Cookie), but you have to be able to deal
[242](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#242)    /// with it anyway, because the HTTP spec explicitly states that this
[243](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#243)    /// transformation is allowed, and so an upstream proxy could do the
[244](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#244)    /// same thing.
[245](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#245)    /// ## `name`
[246](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#246)    /// header name
[247](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#247)    ///

[1](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1)use glib::translate::*;
[2](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#2)use glib::{GString, IntoGStr, IntoOptionalGStr};

[7](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#7)
[8](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#8)impl MessageHeaders {
[9](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#9)    /// Looks up the "Content-Disposition" header in @self, parses it, and
[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    /// returns its value in *@disposition and *@params.
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    ///
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    /// @params can be [`None`] if you are only interested in the disposition-type.
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    ///
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// In HTTP, the most common use of this header is to set a
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// disposition-type of "attachment", to suggest to the browser that a
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// response should be saved to disk rather than displayed in the
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// browser. If @params contains a "filename" parameter, this is a
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// suggestion of a filename to use. (If the parameter value in the
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// header contains an absolute or relative path, libsoup will truncate
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// it down to just the final path component, so you do not need to
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// test this yourself.)
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    ///
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// Content-Disposition is also used in "multipart/form-data", however
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// this is handled automatically by [`Multipart`][crate::Multipart] and the associated
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// form methods.
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    ///
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// # Returns
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    ///
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// [`true`] if @self contains a "Content-Disposition"
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    ///   header, [`false`] if not (in which case *@disposition and *@params
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    ///   will be unchanged).
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    ///
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// ## `disposition`
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// return location for the
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    ///   disposition-type, or [`None`]
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    ///
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    /// ## `params`
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// return
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    ///   location for the Content-Disposition parameters, or [`None`]
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    #[doc(alias = "soup_message_headers_get_content_disposition")]
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    pub fn content_disposition(&self) -> Option<(GString, HashMap<String, String>)> {
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)        let mut disposition = ptr::null_mut();
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)        let mut params = ptr::null_mut();
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)        unsafe {
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)            if bool::from_glib(ffi::soup_message_headers_get_content_disposition(
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)                mut_override(self.to_glib_none().0),
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)                &mut disposition,

[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    /// Contains metrics collected while loading a [`Message`][crate::Message] either from the
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    /// network or the disk cache.
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    ///
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// Metrics are not collected by default for a [`Message`][crate::Message], you need to add the
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// flag [`MessageFlags::COLLECT_METRICS`][crate::MessageFlags::COLLECT_METRICS] to enable the feature.
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    ///
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// Temporal metrics are expressed as a monotonic time and always start with a
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// fetch start event and finish with response end. All other events are optional.
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// An event can be 0 because it hasn't happened yet, because it's optional or
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// because the load failed before the event reached.
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// Size metrics are expressed in bytes and are updated while the [`Message`][crate::Message] is
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// being loaded. You can connect to different [`Message`][crate::Message] signals to get the
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// final result of every value.

[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    /// Represents a multipart HTTP message body, parsed according to the
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    /// syntax of RFC 2046.
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    ///
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// Of particular interest to HTTP are `multipart/byte-ranges` and
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// `multipart/form-data`,
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    ///
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// Although the headers of a [`Multipart`][crate::Multipart] body part will contain the
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// full headers from that body part, libsoup does not interpret them
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// according to MIME rules. For example, each body part is assumed to
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// have "binary" Content-Transfer-Encoding, even if its headers
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// explicitly state otherwise. In other words, don't try to use
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// [`Multipart`][crate::Multipart] for handling real MIME multiparts.
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    pub struct Multipart(Boxed<ffi::SoupMultipart>);
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)

[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)        free => |ptr| glib::gobject_ffi::g_boxed_free(ffi::soup_multipart_get_type(), ptr as *mut _),
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)        type_ => || ffi::soup_multipart_get_type(),
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    }

[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)    /// Handles streams of multipart messages.
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)    ///
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    /// This adds support for the multipart responses. For handling the
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    /// multiple parts the user needs to wrap the [`gio::InputStream`][crate::gio::InputStream] obtained by
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// sending the request with a [`MultipartInputStream`][crate::MultipartInputStream] and use
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// [`next_part()`][Self::next_part()] before reading. Responses
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// which are not wrapped will be treated like non-multipart responses.
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    ///
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// Note that although [`MultipartInputStream`][crate::MultipartInputStream] is a [`gio::InputStream`][crate::gio::InputStream],
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// you should not read directly from it, and the results are undefined
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// if you do.

[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server] provides a basic implementation of an HTTP server. The
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// recommended usage of this server is for internal use, tasks like
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// a mock server for tests, a private service for IPC, etc. It is not
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// recommended to be exposed to untrusted clients as it may be vulnerable
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// to denial of service attacks or other exploits.
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    ///
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// To begin, create a server using `Server::new()`. Add at least one
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// handler by calling [`ServerExtManual::add_handler()`][crate::prelude::ServerExtManual::add_handler()] or
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// [`ServerExtManual::add_early_handler()`][crate::prelude::ServerExtManual::add_early_handler()]; the handler will be called to
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// process any requests underneath the path you pass. (If you want all
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// requests to go to the same handler, just pass "/" (or [`None`]) for
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// the path.)
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    ///
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// When a new connection is accepted (or a new request is started on
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    /// an existing persistent connection), the [`Server`][crate::Server] will emit
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// [`request-started`][struct@crate::Server#request-started] and then begin processing the request
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// as described below, but note that once the message is assigned a
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// status-code, then callbacks after that point will be
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// skipped. Note also that it is not defined when the callbacks happen
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    /// relative to various [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage] signals.
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    ///
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// Once the headers have been read, [`Server`][crate::Server] will check if there is
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    /// a [`AuthDomain`][crate::AuthDomain] `(qv)` covering the Request-URI; if so, and if the
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    /// message does not contain suitable authorization, then the
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    /// [`AuthDomain`][crate::AuthDomain] will set a status of [`Status::Unauthorized`][crate::Status::Unauthorized] on
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    /// the message.
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    ///
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    /// After checking for authorization, [`Server`][crate::Server] will look for "early"
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    /// handlers (added with [`ServerExtManual::add_early_handler()`][crate::prelude::ServerExtManual::add_early_handler()]) matching the
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    /// Request-URI. If one is found, it will be run; in particular, this
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    /// can be used to connect to signals to do a streaming read of the
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    /// request body.
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    ///
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)    /// (At this point, if the request headers contain `Expect:
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)    /// 100-continue`, and a status code has been set, then
[52](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#52)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server] will skip the remaining steps and return the response.
[53](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#53)    /// If the request headers contain `Expect:
[54](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#54)    /// 100-continue` and no status code has been set,
[55](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#55)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server] will return a [`Status::Continue`][crate::Status::Continue] status before
[56](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#56)    /// continuing.)
[57](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#57)    ///
[58](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#58)    /// The server will then read in the response body (if present). At
[59](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#59)    /// this point, if there are no handlers at all defined for the
[60](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#60)    /// Request-URI, then the server will return [`Status::NotFound`][crate::Status::NotFound] to
[61](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#61)    /// the client.
[62](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#62)    ///
[63](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#63)    /// Otherwise (assuming no previous step assigned a status to the
[64](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#64)    /// message) any "normal" handlers (added with
[65](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#65)    /// [`ServerExtManual::add_handler()`][crate::prelude::ServerExtManual::add_handler()]) for the message's Request-URI will be
[66](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#66)    /// run.
[67](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#67)    ///
[68](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#68)    /// Then, if the path has a WebSocket handler registered (and has
[69](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#69)    /// not yet been assigned a status), [`Server`][crate::Server] will attempt to
[70](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#70)    /// validate the WebSocket handshake, filling in the response and
[71](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#71)    /// setting a status of [`Status::SwitchingProtocols`][crate::Status::SwitchingProtocols] or
[72](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#72)    /// [`Status::BadRequest`][crate::Status::BadRequest] accordingly.
[73](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#73)    ///
[74](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#74)    /// If the message still has no status code at this point (and has not
[75](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#75)    /// been paused with [`ServerMessage::pause()`][crate::ServerMessage::pause()]), then it will be
[76](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#76)    /// given a status of [`Status::InternalServerError`][crate::Status::InternalServerError] (because at
[77](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#77)    /// least one handler ran, but returned without assigning a status).
[78](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#78)    ///
[79](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#79)    /// Finally, the server will emit [`request-finished`][struct@crate::Server#request-finished] (or
[80](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#80)    /// [`request-aborted`][struct@crate::Server#request-aborted] if an I/O error occurred before
[81](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#81)    /// handling was completed).
[82](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#82)    ///
[83](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#83)    /// If you want to handle the special "*" URI (eg, "OPTIONS *"), you
[84](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#84)    /// must explicitly register a handler for "*"; the default handler
[85](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#85)    /// will not be used for that case.
[86](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#86)    ///
[87](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#87)    /// If you want to process https connections in addition to (or instead
[88](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#88)    /// of) http connections, you can set the [`tls-certificate`][struct@crate::Server#tls-certificate]
[89](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#89)    /// property.
[90](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#90)    ///
[91](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#91)    /// Once the server is set up, make one or more calls to
[92](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#92)    /// [`ServerExt::listen()`][crate::prelude::ServerExt::listen()], [`ServerExt::listen_local()`][crate::prelude::ServerExt::listen_local()], or
[93](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#93)    /// [`ServerExt::listen_all()`][crate::prelude::ServerExt::listen_all()] to tell it where to listen for
[94](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#94)    /// connections. (All ports on a [`Server`][crate::Server] use the same handlers; if
[95](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#95)    /// you need to handle some ports differently, such as returning
[96](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#96)    /// different data for http and https, you'll need to create multiple
[97](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#97)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server]s, or else check the passed-in URI in the handler
[98](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#98)    /// function.).
[99](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#99)    ///
[100](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#100)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server] will begin processing connections as soon as you return
[101](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#101)    /// to (or start) the main loop for the current thread-default
[102](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#102)    /// [`glib::MainContext`][crate::glib::MainContext].
[103](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#103)    ///
[104](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#104)    /// ## Properties
[105](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#105)    ///
[106](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#106)    ///
[107](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#107)    /// #### `raw-paths`
[108](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#108)    ///  If [`true`], percent-encoding in the Request-URI path will not be
[109](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#109)    /// automatically decoded.
[110](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#110)    ///

[114](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#114)    /// #### `server-header`
[115](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#115)    ///  Server header.
[116](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#116)    ///
[117](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#117)    /// If non-[`None`], the value to use for the "Server" header on
[118](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#118)    /// [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage]s processed by this server.
[119](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#119)    ///
[120](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#120)    /// The Server header is the server equivalent of the
[121](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#121)    /// User-Agent header, and provides information about the
[122](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#122)    /// server and its components. It contains a list of one or
[123](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#123)    /// more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most
[124](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#124)    /// significant product token coming first. The tokens must be
[125](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#125)    /// brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although "-", "_",
[126](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#126)    /// and "." are also allowed), and may optionally include a "/"
[127](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#127)    /// followed by a version string. You may also put comments,
[128](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#128)    /// enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.
[129](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#129)    ///
[130](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#130)    /// Some HTTP server implementations intentionally do not use
[131](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#131)    /// version numbers in their Server header, so that
[132](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#132)    /// installations running older versions of the server don't
[133](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#133)    /// end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security
[134](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#134)    /// holes.
[135](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#135)    ///
[136](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#136)    /// As with [`user_agent`][struct@crate::Session#user_agent], if you set a
[137](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#137)    /// [`server-header`][struct@crate::Server#server-header] property that has trailing
[138](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#138)    /// whitespace, [`Server`][crate::Server] will append its own product token (eg,
[139](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#139)    /// `libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the header for you.
[140](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#140)    ///
[141](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#141)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct
[142](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#142)    ///
[143](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#143)    ///
[144](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#144)    /// #### `tls-auth-mode`
[145](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#145)    ///  A [`gio::TlsAuthenticationMode`][crate::gio::TlsAuthenticationMode] for SSL/TLS client authentication.
[146](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#146)    ///

[152](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#152)    /// [`private-key`][struct@crate::gio::TlsCertificate#private-key] set.

[156](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#156)    ///

[158](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#158)    ///

[160](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#160)    /// #### `tls-database`
[161](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#161)    ///  A [`gio::TlsDatabase`][crate::gio::TlsDatabase] to use for validating SSL/TLS client
[162](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#162)    /// certificates.
[163](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#163)    ///
[164](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#164)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct
[165](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#165)    ///
[166](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#166)    /// ## Signals
[167](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#167)    ///
[168](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#168)    ///
[169](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#169)    /// #### `request-aborted`
[170](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#170)    ///  Emitted when processing has failed for a message.
[171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#171)    ///
[172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#172)    /// This could mean either that it could not be read (if
[173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#173)    /// [`request-read`][struct@crate::Server#request-read] has not been emitted for it yet), or that
[174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#174)    /// the response could not be written back (if [`request-read`][struct@crate::Server#request-read]
[175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#175)    /// has been emitted but [`request-finished`][struct@crate::Server#request-finished] has not been).
[176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#176)    ///
[177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#177)    /// @message is in an undefined state when this signal is
[178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#178)    /// emitted; the signal exists primarily to allow the server to
[179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#179)    /// free any state that it may have allocated in
[180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#180)    /// [`request-started`][struct@crate::Server#request-started].
[181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#181)    ///
[182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#182)    ///
[183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#183)    ///
[184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#184)    ///
[185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#185)    /// #### `request-finished`
[186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#186)    ///  Emitted when the server has finished writing a response to
[187](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#187)    /// a request.
[188](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#188)    ///
[189](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#189)    ///
[190](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#190)    ///
[191](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#191)    ///
[192](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#192)    /// #### `request-read`
[193](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#193)    ///  Emitted when the server has successfully read a request.
[194](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#194)    ///
[195](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#195)    /// @message will have all of its request-side information
[196](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#196)    /// filled in, and if the message was authenticated, @client
[197](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#197)    /// will have information about that. This signal is emitted
[198](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#198)    /// before any (non-early) handlers are called for the message,
[199](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#199)    /// and if it sets the message's #status_code, then normal
[200](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#200)    /// handler processing will be skipped.
[201](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#201)    ///
[202](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#202)    ///
[203](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#203)    ///
[204](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#204)    ///
[205](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#205)    /// #### `request-started`
[206](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#206)    ///  Emitted when the server has started reading a new request.
[207](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#207)    ///
[208](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#208)    /// @message will be completely blank; not even the
[209](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#209)    /// Request-Line will have been read yet. About the only thing
[210](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#210)    /// you can usefully do with it is connect to its signals.
[211](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#211)    ///
[212](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#212)    /// If the request is read successfully, this will eventually
[213](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#213)    /// be followed by a [`request_read`][struct@crate::Server#request_read] signal]. If a
