[273](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#273)    /// Server header.
[274](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#274)    ///
[275](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#275)    /// If non-[`None`], the value to use for the "Server" header on
[276](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#276)    /// [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage]s processed by this server.
[277](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#277)    ///
[278](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#278)    /// The Server header is the server equivalent of the
[279](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#279)    /// User-Agent header, and provides information about the
[280](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#280)    /// server and its components. It contains a list of one or
[281](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#281)    /// more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most
[282](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#282)    /// significant product token coming first. The tokens must be
[283](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#283)    /// brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although "-", "_",
[284](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#284)    /// and "." are also allowed), and may optionally include a "/"
[285](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#285)    /// followed by a version string. You may also put comments,
[286](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#286)    /// enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.
[287](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#287)    ///
[288](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#288)    /// Some HTTP server implementations intentionally do not use
[289](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#289)    /// version numbers in their Server header, so that
[290](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#290)    /// installations running older versions of the server don't
[291](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#291)    /// end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security
[292](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#292)    /// holes.
[293](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#293)    ///
[294](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#294)    /// As with [`user_agent`][struct@crate::Session#user_agent], if you set a
[295](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#295)    /// [`server-header`][struct@crate::Server#server-header] property that has trailing
[296](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#296)    /// whitespace, [`Server`][crate::Server] will append its own product token (eg,
[297](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#297)    /// `libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the header for you.
[298](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#298)    pub fn server_header(self, server_header: impl Into<glib::GString>) -> Self {
[299](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#299)        Self {
[300](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#300)            builder: self.builder.property("server-header", server_header.into()),
[301](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#301)        }
[302](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#302)    }
[303](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#303)
[304](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#304)    /// A [`gio::TlsAuthenticationMode`][crate::gio::TlsAuthenticationMode] for SSL/TLS client authentication.

[349](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#349)    /// Adds a new client stream to the @self.
[350](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#350)    /// ## `stream`
[351](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#351)    /// a #GIOStream
[352](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#352)    /// ## `local_addr`
[353](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#353)    /// the local #GSocketAddress associated with the

[358](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#358)    ///
[359](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#359)    /// # Returns
[360](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#360)    ///
[361](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#361)    /// [`true`] on success, [`false`] if the stream could not be
[362](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#362)    ///   accepted or any other error occurred (in which case @error will be
[363](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#363)    ///   set).
[364](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#364)    #[doc(alias = "soup_server_accept_iostream")]
[365](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#365)    fn accept_iostream(
[366](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#366)        &self,
[367](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#367)        stream: &impl IsA<gio::IOStream>,
[368](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#368)        local_addr: Option<&impl IsA<gio::SocketAddress>>,
[369](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#369)        remote_addr: Option<&impl IsA<gio::SocketAddress>>,
[370](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#370)    ) -> Result<(), glib::Error> {
[371](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#371)        unsafe {
[372](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#372)            let mut error = std::ptr::null_mut();
[373](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#373)            let is_ok = ffi::soup_server_accept_iostream(
[374](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#374)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[375](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#375)                stream.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[376](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#376)                local_addr.map(|p| p.as_ref()).to_glib_none().0,
[377](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#377)                remote_addr.map(|p| p.as_ref()).to_glib_none().0,
[378](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#378)                &mut error,
[379](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#379)            );
[380](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#380)            debug_assert_eq!(is_ok == glib::ffi::GFALSE, !error.is_null());
[381](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#381)            if error.is_null() {
[382](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#382)                Ok(())
[383](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#383)            } else {
[384](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#384)                Err(from_glib_full(error))
[385](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#385)            }
[386](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#386)        }
[387](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#387)    }

[389](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#389)    /// Adds an authentication domain to @self.
[390](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#390)    ///
[391](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#391)    /// Each auth domain will have the chance to require authentication for each
[392](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#392)    /// request that comes in; normally auth domains will require authentication for
[393](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#393)    /// requests on certain paths that they have been set up to watch, or that meet
[394](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#394)    /// other criteria set by the caller. If an auth domain determines that a request
[395](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#395)    /// requires authentication (and the request doesn't contain authentication),
[396](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#396)    /// @self will automatically reject the request with an appropriate status (401
[397](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#397)    /// Unauthorized or 407 Proxy Authentication Required). If the request used the
[398](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#398)    /// SoupServer:100-continue Expectation, @self will reject it before the
[399](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#399)    /// request body is sent.

[538](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#538)    /// Checks whether @self is capable of https.
[539](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#539)    ///
[540](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#540)    /// In order for a server to run https, you must call
[541](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#541)    /// [`set_tls_certificate()`][Self::set_tls_certificate()], or set the
[542](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#542)    /// [`tls-certificate`][struct@crate::Server#tls-certificate] property, to provide it with a
[543](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#543)    /// certificate to use.
[544](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#544)    ///
[545](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#545)    /// If you are using the deprecated single-listener APIs, then a return value of
[546](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#546)    /// [`true`] indicates that the [`Server`][crate::Server] serves https exclusively. If you are
[547](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#547)    /// using [`listen()`][Self::listen()], etc, then a [`true`] return value merely indicates
[548](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#548)    /// that the server is *able* to do https, regardless of whether it actually
[549](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#549)    /// currently is or not. Use [`uris()`][Self::uris()] to see if it currently has
[550](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#550)    /// any https listeners.
[551](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#551)    ///
[552](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#552)    /// # Returns
[553](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#553)    ///
[554](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#554)    /// [`true`] if @self is configured to serve https.
[555](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#555)    #[doc(alias = "soup_server_is_https")]
[556](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#556)    fn is_https(&self) -> bool {
[557](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#557)        unsafe { from_glib(ffi::soup_server_is_https(self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0)) }
[558](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#558)    }
[559](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#559)
[560](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#560)    /// Attempts to set up @self to listen for connections on @address.
[561](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#561)    ///
[562](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#562)    /// If @options includes [`ServerListenOptions::HTTPS`][crate::ServerListenOptions::HTTPS], and @self has
[563](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#563)    /// been configured for TLS, then @self will listen for https
[564](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#564)    /// connections on this port. Otherwise it will listen for plain http.
[565](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#565)    ///
[566](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#566)    /// You may call this method (along with the other "listen" methods)
[567](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#567)    /// any number of times on a server, if you want to listen on multiple
[568](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#568)    /// ports, or set up both http and https service.
[569](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#569)    ///
[570](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#570)    /// After calling this method, @self will begin accepting and processing
[571](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#571)    /// connections as soon as the appropriate [`glib::MainContext`][crate::glib::MainContext] is run.
[572](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#572)    ///
[573](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#573)    /// Note that this API does not make use of dual IPv4/IPv6 sockets; if
[574](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#574)    /// @address is an IPv6 address, it will only accept IPv6 connections.
[575](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#575)    /// You must configure IPv4 listening separately.
[576](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#576)    /// ## `address`
[577](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#577)    /// the address of the interface to listen on
[578](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#578)    /// ## `options`
[579](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#579)    /// listening options for this server
[580](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#580)    ///
[581](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#581)    /// # Returns
[582](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#582)    ///
[583](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#583)    /// [`true`] on success, [`false`] if @address could not be
[584](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#584)    ///   bound or any other error occurred (in which case @error will be
[585](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#585)    ///   set).
[586](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#586)    #[doc(alias = "soup_server_listen")]
[587](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#587)    fn listen(
[588](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#588)        &self,
[589](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#589)        address: &impl IsA<gio::SocketAddress>,
[590](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#590)        options: ServerListenOptions,
[591](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#591)    ) -> Result<(), glib::Error> {
[592](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#592)        unsafe {
[593](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#593)            let mut error = std::ptr::null_mut();
[594](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#594)            let is_ok = ffi::soup_server_listen(
[595](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#595)                self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[596](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#596)                address.as_ref().to_glib_none().0,
[597](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#597)                options.into_glib(),
[598](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#598)                &mut error,
[599](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#599)            );
[600](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#600)            debug_assert_eq!(is_ok == glib::ffi::GFALSE, !error.is_null());
[601](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#601)            if error.is_null() {
[602](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#602)                Ok(())
[603](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#603)            } else {
[604](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#604)                Err(from_glib_full(error))
[605](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#605)            }
[606](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#606)        }
[607](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#607)    }
[608](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#608)
[609](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#609)    /// Attempts to set up @self to listen for connections on all interfaces

[617](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#617)    /// what port it ended up choosing.

[622](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#622)    /// ## `options`
[623](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#623)    /// listening options for this server
[624](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#624)    ///
[625](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#625)    /// # Returns
[626](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#626)    ///
[627](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#627)    /// [`true`] on success, [`false`] if @port could not be bound
[628](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#628)    ///   or any other error occurred (in which case @error will be set).

[720](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#720)    /// Pauses I/O on @msg.
[721](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#721)    ///
[722](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#722)    /// This can be used when you need to return from the server handler without
[723](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#723)    /// having the full response ready yet. Use [`unpause_message()`][Self::unpause_message()] to
[724](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#724)    /// resume I/O.
[725](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#725)    ///
[726](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#726)    /// This must only be called on a [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage] which was created by the
[727](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#727)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server] and are currently doing I/O, such as those passed into a
[728](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#728)    /// `callback::ServerCallback or emitted in a [`request-read`][struct@crate::Server#request-read]
[729](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#729)    /// signal.
[730](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#730)    ///
[731](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#731)    /// # Deprecated since 3.2
[732](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#732)    ///
[733](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#733)    /// Use soup_server_message_pause() instead.
[734](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#734)    /// ## `msg`
[735](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#735)    /// a #SoupServerMessage associated with @self.
[736](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#736)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "v3_2", deprecated = "Since 3.2")]
[737](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#737)    #[allow(deprecated)]
[738](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#738)    #[doc(alias = "soup_server_pause_message")]
[739](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#739)    fn pause_message(&self, msg: &ServerMessage) {
[740](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#740)        unsafe {
[741](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#741)            ffi::soup_server_pause_message(self.as_ref().to_glib_none().0, msg.to_glib_none().0);
[742](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#742)        }

[854](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#854)    /// Server header.
[855](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#855)    ///
[856](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#856)    /// If non-[`None`], the value to use for the "Server" header on
[857](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#857)    /// [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage]s processed by this server.
[858](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#858)    ///
[859](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#859)    /// The Server header is the server equivalent of the
[860](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#860)    /// User-Agent header, and provides information about the
[861](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#861)    /// server and its components. It contains a list of one or
[862](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#862)    /// more product tokens, separated by whitespace, with the most
[863](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#863)    /// significant product token coming first. The tokens must be
[864](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#864)    /// brief, ASCII, and mostly alphanumeric (although "-", "_",
[865](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#865)    /// and "." are also allowed), and may optionally include a "/"
[866](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#866)    /// followed by a version string. You may also put comments,
[867](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#867)    /// enclosed in parentheses, between or after the tokens.
[868](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#868)    ///
[869](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#869)    /// Some HTTP server implementations intentionally do not use
[870](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#870)    /// version numbers in their Server header, so that
[871](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#871)    /// installations running older versions of the server don't
[872](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#872)    /// end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security
[873](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#873)    /// holes.
[874](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#874)    ///
[875](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#875)    /// As with [`user_agent`][struct@crate::Session#user_agent], if you set a
[876](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#876)    /// [`server-header`][struct@crate::Server#server-header] property that has trailing
[877](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#877)    /// whitespace, [`Server`][crate::Server] will append its own product token (eg,
[878](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#878)    /// `libsoup/2.3.2`) to the end of the header for you.
[879](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#879)    #[doc(alias = "server-header")]
[880](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#880)    fn server_header(&self) -> Option<glib::GString> {
[881](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#881)        ObjectExt::property(self.as_ref(), "server-header")
[882](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#882)    }
[883](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#883)
[884](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#884)    /// Server header.

[901](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#901)    /// installations running older versions of the server don't
[902](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#902)    /// end up advertising their vulnerability to specific security

[914](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#914)    /// Emitted when processing has failed for a message.
[915](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#915)    ///
[916](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#916)    /// This could mean either that it could not be read (if
[917](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#917)    /// [`request-read`][struct@crate::Server#request-read] has not been emitted for it yet), or that
[918](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#918)    /// the response could not be written back (if [`request-read`][struct@crate::Server#request-read]

[920](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#920)    ///

[929](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#929)        &self,
[930](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#930)        f: F,
[931](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#931)    ) -> SignalHandlerId {

[933](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#933)            P: IsA<Server>,
[934](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#934)            F: Fn(&P, &ServerMessage) + 'static,

[937](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#937)            message: *mut ffi::SoupServerMessage,

[940](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#940)            unsafe {
[941](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#941)                let f: &F = &*(f as *const F);
[942](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#942)                f(
[943](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#943)                    Server::from_glib_borrow(this).unsafe_cast_ref(),
[944](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#944)                    &from_glib_borrow(message),
[945](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#945)                )
[946](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#946)            }
[947](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#947)        }
[948](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#948)        unsafe {
[949](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#949)            let f: Box_<F> = Box_::new(f);
[950](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#950)            connect_raw(
[951](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#951)                self.as_ptr() as *mut _,
[952](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#952)                c"request-aborted".as_ptr(),

[954](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#954)                    request_aborted_trampoline::<Self, F> as *const (),
[955](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#955)                )),
[956](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#956)                Box_::into_raw(f),
[957](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#957)            )
[958](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#958)        }

[1001](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1001)    /// @message will have all of its request-side information

[1003](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1003)    /// will have information about that. This signal is emitted
[1004](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1004)    /// before any (non-early) handlers are called for the message,
[1005](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1005)    /// and if it sets the message's #status_code, then normal

[1007](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1007)    /// ## `message`

# soup/server.rs

[1](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#1)use crate::{Server, ServerMessage, WebsocketConnection, prelude::*};

[7](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#7)    pub trait Sealed {}
[8](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#8)    impl<T: super::IsA<crate::Server>> Sealed for T {}
[9](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#9)}
[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)pub trait ServerExtManual: IsA<Server> + sealed::Sealed + 'static {
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)    /// Adds an "early" handler to @self for requests prefixed by @path.
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)    ///
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)    /// Note that "normal" and "early" handlers are matched up together, so if you
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)    /// add a normal handler for "/foo" and an early handler for "/foo/bar", then a
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)    /// request to "/foo/bar" (or any path below it) will run only the early handler.
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    /// (But if you add both handlers at the same path, then both will get run.)
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    ///
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// For requests under @path (that have not already been assigned a
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    /// status code by a [`AuthDomain`][crate::AuthDomain] or a signal handler), @callback
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// will be invoked after receiving the request headers, but before
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// receiving the request body; the message's method and
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// request-headers properties will be set.
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    ///
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// Early handlers are generally used for processing requests with request bodies
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// in a streaming fashion. If you determine that the request will contain a
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// message body, normally you would call [`MessageBody::set_accumulate()`][crate::MessageBody::set_accumulate()] on
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// the message's request-body to turn off request-body accumulation, and connect
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// to the message's [`got-chunk`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#got-chunk] signal to process each
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// chunk as it comes in.
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    ///
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// To complete the message processing after the full message body has
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// been read, you can either also connect to [`got-body`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#got-body],
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// or else you can register a non-early handler for @path as well. As
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// long as you have not set the status-code by the time
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    /// [`got-body`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#got-body] is emitted, the non-early handler will be
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    /// run as well.
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// ## `path`
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    /// the toplevel path for the handler
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    /// ## `callback`
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    /// callback to invoke for
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    ///   requests under @path
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    #[doc(alias = "soup_server_add_early_handler")]
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    fn add_early_handler<P: Fn(&Server, &ServerMessage, &str, HashMap<&str, &str>) + 'static>(
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)        &self,
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)        path: Option<&str>,
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)        callback: P,
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    ) {
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)        let callback_data: Box_<P> = Box_::new(callback);
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)        unsafe extern "C" fn callback_func<
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)            P: Fn(&Server, &ServerMessage, &str, HashMap<&str, &str>) + 'static,

[91](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#91)    /// Adds a handler to @self for requests prefixed by @path.
[92](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#92)    ///
[93](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#93)    /// If @path is [`None`] or "/", then this will be the default handler for all
[94](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#94)    /// requests that don't have a more specific handler. (Note though that if you
[95](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#95)    /// want to handle requests to the special "*" URI, you must explicitly register
[96](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#96)    /// a handler for "*"; the default handler will not be used for that case.)
[97](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#97)    ///
[98](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#98)    /// For requests under @path (that have not already been assigned a
[99](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#99)    /// status code by a [`AuthDomain`][crate::AuthDomain], an early server handler, or a
[100](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#100)    /// signal handler), @callback will be invoked after receiving the
[101](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#101)    /// request body; the [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage]'s method, request-headers,
[102](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#102)    /// and request-body properties will be set.
[103](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#103)    ///
[104](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#104)    /// After determining what to do with the request, the callback must at a minimum
[105](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#105)    /// call [`ServerMessage::set_status()`][crate::ServerMessage::set_status()] on the message to set the response
[106](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#106)    /// status code. Additionally, it may set response headers and/or fill in the
[107](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#107)    /// response body.
[108](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#108)    ///
[109](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#109)    /// If the callback cannot fully fill in the response before returning
[110](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#110)    /// (eg, if it needs to wait for information from a database, or
[111](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#111)    /// another network server), it should call [`ServerMessage::pause()`][crate::ServerMessage::pause()]
[112](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#112)    /// to tell @self to not send the response right away. When the
[113](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#113)    /// response is ready, call [`ServerMessage::unpause()`][crate::ServerMessage::unpause()] to cause it
[114](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#114)    /// to be sent.
[115](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#115)    ///
[116](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#116)    /// To send the response body a bit at a time using "chunked" encoding, first
[117](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#117)    /// call [`MessageHeaders::set_encoding()`][crate::MessageHeaders::set_encoding()] to set [`Encoding::Chunked`][crate::Encoding::Chunked] on
[118](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#118)    /// the response-headers. Then call `MessageBody::append()` (or
[119](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#119)    /// [`MessageBody::append_bytes()`][crate::MessageBody::append_bytes()])) to append each chunk as it becomes ready,
[120](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#120)    /// and [`ServerMessage::unpause()`][crate::ServerMessage::unpause()] to make sure it's running. (The server
[121](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#121)    /// will automatically pause the message if it is using chunked encoding but no
[122](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#122)    /// more chunks are available.) When you are done, call
[123](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#123)    /// [`MessageBody::complete()`][crate::MessageBody::complete()] to indicate that no more chunks are coming.
[124](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#124)    /// ## `path`
[125](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#125)    /// the toplevel path for the handler
[126](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#126)    /// ## `callback`
[127](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#127)    /// callback to invoke for
[128](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#128)    ///   requests under @path

[177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#177)    /// Adds a WebSocket handler to @self for requests prefixed by @path.
[178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#178)    ///
[179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#179)    /// If @path is [`None`] or "/", then this will be the default handler for all
[180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#180)    /// requests that don't have a more specific handler.
[181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#181)    ///
[182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#182)    /// When a path has a WebSocket handler registered, @self will check
[183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#183)    /// incoming requests for WebSocket handshakes after all other handlers
[184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#184)    /// have run (unless some earlier handler has already set a status code
[185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#185)    /// on the message), and update the request's status, response headers,
[186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#186)    /// and response body accordingly.
[187](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#187)    ///
[188](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#188)    /// If @origin is non-[`None`], then only requests containing a matching
[189](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#189)    /// "Origin" header will be accepted. If @protocols is non-[`None`], then
[190](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#190)    /// only requests containing a compatible "Sec-WebSocket-Protocols"
[191](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#191)    /// header will be accepted. More complicated requirements can be
[192](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#192)    /// handled by adding a normal handler to @path, and having it perform
[193](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#193)    /// whatever checks are needed and

[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    ///
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// A [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage] represents an HTTP message that is being sent or
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// received on a [`Server`][crate::Server].
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// [`Server`][crate::Server] will create [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage]s automatically for
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// incoming requests, which your application will receive via handlers.
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    ///
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// Note that libsoup's terminology here does not quite match the HTTP
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    /// specification: in RFC 2616, an "HTTP-message" is *either* a Request, *or* a
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// Response. In libsoup, a [`ServerMessage`][crate::ServerMessage] combines both the request and the
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// response.
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    ///
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// ## Properties
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    ///
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    ///
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// #### `tls-peer-certificate`
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    ///  The peer's #GTlsCertificate associated with the message
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    ///
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// Readable
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    ///
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    ///
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// #### `tls-peer-certificate-errors`
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    ///  The verification errors on [`tls-peer-certificate`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#tls-peer-certificate]
[40](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#40)    ///
[41](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#41)    /// Readable
[42](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#42)    ///
[43](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#43)    /// ## Signals
[44](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#44)    ///
[45](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#45)    ///
[46](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#46)    /// #### `accept-certificate`
[47](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#47)    ///  Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake
[48](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#48)    /// after client TLS certificate has been received.
[49](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#49)    /// You can return [`true`] to accept @tls_certificate despite
[50](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#50)    /// @tls_errors.
[51](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#51)    ///
[52](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#52)    ///
[53](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#53)    ///
[54](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#54)    ///
[55](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#55)    /// #### `connected`
[56](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#56)    ///  Emitted when the @msg's socket is connected and the TLS handshake completed.
[57](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#57)    ///
[58](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#58)    ///
[59](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#59)    ///
[60](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#60)    ///
[61](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#61)    /// #### `disconnected`
[62](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#62)    ///  Emitted when the @msg's socket is disconnected.
[63](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#63)    ///
[64](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#64)    ///
[65](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#65)    ///
[66](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#66)    ///
[67](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#67)    /// #### `finished`
[68](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#68)    ///  Emitted when all HTTP processing is finished for a message.
[69](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#69)    /// (After [`wrote-body`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#wrote-body]).
[70](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#70)    ///
[71](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#71)    ///
[72](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#72)    ///
[73](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#73)    ///
[74](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#74)    /// #### `got-body`
[75](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#75)    ///  Emitted after receiving the complete request body.
[76](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#76)    ///
[77](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#77)    ///
[78](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#78)    ///
[79](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#79)    ///
[80](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#80)    /// #### `got-chunk`
[81](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#81)    ///  Emitted after receiving a chunk of a message body.
[82](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#82)    ///
[83](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#83)    /// Note that "chunk" in this context means any subpiece of the body, not
[84](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#84)    /// necessarily the specific HTTP 1.1 chunks sent by the other side.
[85](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#85)    ///
[86](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#86)    ///
[87](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#87)    ///
[88](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#88)    ///
[89](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#89)    /// #### `got-headers`
[90](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#90)    ///  Emitted after receiving the Request-Line and request headers.
[91](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#91)    ///
[92](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#92)    ///
[93](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#93)    ///
[94](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#94)    ///
[95](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#95)    /// #### `wrote-body`
[96](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#96)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing the complete response body for a
[97](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#97)    /// message.
[98](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#98)    ///
[99](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#99)    ///
[100](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#100)    ///
[101](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#101)    ///
[102](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#102)    /// #### `wrote-body-data`
[103](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#103)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing a portion of the message
[104](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#104)    /// body to the network.
[105](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#105)    ///
[106](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#106)    ///
[107](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#107)    ///
[108](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#108)    ///
[109](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#109)    /// #### `wrote-chunk`
[110](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#110)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing a body chunk for a message.
[111](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#111)    ///
[112](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#112)    /// Note that this signal is not parallel to
[113](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#113)    /// [`got-chunk`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#got-chunk]; it is emitted only when a complete
[114](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#114)    /// chunk (added with `MessageBody::append()` or
[115](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#115)    /// [`MessageBody::append_bytes()`][crate::MessageBody::append_bytes()] has been written. To get
[116](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#116)    /// more useful continuous progress information, use
[117](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#117)    /// [`wrote-body-data`][struct@crate::ServerMessage#wrote-body-data].
[118](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#118)    ///
[119](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#119)    ///
[120](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#120)    ///
[121](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#121)    ///
[122](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#122)    /// #### `wrote-headers`
[123](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#123)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing the response headers for a
[124](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#124)    /// message.
[125](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#125)    ///
[126](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#126)    ///
[127](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#127)    ///
[128](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#128)    ///
[129](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#129)    /// #### `wrote-informational`
[130](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#130)    ///  Emitted immediately after writing a 1xx (Informational) response.
[131](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#131)    ///
[132](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#132)    ///
[133](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#133)    ///
[134](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#134)    /// # Implements
[135](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#135)    ///

[304](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#304)    /// made on the same persistent HTTP connection (eg, as the ntlm-test
[305](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#305)    /// test program does), you will need to pay attention to socket
[306](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#306)    /// destruction as well (eg, by using weak references), so that you do
[307](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#307)    /// not get fooled when the allocator reuses the memory address of a
[308](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#308)    /// previously-destroyed socket to represent a new socket.

[313](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#313)    ///   associated with, [`None`] if you used [`ServerExt::accept_iostream()`][crate::prelude::ServerExt::accept_iostream()].

[526](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#526)    /// Emitted during the @msg's connection TLS handshake
[527](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#527)    /// after client TLS certificate has been received.
[528](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#528)    /// You can return [`true`] to accept @tls_certificate despite
[529](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#529)    /// @tls_errors.
[530](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#530)    /// ## `tls_peer_certificate`
[531](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#531)    /// the peer's #GTlsCertificate
[532](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#532)    /// ## `tls_peer_errors`
[533](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#533)    /// the tls errors of @tls_certificate
[534](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#534)    ///
[535](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#535)    /// # Returns
[536](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#536)    ///
[537](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#537)    /// [`true`] to accept the TLS certificate and stop other
[538](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#538)    ///   handlers from being invoked, or [`false`] to propagate the
[539](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#539)    ///   event further.
[540](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#540)    #[doc(alias = "accept-certificate")]
[541](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#541)    pub fn connect_accept_certificate<
[542](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#542)        F: Fn(&Self, &gio::TlsCertificate, gio::TlsCertificateFlags) -> bool + 'static,
[543](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#543)    >(
[544](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#544)        &self,
[545](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#545)        f: F,
[546](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#546)    ) -> SignalHandlerId {
[547](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#547)        unsafe extern "C" fn accept_certificate_trampoline<
[548](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#548)            F: Fn(&ServerMessage, &gio::TlsCertificate, gio::TlsCertificateFlags) -> bool + 'static,
[549](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#549)        >(
[550](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#550)            this: *mut ffi::SoupServerMessage,
[551](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#551)            tls_peer_certificate: *mut gio::ffi::GTlsCertificate,
[552](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#552)            tls_peer_errors: gio::ffi::GTlsCertificateFlags,
[553](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#553)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[554](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#554)        ) -> glib::ffi::gboolean {
[555](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#555)            unsafe {
[556](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#556)                let f: &F = &*(f as *const F);
[557](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#557)                f(
[558](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#558)                    &from_glib_borrow(this),
[559](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#559)                    &from_glib_borrow(tls_peer_certificate),
[560](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#560)                    from_glib(tls_peer_errors),
[561](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#561)                )
[562](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#562)                .into_glib()
[563](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#563)            }
[564](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#564)        }
[565](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#565)        unsafe {

[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)    ///
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)    /// Provides support for the [WebSocket](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6455)
[19](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#19)    /// protocol.
[20](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#20)    ///
[21](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#21)    /// To connect to a WebSocket server, create a [`Session`][crate::Session] and call
[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)    /// `Session::websocket_connect_async()`. To accept WebSocket
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)    /// connections, create a [`Server`][crate::Server] and add a handler to it with
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)    /// [`ServerExtManual::add_websocket_handler()`][crate::prelude::ServerExtManual::add_websocket_handler()].
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)    ///
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)    /// (Lower-level support is available via
[27](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#27)    /// `websocket_client_prepare_handshake()` and
[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    /// `websocket_client_verify_handshake()`, for handling the client side of the
[29](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#29)    /// WebSocket handshake, and `websocket_server_process_handshake()` for
[30](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#30)    /// handling the server side.)
[31](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#31)    ///
[32](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#32)    /// [`WebsocketConnection`][crate::WebsocketConnection] handles the details of WebSocket communication. You
[33](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#33)    /// can use [`send_text()`][Self::send_text()] and
[34](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#34)    /// `WebsocketConnection::send_binary()` to send data, and the
[35](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#35)    /// [`message`][struct@crate::WebsocketConnection#message] signal to receive data.
[36](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#36)    /// ([`WebsocketConnection`][crate::WebsocketConnection] currently only supports asynchronous I/O.)
[37](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#37)    ///
[38](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#38)    /// ## Properties
[39](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#39)    ///

[130](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#130)    ///
[131](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#131)    /// For servers this represents the address of the WebSocket,
[132](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#132)    /// and for clients it is the address connected to.
[133](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#133)    ///
[134](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#134)    /// Readable | Writeable | Construct Only
[135](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#135)    ///
[136](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#136)    /// ## Signals
[137](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#137)    ///
[138](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#138)    ///
[139](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#139)    /// #### `closed`
[140](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#140)    ///  Emitted when the connection has completely closed.
[141](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#141)    ///
[142](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#142)    /// This happens either due to an orderly close from the peer, one
[143](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#143)    /// initiated via [`WebsocketConnection::close()`][crate::WebsocketConnection::close()] or a fatal error
[144](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#144)    /// condition that caused a close.
[145](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#145)    ///
[146](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#146)    /// This signal will be emitted once.
[147](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#147)    ///
[148](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#148)    ///
[149](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#149)    ///
[150](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#150)    ///
[151](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#151)    /// #### `closing`
[152](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#152)    ///  This signal will be emitted during an orderly close.
[153](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#153)    ///
[154](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#154)    ///
[155](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#155)    ///
[156](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#156)    ///
[157](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#157)    /// #### `error`
[158](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#158)    ///  Emitted when an error occurred on the WebSocket.
[159](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#159)    ///
[160](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#160)    /// This may be fired multiple times. Fatal errors will be followed by
[161](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#161)    /// the [`closed`][struct@crate::WebsocketConnection#closed] signal being emitted.
[162](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#162)    ///
[163](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#163)    ///
[164](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#164)    ///
[165](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#165)    ///
[166](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#166)    /// #### `message`
[167](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#167)    ///  Emitted when we receive a message from the peer.
[168](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#168)    ///
[169](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#169)    /// As a convenience, the @message data will always be
[170](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#170)    /// [`None`]-terminated, but the NUL byte will not be included in
[171](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#171)    /// the length count.
[172](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#172)    ///
[173](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#173)    ///
[174](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#174)    ///
[175](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#175)    ///
[176](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#176)    /// #### `pong`
[177](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#177)    ///  Emitted when we receive a Pong frame (solicited or
[178](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#178)    /// unsolicited) from the peer.
[179](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#179)    ///
[180](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#180)    /// As a convenience, the @message data will always be
[181](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#181)    /// [`None`]-terminated, but the NUL byte will not be included in
[182](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#182)    /// the length count.
[183](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#183)    ///
[184](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#184)    ///
[185](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#185)    ///
[186](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#186)    /// # Implements
[187](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#187)    ///
[188](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#188)    /// [`trait@glib::ObjectExt`], [`WebsocketConnectionExtManual`][trait@crate::prelude::WebsocketConnectionExtManual]
[189](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#189)    #[doc(alias = "SoupWebsocketConnection")]
[190](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#190)    pub struct WebsocketConnection(Object<ffi::SoupWebsocketConnection, ffi::SoupWebsocketConnectionClass>);

[206](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#206)    /// Close the connection in an orderly fashion.
[207](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#207)    ///
[208](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#208)    /// Note that until the [`closed`][struct@crate::WebsocketConnection#closed] signal fires, the connection
[209](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#209)    /// is not yet completely closed. The close message is not even sent until the
[210](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#210)    /// main loop runs.
[211](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#211)    ///
[212](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#212)    /// The @code and @data are sent to the peer along with the close request.
[213](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#213)    /// If @code is [`WebsocketCloseCode::NoStatus`][crate::WebsocketCloseCode::NoStatus] a close message with no body
[214](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#214)    /// (without code and data) is sent.
[215](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#215)    /// Note that the @data must be UTF-8 valid.
[216](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#216)    /// ## `code`
[217](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#217)    /// close code
[218](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#218)    /// ## `data`
[219](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#219)    /// close data
[220](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#220)    #[doc(alias = "soup_websocket_connection_close")]
[221](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#221)    pub fn close(&self, code: libc::c_ushort, data: Option<&str>) {
[222](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#222)        unsafe {
[223](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#223)            ffi::soup_websocket_connection_close(
[224](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#224)                self.to_glib_none().0,
[225](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#225)                code,
[226](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#226)                data.to_glib_none().0,
[227](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#227)            );
[228](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#228)        }
[229](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#229)    }
[230](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#230)

[513](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#513)    /// Emitted when the connection has completely closed.
[514](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#514)    ///
[515](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#515)    /// This happens either due to an orderly close from the peer, one
[516](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#516)    /// initiated via [`close()`][Self::close()] or a fatal error
[517](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#517)    /// condition that caused a close.
[518](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#518)    ///
[519](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#519)    /// This signal will be emitted once.
[520](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#520)    #[doc(alias = "closed")]
[521](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#521)    pub fn connect_closed<F: Fn(&Self) + 'static>(&self, f: F) -> SignalHandlerId {
[522](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#522)        unsafe extern "C" fn closed_trampoline<F: Fn(&WebsocketConnection) + 'static>(
[523](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#523)            this: *mut ffi::SoupWebsocketConnection,
[524](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#524)            f: glib::ffi::gpointer,
[525](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#525)        ) {
[526](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#526)            unsafe {
[527](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#527)                let f: &F = &*(f as *const F);
[528](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#528)                f(&from_glib_borrow(this))
[529](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#529)            }
[530](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#530)        }
[531](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#531)        unsafe {
[532](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#532)            let f: Box_<F> = Box_::new(f);
[533](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#533)            connect_raw(
[534](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#534)                self.as_ptr() as *mut _,
[535](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#535)                c"closed".as_ptr(),
[536](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#536)                Some(std::mem::transmute::<*const (), unsafe extern "C" fn()>(
[537](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#537)                    closed_trampoline::<F> as *const (),
[538](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#538)                )),
[539](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#539)                Box_::into_raw(f),
[540](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#540)            )
[541](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#541)        }
[542](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#542)    }

[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)/// This is useful for compiling against older versions of libsoup, but using
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)/// features from newer versions.
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)/// ## `major`
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)/// the major version to check

[22](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#22)///
[23](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#23)/// [`true`] if the version of the libsoup currently loaded
[24](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#24)///   is the same as or newer than the passed-in version.
[25](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#25)#[doc(alias = "soup_check_version")]
[26](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#26)pub fn check_version(major: u32, minor: u32, micro: u32) -> bool {

[28](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#28)    unsafe { from_glib(ffi::soup_check_version(major, minor, micro)) }

[315](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#315)/// Parses the headers of an HTTP request or response in @str and
[316](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#316)/// stores the results in @dest.
[317](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#317)///
[318](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#318)/// Beware that @dest may be modified even on failure.

[321](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#321)/// [`headers_parse_request()`][crate::headers_parse_request()] or [`headers_parse_response()`][crate::headers_parse_response()].
[322](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#322)/// ## `str`

[327](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#327)/// ## `dest`
[328](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#328)/// #SoupMessageHeaders to store the header values in
[329](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#329)///
[330](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#330)/// # Returns
[331](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#331)///
[332](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#332)/// success or failure
[333](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#333)#[doc(alias = "soup_headers_parse")]

[346](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#346)/// Parses the headers of an HTTP request in @str and stores the
[347](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#347)/// results in @req_method, @req_path, @ver, and @req_headers.
[348](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#348)///

[350](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#350)/// ## `str`
[351](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#351)/// the headers (up to, but not including, the trailing blank line)
[352](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#352)/// ## `len`
[353](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#353)/// length of @str
[354](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#354)/// ## `req_headers`

[357](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#357)/// # Returns
[358](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#358)///
[359](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#359)/// [`Status::Ok`][crate::Status::Ok] if the headers could be parsed, or an
[360](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#360)///   HTTP error to be returned to the client if they could not be.
[361](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#361)///
[362](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#362)/// ## `req_method`
[363](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#363)/// if non-[`None`], will be filled in with the
[364](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#364)///   request method
[365](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#365)///
[366](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#366)/// ## `req_path`

[369](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#369)///
[370](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#370)/// ## `ver`

[372](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#372)///   version

[379](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#379)    let len = str.len() as _;
[380](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#380)    unsafe {
[381](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#381)        let mut req_method = std::ptr::null_mut();
[382](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#382)        let mut req_path = std::ptr::null_mut();
[383](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#383)        let mut ver = std::mem::MaybeUninit::uninit();
[384](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#384)        let ret = ffi::soup_headers_parse_request(
[385](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#385)            str.to_glib_none().0,
[386](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#386)            len,
[387](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#387)            req_headers.to_glib_none().0,
[388](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#388)            &mut req_method,
[389](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#389)            &mut req_path,
[390](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#390)            ver.as_mut_ptr(),
[391](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#391)        );
[392](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#392)        (
[393](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#393)            ret,
[394](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#394)            from_glib_full(req_method),
[395](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#395)            from_glib_full(req_path),
[396](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#396)            from_glib(ver.assume_init()),
[397](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#397)        )
[398](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#398)    }

[527](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#527)/// Finds the base domain for a given @hostname
[528](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#528)///
[529](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#529)/// The base domain is composed by the top level domain (such as .org, .com,
[530](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#530)/// .co.uk, etc) plus the second level domain, for example for
[531](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#531)/// myhost.mydomain.com it will return mydomain.com.
[532](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#532)///
[533](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#533)/// Note that [`None`] will be returned for private URLs (those not ending
[534](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#534)/// with any well known TLD) because choosing a base domain for them
[535](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#535)/// would be totally arbitrary.
[536](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#536)///
[537](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#537)/// Prior to libsoup 2.46, this function required that @hostname be in
[538](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#538)/// UTF-8 if it was an IDN. From 2.46 on, the name can be in either
[539](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#539)/// UTF-8 or ASCII format (and the return value will be in the same
[540](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#540)/// format).
[541](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#541)/// ## `hostname`
[542](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#542)/// a hostname
[543](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#543)///
[544](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#544)/// # Returns
[545](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#545)///
[546](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#546)/// a pointer to the start of the base domain in @hostname. If
[547](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#547)///   an error occurs, [`None`] will be returned and @error set.
[548](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#548)#[doc(alias = "soup_tld_get_base_domain")]
[549](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#549)pub fn tld_get_base_domain(hostname: &str) -> Result<glib::GString, glib::Error> {
[550](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#550)    assert_initialized_main_thread!();
[551](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#551)    unsafe {
[552](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#552)        let mut error = std::ptr::null_mut();
[553](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#553)        let ret = ffi::soup_tld_get_base_domain(hostname.to_glib_none().0, &mut error);
[554](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#554)        if error.is_null() {
[555](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#555)            Ok(from_glib_none(ret))
[556](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#556)        } else {
[557](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#557)            Err(from_glib_full(error))
[558](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#558)        }
[559](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#559)    }
[560](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#560)}

[3](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#3)/// Appends something like `name=value` to @string, taking care to quote @value
[4](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#4)/// if needed, and if so, to escape any quotes or backslashes in @value.
[5](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#5)///
[6](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#6)/// Alternatively, if @value is a non-ASCII UTF-8 string, it will be
[7](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#7)/// appended using RFC5987 syntax. Although in theory this is supposed
[8](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#8)/// to work anywhere in HTTP that uses this style of parameter, in
[9](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#9)/// reality, it can only be used portably with the Content-Disposition
[10](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#10)/// "filename" parameter.
[11](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#11)///
[12](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#12)/// If @value is [`None`], this will just append @name to @string.
[13](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#13)/// ## `string`
[14](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#14)/// a #GString being used to construct an HTTP header value
[15](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#15)/// ## `name`
[16](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#16)/// a parameter name
[17](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#17)/// ## `value`
[18](https://world.pages.gitlab.gnome.org#18)/// a parameter value, or [`None`]
